summary: The motion proposes that holders of a B driving license be permitted to operate a light motorcycle with an engine capacity of up to 125 cubic centimeters, arguing that this would help reduce congestion in urban areas and lessen environmental impact compared to traditional cars, while acknowledging that B license holders have already demonstrated understanding of traffic rules.

title: Forskning – en satsning för framtiden
summary: The suggestion proposes to change the seating arrangement of members in the Swedish Parliament's plenary hall from a constituency-based system to one based on party affiliation. The current setup is seen as outdated, and the motion argues that aligning members by party would facilitate communication within groups and streamline voting processes. The motion suggests that this change would have minimal financial implications and calls for an expedited implementation.

title: Förutsättningar för en grundskola i världsklass
summary: The motion proposes to amend the Swedish constitution by removing the inscription of Sweden's EU membership and calls for the removal of the EU flag from the Parliament's plenary chamber. The motion argues that Sweden has succeeded as a welfare state independent of EU oversight and that current EU regulations undermine Swedish sovereignty and democracy. The proponent advocates for a shift towards a more intergovernmental collaboration within the EU, emphasizing national self-determination and the need for Sweden to have the flexibility to renegotiate or exit the EU without constitutional impediments.

title: Svensk gymnasieskola och vuxenutbildning
summary: The motion proposes to reinstate the ceremonial opening of the Swedish Parliament in the Rikssalen at Stockholm Palace, a tradition that was discontinued in 1974 when the opening was moved to the parliament's plenary chamber. The proponent emphasizes the importance of honoring Swedish traditions and history, and suggests that bringing back this ceremony would enhance the public's perception of both the monarchy and the parliament.

title: En förskola i världsklass
summary: This motion proposes a legislative change to extend the right to self-defense in Sweden, advocating for a more permissive law regarding self-defense and excess in self-defense cases. The proposal is based on a case where a man was sentenced to 18 months in prison for accidentally killing an aggressor during an attempt to protect himself and others. The motion argues that the current legal framework forces lawful citizens to endure aggressive threats without adequate means of protection, necessitating a reevaluation of the standards for what constitutes acceptable self-defense in pressure situations.

title: En grundskola i världsklass
summary: The motion proposes the establishment of a state-run testament registry managed by the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket) to prevent disputes over inheritances that can arise from missing or unregistered wills. The aim is to provide families dealing with the loss of a loved one with a secure and reliable way to ensure that their testament is preserved, reducing the potential for conflict during an already difficult time.

title: Värna kvalitet och frihet inom högskolan
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish government should establish a state-led management structure for the healthcare system, arguing that the current 21 regional healthcare authorities lead to inconsistencies in care delivery and regulations across the country. The motion highlights the need for a unified national healthcare organization to ensure equal access and quality of care for all citizens, citing challenges revealed during the COVID-19 pandemic, including regional disparities in healthcare capacity and response. The aim is to streamline services, reduce bureaucracy, and improve efficiency in the healthcare system.

title: En skola med studiemiljö i världsklass
summary: This motion proposes that the Swedish parliament should not impose taxes on plastic products made from recycled or environmentally friendly materials. The motion critiques the existing plastic bag tax for being ineffective and potentially harmful to the environment, arguing that it discourages the production of sustainable plastics and has led to increased use of less eco-friendly alternatives. It highlights the need for a reformed tax structure that supports environmental goals without negatively affecting Swedish consumers.

title: Fördelning av de regionala utvecklingsmedlen
summary: The motion proposes to prohibit the use of carbon dioxide for stunning animals before slaughter, arguing that this method causes unnecessary suffering and stress to the animals, particularly pigs. It calls for the establishment of a deadline for phasing out this method and encourages the government to explore alternative stunning methods, such as nitrogen foam, which have shown promise in preliminary research. The motion emphasizes the importance of ensuring animal welfare in line with Swedish animal protection laws.

title: Hantverkare behövs i en cirkulär ekonomi
summary: The motion proposes a transparent tax system in Sweden by advocating for clearer reporting of value-added tax (VAT) for consumers, social fees in income declarations, and their presentation in payslips. It calls for an investigation into how to efficiently display tax allocation on final tax statements and the introduction of accessible budget reports for public entities. The intention behind these suggestions is to enhance public awareness about taxation and how funds are utilized, fostering political engagement among citizens.

title: Reformerad arbetsskadeförsäkring
summary: The motion proposes the establishment of a Finnish-inspired preparedness law in Sweden to rebuild and maintain essential reserves of food, medical supplies, and other vital resources that have been diminished over the past two decades. It argues that Sweden has moved away from the practice of stockpiling necessary supplies, unlike Finland, which has maintained robust stockpiles to ensure sufficient resources during crises, such as the current pandemic. The motion calls for the government to take action to create similar preparedness measures.

title: Minska regelkrånglet för hästnäringen
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish parliament investigate the introduction of assisted dying for severely ill patients, recognizing the need to alleviate suffering and uphold patient autonomy at the end of life. It highlights current limitations in Swedish healthcare regarding euthanasia, discusses existing models in other countries, and cites a case from Gotland that underscores the urgency of reevaluating the law. Public opinion reportedly supports the idea, prompting the motion to encourage legislative action towards a formal inquiry into assisted dying options in Sweden, with a focus on the Oregon model.

title: Utvärdera kassaregistren
summary: The suggestion proposes that confidentiality should be maintained in cases of rape to protect the victims from the burden of public knowledge about the details of the crime. It argues that the current rules lead to public access to sensitive information that can cause additional trauma to victims. The proposal aims to ensure that details of the event remain confidential regardless of the outcome of the judicial process, thereby safeguarding the individual rights of both male and female victims.

title: Återbetalning av fordonsskatt
summary: The motion emphasizes the need for increased legal safeguards in social services investigations to ensure fairness and objectivity. It identifies current issues where subjective biases may affect outcomes, particularly impacting children, and proposes that investigative procedures should include measures such as reading and confirming responses from those interviewed, employing alternative hypotheses during assessments, and ensuring transparency in the methods used.

title: Avskaffa kravet på momspliktig verksamhet vid fastighetsuthyrning
summary: The Swedish government has proposed an extra budget amendment for 2020 in response to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. This includes extending and increasing financial support to businesses and individual entrepreneurs affected by the crisis, as well as additional funding for cultural and sports activities. The proposal details changes in various budget allocations to accommodate these measures, which aim to mitigate the significant economic impacts of the pandemic on society and support the recovery process.

title: Digital tillgång för omhändertagna barn och unga
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament advocate for visa-free travel for the people of Kosovo and promote increased trade between Kosovo, the EU, and Sweden. It highlights the importance of these measures for Kosovo's economic development, given its strategic location in the Balkans, and addresses current challenges such as political conflicts, corruption, and the need for modernization within the country's governance systems.

title: En reformerad hälso- och sjukvårdslag
summary: The motion addresses the need for the Swedish government to review and enhance vocational training programs in collaboration with various industries to better align education with labor market needs. It highlights the demographic growth of Sweden, the challenges of integrating youth and immigrants into the workforce, and proposes targeted training, including vocational Swedish, to improve employability.

title: Tillnyktringsenheter för berusade personer
summary: The proposal suggests the introduction of a tax on sugary and carbonated beverages to combat obesity and related health issues in Sweden. The motion cites rising obesity rates, particularly among the youth, as a significant public health concern and references successful implementations of similar taxes in countries like Mexico and France, which have led to reduced consumption of sugary drinks. The authors argue that economic measures are essential to change consumption behaviors and draw on experiences with high taxes on tobacco and alcohol in Sweden as a precedent for such a tax.

title: Planfria korsningar - ökad trafiksäkerhet
summary: The motion proposes to clarify the criminal code to ensure that hate crimes against ethnic and cultural Swedes are treated equally under the law, just like hate crimes targeting other groups. The motion argues that, despite existing protections, there have been no convictions for hate crimes against ethnic and cultural Swedes due to a perceived bias in the legal framework, which primarily protects minority groups. It calls for equal legal protection for all groups, emphasizing the need for the law to address increasing hate crimes against ethnic and cultural Swedes, particularly in areas where they may be in the minority.

title: Dela data mellan myndigheter
summary: The proposal seeks to abolish the requirement for a certified control manager in private construction of small houses, allowing builders to appoint a quality manager themselves instead. It argues that the existing certification process adds unnecessary administrative costs for private builders and that existing building regulations are sufficient to ensure compliance without mandated certified oversight.

title: Demokratiskt vald statschef
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1918 av Hillevi Larsson och Emilia Töyrä (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes to introduce stricter requirements for signatures on identity documents issued by authorities in Sweden. It highlights a trend where individuals write comments or messages unrelated to their name, such as derogatory remarks aimed at the police. The lawmakers argue that the current regulations lack clear guidelines on how signatures should appear, allowing for unreadable or inappropriate signatures. The motion calls for an investigation into the possibility of implementing stricter standards while still allowing individuals the freedom to define their own signature, as long as it does not carry unrelated meanings.

title: Stärk tillsynen av mänskliga rättigheter för personer med funktionsvariationer i Sverige
summary: The motion proposes the introduction of mandatory identification marking for cats in Sweden to address the issue of over 100,000 homeless cats, many of which suffer due to neglect or abandonment. The absence of ID marking makes it difficult to return lost cats to their owners and enforce animal abandonment laws effectively. The authors argue that requiring ID marking, similar to existing regulations for dogs, would help protect cats and ensure that owners can be held accountable for neglect.

title: Gör midsommarafton till nationaldag
summary: The motion proposes to increase the asset limit for the means testing of housing supplements for pensioners to 300,000 SEK for single individuals and 450,000 SEK for couples. The authors argue that many pensioners with low incomes are adversely affected by the current asset limits, which have not changed since 2003. They highlight the necessity of a financial buffer to manage unexpected expenses and advocate for fairer access to housing supplements, reflecting the financial realities faced by long-term workers in the pension system.

title: Kompetensutveckling genom hela arbetslivet
summary: This motion proposes the abolition of the 2014 law on completion protection, which currently mandates a form of insurance or bank guarantee to protect consumers in the construction sector. The authors argue that the law does not benefit consumers but rather insurance companies, as the costs of the insurance are high in relation to the limited compensation consumers can receive. They advocate for a more flexible approach to insurance that does not impose mandatory coverage for such limited liabilities.

title: Forskning om kvinnosjukdomar och kvinnors hälsa
summary: The motion proposes simplifying regulations for the recalculation of share ratios in road associations in Sweden, drawing inspiration from a Finnish model where associations can determine their own share ratios. The current legislative framework has led to outdated ratios and significant discrepancies across associations. The motion aims to enhance legal clarity and financial stability for these associations by allowing them to update their share ratios through their own decision-making processes, thus avoiding bureaucratic bottlenecks and potential legal disputes.

title: Nationell handlingsplan för endometriosvården
summary: The motion proposes increasing collaboration between traffic police and trained vehicle inspectors to improve traffic oversight and enforcement of transportation regulations. It highlights the growing number of vehicles on the roads and the need for specialized knowledge to assess compliance with traffic laws and loading regulations. The authors argue that by employing trained inspectors, traffic police can focus on monitoring, leading to more efficient traffic enforcement and increased road safety.

title: Eftersupning vid trafikbrott
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1912 av Adnan Dibrani och Hans Hoff (båda S)
summary: This motion proposes to the Swedish parliament to review the possibility of reallocating existing project-based funding for civil society organizations to more sustainable annual association support. It also suggests reviewing the regulations concerning the General Heritage Fund to improve the allocation of funds. The motivation emphasizes the importance of civil society in creating societal value and the need for more stable financial support to enable long-term projects and collaborations between civil society and government entities.

title: Trafikskadeförsäkringen
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1911 av Adnan Dibrani och Mattias Jonsson (båda S)
summary: The motion advocates for simplifying regulations for businesses in the tourism sector by allowing local decisions on shoreline protection, permitting the sale of all farm-produced goods on-site, introducing more flexible employment contracts, and investigating differentiated legislation based on company size. These changes aim to support the growth of small businesses within the tourism industry, enhance local tourism, and adapt to varying market demands.

title: Förändrade åldersregler vid adoption
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1910 av Adnan Dibrani och Mattias Jonsson (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish parliament mandates authorities to review and streamline the various permits required for businesses. It suggests appointing a coordinator to work with businesses to assess legislative requirements, differentiating permit criteria based on the size and duration of operation of firms. Additionally, it advocates for authorities to provide guidance and support to businesses during permit applications and inspections, aiming to simplify the process and ensure a fair approach to regulation while enhancing the compliance framework for both new and established companies.

title: Vägarna kring Ullared
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament encourages governmental agencies to collaborate across sectors to reduce mental health issues in society. It highlights the increasing prevalence of mental health problems, attributing this to workplace environments and societal norms, and calls for all responsible parties, from individuals to employers and authorities, to work together. The aim is to improve occupational health and streamline processes related to sick leave to alleviate stress for affected individuals.

title: En bättre arbetsmiljö
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1908 av Johan Büser och Gunilla Carlsson (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish parliament investigate how all regions can access emergency airports, in response to recent forest fires and the need for better healthcare transport options. Currently, there are ten operational emergency airports, but significant gaps exist, particularly affecting regions such as Västmanland, Kronoberg, Kalmar, and Halland. The motion emphasizes the importance of expanding emergency flight facilities to enhance healthcare delivery across the country.

title: Israel och Palestina
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1907 av Johan Büser och Elin Gustafsson (båda S)
summary: The proposal aims to review and enhance existing support systems for individuals who are distant from the labor market, suggesting that government assistance should focus on providing dedicated workplace supervision and training rather than solely reducing employer costs. By allowing companies to share training costs with the state, especially in cases where individuals may lack formal education but possess the necessary qualities, more small and medium-sized enterprises can hire these individuals, thereby promoting job creation and reducing dependency on welfare programs.

title: Riksdagsledamöternas placering i kammaren
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1906 av Markus Wiechel och Bo Broman (båda SD)
summary: The proposal suggests that the Swedish Parliament should address the costs associated with appeal processes, particularly in the building industry, where excessive appeals can delay or halt development projects. It calls for a government investigation to assess a system where the first appeal is free, but subsequent appeals in higher courts would incur a fee, potentially implemented for individuals, municipalities, and organizations.

title: Proportionella bötesbelopp
summary: This motion proposes an investigation into how to create equal conditions for all providers in the fields of education, healthcare, and social care in Sweden. It calls for an assessment of the obstacles facing non-public organizations and the impact of fees associated with obtaining permissions for providing care services. The aim is to ensure greater choice and quality in services available to individuals, promoting innovation and individualized care regardless of whether the provider is public, private, or non-profit.

title: Rekrytering av rektorer
summary: The suggestion proposes the establishment of a national police unit dedicated to investigating crimes committed by animal rights activists against farmers in Sweden. It highlights an alarming increase in threats and criminal activities targeting agricultural producers, indicating that farmers and their families live in constant fear. The motion emphasizes the need for a coordinated police effort to track and investigate these incidents to protect both farmers and the country's food production.

title: Ändrade regler för studiestöd
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament support an initiative allowing school authorities to purchase pedagogical services and to increase the subjects permitted for remote teaching. This is aimed at ensuring that all children have a secure educational experience and can attain passing grades. It highlights current challenges in staffing qualified teachers for certain subjects, especially in smaller schools or for less commonly taught languages, and suggests that enabling the purchasing of teaching services and expanding remote instruction in various subjects can enhance educational quality.

title: Kunskapsmål gällande cykling
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1902 av Johan Büser och Anna Johansson (båda S)
summary: The motion advocates for increased collaboration in the planning of the electricity grid in Sweden, emphasizing the importance of renewable energy access for all regions. It calls for Svenska kraftnät to involve local authorities, counties, and landowners early in the planning process for new transmission lines to minimize impact on individuals and landowners. The proposal seeks to ensure that local input is integrated into the decision-making regarding the infrastructure required to support the growing demand for electric power in various sectors, including transportation.

title: Västsahara
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish government ensure that compensation is paid to victims who have been awarded damages by the courts, addressing the issue that many convicted individuals do not have the financial means to fulfill their payment obligations. This can lead to a situation where the punishment is seen as ineffective, and the debts of the convicted continue to grow, exacerbating the problem. The motion calls for legislative review to facilitate timely payments to victims and to explore ways to ensure that those ordered to pay damages can do so.

title: Kärnvapen
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1900 av Johan Büser och Gunilla Carlsson (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes improvements to the tax deduction legislation for donations to non-profit organizations, including exploring options for legal entities to receive tax reductions, expanding eligible charitable purposes, raising deduction limits, and simplifying the reporting process for recipient organizations. The aim is to enhance the support for civil society and strengthen social capital in Sweden.

title: Komplettera kraven för auktion av frekvenserna 3,4–3,8 GHz avsedda för 5G-utbyggnad
summary: The motion proposes that Sweden deepens its transatlantic cooperation to work towards the global decriminalization of homosexuality by officially joining the U.S. campaign on this issue and declaring it as a primary objective of Sweden's foreign policy. This aims to address laws in around seventy countries that criminalize homosexuality and lead to persecution and violence against LGBTQ+ individuals, leveraging U.S. political and economic influence for better outcomes.

title: Omorganisation av körskoleutbildningen till gymnasie- och vuxenutbildningen
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1898 av Hanna Westerén och Anna-Caren Sätherberg (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament increase state funding for the decontamination of polluted land in Småland's Glass Kingdom and other locations in the country. It highlights the risks posed to public health by hazardous substances such as arsenic, cadmium, and lead that have contaminated areas due to historical glass production. The motion emphasizes the long-standing nature of these environmental issues and the inadequacy of current state support, which has left crucial decontamination projects at risk of delay.

title: Gotländsk färjetrafik – en del av svensk infrastruktur
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1897 av Hanna Westerén och Laila Naraghi (båda S)
summary: The proposal by the Left Party calls for the rejection of the government's bill which allows for advance payment for public document requests. They assert that the right to access public documents is fundamental to democracy and argue that requiring advance payment could hinder access. The Left Party suggests that advance payment should only be pursued in cases where there are specific grounds for doing so, ensuring that the process remains accessible and efficient.

title: Flygets betydelse för Gotland
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish government assign a suitable authority to conduct a comprehensive study on the vulnerability of police officers to crime while on duty and how such crimes affect individual officers. Additionally, it calls for the government to present measures aimed at enhancing the safety of police officers' working environment, particularly for those in external service. The motion emphasizes the importance of improving both the physical and psychosocial work conditions for police officers to ensure the law enforcement agency remains an attractive workplace.

title: Gotländsk reservhamn
summary: The proposal urges the Swedish government to promptly review the regulations within the condominium law and other relevant provisions based on the recommendations from the National Audit Office. It emphasizes the need to strengthen consumer protection for buyers of newly constructed condominiums due to existing inadequacies compared to protections offered in other consumer markets. The recommendation calls for government action to provide timely legal protections that recognize the significant financial implications for individual buyers.

title: Stoppa Israels annektering av palestinskt territorium
summary: The motion addresses the increasing problem of illegal signage along roads, highlighting various types of unauthorized signs that pose traffic dangers and detract from the natural landscape. It calls for improved oversight by having the same authority responsible for both issuing permits and conducting inspections, as well as introducing sanctions for non-compliance. The motion also proposes implementing a responsibility for those placing signs on others' property to ensure that proper permissions have been obtained.

title: Förbättrad integration
summary: The motion proposed by Monika Lövgren and Mikael Strandman of the Sweden Democrats (SD) advocates for the establishment of adequate stockpiles of iodine tablets in healthcare facilities such as hospitals, healthcare centers, and pharmacies in Sweden to ensure preparedness for potential radioactive incidents. Additionally, it suggests allowing the public to order iodine tablets directly from pharmacies. The proposal underscores the need for improved societal preparedness, particularly in light of past nuclear accidents and the potential threats posed by radioactive releases due to various incidents.

title: Beräkningen av bostadstillägget
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1892 av Hanna Westerén och Laila Naraghi (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes that the TBE vaccine be gradually included in the national childhood vaccination program to ensure equal access to healthcare and protection against a serious viral disease that can have severe long-term effects, regardless of individuals' financial capacity.

title: Aktiv bostadspolitik
summary: The suggestion advocates for the Inspektionen för strategiska produkter (ISP) to be equipped with necessary financial expertise to fulfill its new responsibilities related to foreign investments, particularly in light of security risks posed by inappropriate international actors. It emphasizes the importance of attracting foreign direct investments for Sweden's economic development while safeguarding vital assets from undue influence, urging the government to enhance ISP's capabilities and consider a national review system for foreign investments.

title: Riksintressen
summary: The motion proposes a prohibition on new Muslim charter schools in Sweden and calls for stricter oversight of all religious charter schools, specifically targeting perceived violations of democratic values and regulations within Muslim schools. The motion argues that existing Muslim charter schools have displayed significant misconduct, including reports of violence, gender segregation, and ties to extremist ideologies, and asserts that these issues contribute to the ongoing 'Islamization' of Sweden. The goal is to ensure compliance with non-confessional educational standards and promote integration into Swedish society.

title: Digitaliseringspolitik – styrning och ledning
summary: This proposal calls for a ban on the wearing of full-face Muslim veils, such as burqas and niqabs, in all public spaces in Sweden, citing similar bans already in place in Denmark and several other European countries. The motion emphasizes the importance of defending democratic, cultural, and secular values against perceived threats posed by such garments, which are characterized as oppressive to women.

title: Funktionshinderspolitik
summary: The proposal calls for an investigation into the extent of foreign funding received by mosques and Muslim congregations in Sweden, particularly from countries associated with Islamist ideologies. It urges the government to consider banning foreign financing for religious groups and to establish that Muslim organizations operating in Sweden should hold a fundamentally positive view of Swedish society and its norms.

title: Offentliga försäkringar och a-kassa
summary: The motion proposes a ban on the wearing of Muslim veils in Swedish preschools and elementary schools, arguing that such veils symbolize religious subservience and gender segregation, which contradict the values of equality and democracy in Swedish society. It emphasizes the need to protect children from religious pressures, allowing them to grow as independent and critical thinkers, and claims that such practices violate children's rights as outlined in the Convention on the Rights of the Child.

title: Jämlik skattepolitik
summary: The motion suggests that all official uniforms, particularly for the police and military, should be completely free of any religious or political symbols to maintain neutrality in governmental authority. The proponent, Richard Jomshof, argues that allowing religious symbols could undermine trust in the police and that neutral representation is essential for public confidence, stressing that if some groups are permitted to display religious symbols, it would necessitate similar allowances for others, potentially leading to discrimination.

title: Differentierad ölskatt
summary: The proposal advocates for a ban on halal and kosher slaughter methods in Sweden, asserting that meat from animals slaughtered without prior stunning causes unnecessary pain and suffering. It calls for clear labeling of such meat sold in the country, efforts to push for regulations at the EU level to introduce similar labeling requirements, and seeks exceptions in EU rules to prohibit the import of non-stunned slaughtered meat. The motion emphasizes strengthening Sweden's stance against such practices within the EU and ensuring that meat procured through public contracts adheres to Swedish animal welfare standards.

title: En avgiftsfri skola på riktigt
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1883 av Joakim Järrebring och Kenneth G Forslund (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes a ban on the commercial use of natural resources under Sweden's right of public access (allemansrätten) without the landowner's permission. It highlights tensions between landowners and commercial enterprises regarding organized berry and mushroom picking and suggests that companies should rent land for such activities to protect both the right of access and the interests of landowners.

title: NPF-säkrad skola
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1882 av Joakim Järrebring och Kenneth G Forslund (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish parliament should prohibit applause during debates, arguing that applause can create an unequal representation of opinions based on the number of members present and their party affiliations. The authors believe that removing applause would foster a more respectful debate climate, as each elected representative's voice is meant to represent the views of many citizens equally.

title: Förbjud införsel av kärnvapen (FISE)
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1881 av Joakim Järrebring och Aylin Fazelian (båda S)
summary: The proposal suggests that non-medical interventions, such as cosmetic surgeries, should not qualify for sickness benefits. The rationale is that the current system imposes significant financial burdens on both businesses and the state when employees take sick leave for non-medical procedures. The motion advocates for a revision of the legislation to exclude these interventions from being sickness benefit qualifying events.

title: Förebyggande folkhälsoansvar
summary: The Swedish government proposes to strengthen consumer protection in the deposit market by repealing the current law governing deposit companies. This change aims to ensure that deposits in such companies are subject to stricter regulations, akin to those governing traditional banks, including the necessity for obtaining an operating license. The goal is to facilitate better consumer understanding of the safety of their deposits and the distinction between guaranteed and non-guaranteed deposits.

title: Säkra riksvägarnas kvalitet
summary: The proposal suggests a review of the Swedish Broadcasting Authority's impartiality, aiming to investigate the future operation of the examination committee and the appointment process of its members. The motion points to an increase in complaints regarding public service broadcasting, despite a decrease in the number of critical rulings. It highlights concerns over potential biases among journalists, suggesting that the public must trust the impartiality of public service media given its significant role in democratic discourse.

title: Sänkning av hastighetsgränser
summary: The proposal suggests that the Swedish parliament should review the possibility of abolishing a 2% surcharge on fuel taxes, which is applied in addition to the general price indexation. The motion argues that recent tax increases on gasoline and diesel, including this additional surcharge, have led to unsustainable hikes in fuel prices. It contends that such tax increases should be decided by parliament rather than applied automatically, and emphasizes the importance of maintaining affordable fuel prices for families and individuals who rely on cars for daily activities, while also calling for technological advancements to reduce emissions instead of relying on higher taxes.

title: Den cirkulära ekonomins behov av hantverkare
summary: The motion proposes stricter regulations regarding coordination numbers to combat widespread misuse in society. It suggests implementing stronger penalties for misusing coordination numbers, exceeding those for forgery, and requires a clearer mechanism for verifying the legitimacy of individuals connected to these numbers. Additionally, the proposal advocates for biometric data integration, limits on vehicle registration tied to coordination numbers, and the establishment of a database for employers to check valid work permits.

title: Transparent kontakt elev-skola-vårdnadshavare genom hela skoltiden
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1876 av Lotta Finstorp och Ann-Sofie Lifvenhage (båda M)
summary: The motion proposes stricter regulations for the issuance and handling of Swedish passports, suggesting that each passport holder should only be allowed to possess two passports within a five-year period and implement more costly replacements for lost passports. It also calls for enhanced penalties for illegal activities related to passport handling, including the sale, loan, or unauthorized manipulation of passports. The proposal emphasizes increased police involvement and the use of biometric data to strengthen passport security.

title: Myndigheter i hela Sverige - inte bara i storstäderna
summary: This motion proposes to strengthen the control over benefit recipients' residence status during benefit disbursements, allow government agencies to share their registers for better detection of fraud, and conduct a census to clarify residency registrations and benefits eligibility. It highlights cases where individuals affiliated with foreign governments unlawfully receive Swedish aid and calls for tighter regulations to prevent taxpayer-funded fraud.

title: Kronofogdemyndighetens kontor
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament appoint the Broadcasting Board through a parliamentary group and calls for stricter penalties for violations of broadcasting licenses. The current operation of the Broadcasting Board has been deemed unsatisfactory, particularly regarding its impartiality rulings, leading to demands for a more proportionate representation of party interests in the Board's appointment process and the imposition of meaningful sanctions for serious breaches of regulations.

title: Fler poliser – även på mindre orter
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1873 av Viktor Wärnick och John Weinerhall (båda M)
summary: The proposal advocates for the increase of penalties for crimes against ancient monuments, emphasizing the recent vandalism of historical sites and the irreversible damage inflicted on these cultural heritage items. The motion suggests that current penalties are insufficient to deter such crimes, leading to a lack of police investigations, and calls for a doubling of the punishment scale, mandating a minimum six-month prison sentence for theft and higher fines for negligent damages.

title: Skärpta befogenheter vid förvar av utlänningar
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament clarifies the Social Services Act to explicitly state that individuals residing illegally in Sweden are not entitled to financial assistance. The suggestion aims to provide clear guidance to municipalities regarding the rights to social support for undocumented migrants, as there are currently varying interpretations of the law across different regions.

title: Sanering av mark för att möjliggöra tillväxt
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish government should approve foreign investments and purchases of strategically important infrastructure by foreign entities, particularly those from outside the EU, such as China and Russia. It emphasizes the need for government oversight on these transactions, especially those deemed critical to national security, and suggests that the government should have the authority to deny any such investment that could jeopardize national safety, overriding municipal autonomy in the process.

title: Allmän jakt på skarv samt andra åtgärder
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1870 av Viktor Wärnick och John Weinerhall (båda M)
summary: The proposal suggests that the Swedish Parliament declare Uppåkra a national interest and ensure the continuation of its operations by collaborating with the foundation and the county administrative board to establish museum and educational activities at the site. Given Uppåkra's significant archaeological value, being one of the oldest inhabited locations in Sweden, the motion emphasizes the need for state involvement to maintain its historical relevance and visitor engagement.

title: Strandskyddet
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1869 av Viktor Wärnick och John Weinerhall (båda M)
summary: Robert Stenkvist from the Sweden Democrats proposes a requirement for the registration of prepaid mobile phone cards, arguing that this change would hinder criminal activities that utilize anonymous cards. The motion emphasizes that requiring personal registration will facilitate police investigations and outweigh concerns about privacy and ease of access to prepaid cards.

title: Länen norr om Dalälven
summary: This proposal suggests establishing time limits for the use of state-funded language interpretation services, advocating that individuals who have lived in Sweden for more than five years should not be entitled to such services. The aim is to emphasize the importance of learning the Swedish language as part of integration into Swedish society, with exceptions for those who have medical reasons affecting their language abilities.

title: Bygga ut E4 Söderhamn–Gävle till fyrfältsväg
summary: The proposal advocates for the preservation and recognition of the Elfdalian language, highlighting its historical significance and distinctiveness from modern Swedish. It calls for the Swedish Parliament to officially acknowledge Elfdalian as a regional or minority language and to allocate funds for educational resources, such as textbooks and classes, to support its teaching in schools, underlining the importance of cultural heritage.

title: Dubbelspår längs Ostkustbanan
summary: The motion proposed by the Sweden Democrats emphasizes the necessity for security policy competence within the authority responsible for handling foreign direct investments in Sweden. The authors argue that such expertise is crucial for effective control and assessment of these investments, particularly given current security challenges. They also propose that decisions made by this authority should not be subject to appeal in general administrative courts, citing concerns that the ability to contest these decisions could hinder the timely collection of information essential for thorough oversight.

title: Stoppa klippningarna av kopparnäten
summary: The motion proposed by Gudrun Brunegård calls for the Swedish Parliament to honor the memory and contributions of Dag Hammarskjöld, the former United Nations Secretary-General, recognizing his significant role in promoting world peace and his humanitarian efforts. The motion suggests that Hammarskjöld's legacy, including his diplomacy during the Korean War and the Suez Crisis, as well as his posthumous Nobel Peace Prize, merits acknowledgment in the 'Room of Good Deeds' in Parliament, where notable humanitarian figures are commemorated.

title: Utredning gällande ett slöjförbud i för- och grundskolan
summary: The Swedish government's submission to the parliament discusses the International Labour Organization's (ILO) Centenary Declaration for the Future of Work, which emphasizes the importance of social justice in the workforce and outlines key challenges and priorities for member states in shaping equitable and sustainable work environments. Among its main points, the declaration promotes lifelong learning, equality in the workplace, and the transition from informal to formal economies, highlighting the need for collaboration between governments, employers, and workers to address evolving labor challenges while securing decent working conditions globally.

title: Åtgärder mot bidragsfusk genom att dela information
summary: The proposed law aims to establish confidentiality obligations for private service providers when they are contracted by public authorities to technically process or store data. This law seeks to ensure that the data handled by these service providers receives the same level of protection as if it were managed by a public authority, thus enhancing data security during outsourcing operations.

title: Giltighetstid för bygglov
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1862 av Johan Hultberg och Ann-Sofie Alm (båda M)
summary: The Swedish government has submitted a response to the Riksrevisionen's report on the governance and management of holding companies associated with universities and colleges. The report highlights deficiencies in the government’s oversight, suggesting that it has not provided the necessary conditions for active and professional management of these holding companies. The government agrees with most of the findings and has initiated new guidelines to enhance governance and accountability structures. Additionally, a special investigator has been appointed to propose changes to the innovation support frameworks at state universities and colleges.

title: Minska polisbristen – anställ norska poliser
summary: The government's proposal aims to implement stricter regulations regarding the handling of firearms and explosives in Sweden. It seeks to enhance penalties for serious gun offenses and violations related to explosives permits, recognizing the growing issue of illegal weapons and explosives. This includes an increase in maximum prison sentences for particularly severe offenses from six to seven years, and the introduction of new classifications for smuggling weapons and explosives, which will also carry distinct penalties. The proposed changes are set to come into effect on December 1, 2020.

title: Förebygg överdoser efter frigivning från häkte eller fängelse
summary: The government proposes a new law to implement supplementary provisions to the EU regulation on mutual recognition of freezing and forfeiture decisions, aimed at efficiently combatting serious crime and recovering illicit gains. This law will allow for the recognition and enforcement of such decisions across EU member states, enhance international cooperation, and align Swedish legislation with European standards. The proposed law includes amendments to existing laws regarding cooperation with other Nordic countries and the implementation of cross-border legal decisions.

title: Kommunalskatt för delårsboende
summary: The government proposes amendments to the delegation procedures for the Tax Law Committee and the Research Tax Committee. These amendments aim to allow designated officials to make additional decisions beyond preliminary approvals or rejections of such requests. The proposition also addresses the need to combat harmful tax competition, following OECD evaluations that indicate Sweden's shortcomings in meeting international standards for tax information exchange. The proposed changes are intended to enhance the capacity of the Swedish Tax Agency to gather necessary information for decision-making and to adjust local reporting requirements in relation to international standards.

title: Privata arbetsförmedlingar
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1858 av Camilla Waltersson Grönvall och Sten Bergheden (båda M)
summary: The government proposes amendments to the property tax law concerning agricultural properties, aiming to clarify and simplify regulations to enhance the quality of records and ensure fair assessment values. Furthermore, it seeks to enable the tax authority to automate review decisions within property tax assessments, which is expected to reduce processing time and free up resources at the tax authority. The proposed changes are set to take effect from January 1, 2021, with their first application during the general property tax assessment in 2023.

title: Kapitalvinstbeskattning av bostäder
summary: The government proposes a new law with supplementary provisions to the EU regulation on foreign direct investments, establishing a contact point in Sweden for implementing the regulation. The law will grant the designated authority the power to request information from foreign investors and related companies. The proposed changes are set to come into effect on November 1, 2020.

title: Betydelsen av arbete och integration i ett rättssäkert Sverige
summary: The government proposes changes to the regulations regarding minority protection in corporations and economic associations, including housing cooperatives. The aim is to strengthen minority rights while preventing abuse of these rules. The suggestions include allowing a specific auditor or minority auditor to be appointed by the Companies Registration Office without prior approval from a shareholders' meeting, provided at least one-tenth of the shareholders or members support the application. Additionally, it establishes criteria for the independence and suitability of the auditors appointed. The changes are intended to reduce the misuse of minority reviews as a pressure tactic and provide greater freedom to shareholders regarding arbitration procedures in minority share redemption cases.

title: Förutsättningar för och lönsamhet i att investera i kompetensutveckling
summary: Riksrevisionen has examined the efficiency of the employment agency's operations, revealing discrepancies in different employment agents' methods and results, which indicate potential for better efficiency. The findings suggest that agents who adopt a more activity-focused approach significantly improve job placements for job seekers. Moreover, it highlights the inconsistencies in granting training and external support to applicants. Although Riksrevisionen does not propose specific recommendations for the government, it emphasizes the need for the Employment Agency to work towards making better use of allocations for effective operations.

title: Momsfria vårdtjänster
summary: The Swedish government's report addresses the observations and recommendations of the National Audit Office regarding the return operations for individuals without residency in Sweden. The report highlights issues such as ineffective results, high costs, and the weak overall management of return operations conducted by multiple authorities, including the Migration Agency and Police Authority. The government acknowledges the audit's findings and agrees on the necessity to enhance information sharing among agencies to improve the efficiency of return procedures.

title: Bättre förebyggande insatser för unga som riskerar att hamna i kriminalitet
summary: The Swedish government's proposal aims to enhance the working conditions and employee protection for police personnel by introducing three key legislative amendments: allowing police to conduct body searches of interviewees in police or security police facilities for security reasons, expanding the scope of qualified protection identities to include other police personnel, and extending health care staff's obligation to provide certain information to the security police for personal protection work. These changes are intended to improve police recruitment and safety, with the legislation set to take effect on January 1, 2021.

title: Hyvling av anställning/arbetstid
summary: The document presents an account of the management and distribution of funds from the General Inheritance Fund during the fiscal year 2019. It details how the fund supports various initiatives aimed at benefiting children, youth, and individuals with disabilities, along with the evaluation of the Execution Committee’s activities. The government also identifies priority areas for future funding distribution from the fund.

title: Yrkeslegitimationer
summary: The proposal aims to change tax regulations for temporarily employed workers in Sweden, specifically focusing on foreign employees. It seeks to eliminate the current 183-day rule that exempts foreign workers hired from companies without a permanent establishment in Sweden from being taxed if they work for less than 183 days. The new regulations would require these foreign workers to be taxed on income earned while working in Sweden, creating a more equitable tax environment. Additionally, there are adjustments proposed for withholding tax responsibilities for employers outside of Sweden.

title: Utvecklad hälso- och sjukvård efter coronapandemin
summary: The proposal aims to enhance the efficiency and security of court procedures in Sweden by promoting digital communication. It suggests amendments to legal requirements that currently hinder digital processes, allowing for submissions, power of attorney, and other court documents to be filed electronically, thereby reducing reliance on paper documentation. The changes are intended to streamline interactions with the judicial system and facilitate a more modern approach to legal proceedings.

title: En trygg och förutsägbar sjukförsäkring
summary: The proposal seeks to extend the validity of the law (2013:794) governing certain registers for research into the effects of heredity and environment on human health until December 31, 2023. This law is crucial for processing personal data associated with research on significant health issues such as cancer, cardiovascular diseases, and COVID-19. The extension is necessary to ensure that essential research can continue while a long-term regulatory framework for research databases is being developed.

title: Rättssäkerhet och bättre kunskap kring trafikskador
summary: The government presents a proposition outlining Sweden's commitment to implement Agenda 2030 and the sustainable development goals, emphasizing the importance of a cohesive policy nationally and internationally. The proposal includes a proposed overarching goal for sustainable development spanning economic, social, and environmental dimensions, with a commitment to ensuring that no one is left behind. The government highlights the necessity for ongoing integration of these goals into regular processes, and outlines mechanisms for monitoring and reporting progress to the parliament and the international community.

title: Skärpta krav och kontroll av yrkestrafiken
summary: The Swedish government's response to the National Audit Office's report on collaborative and strategic innovation programs highlights issues of clarity and effectiveness in governmental operations. While the government agrees with some of the audit's findings regarding strategic innovation programs, it points out that the audit did not fully appreciate the purpose and logic behind collaborative programs. The government plans to revise its governing documents to enhance clarity in the roles of the involved authorities and aims to ensure effective evaluations of these programs in future innovation efforts.

title: Jönköping Universitys betydelse för regional tillväxt
summary: The proposal aims to introduce a provision allowing the government to establish special regulations for calculating dental care compensation during extraordinary events, such as the COVID-19 pandemic. This is necessary to prevent patients from losing their entitlement to state subsidies due to the inability to complete planned dental treatments within the existing compensation periods, which has been affected by the pandemic. The proposed change is set to take effect on September 1, 2020, and seeks to temporarily address the financial implications for patients unable to access dental care during this period.

title: Stärkt omställningsförmåga genom livslångt lärande
summary: The Swedish government's statement reviews the Riksrevisionen's report on consumer protection related to the purchase of newly produced condominiums. The government acknowledges that it has not adequately safeguarded buyers' interests and agrees with the Riksrevisionen's recommendations for amending the condominium law and related regulations to align consumer protection with other markets. The report emphasizes the need for clearer information about risks and responsibilities during the buying process, as well as increased oversight and transparency in transactions involving new condominiums.

title: Lika tillgång till konsumentvägledning
summary: This parliamentary motion by Elisabeth Svantesson and others from the Moderaterna (Moderates) party addresses the need for the Swedish government to evaluate its funding contributions to public health and healthcare in the context of coronavirus. It emphasizes the importance of having a clear vaccine strategy, ensuring vaccine availability, and managing the vaccination process effectively. Additionally, it argues for a review of financial support to businesses affected by COVID-19, such as Lernia, and calls for necessary capital contributions to Swedavia to ensure the continued development of Arlanda Airport. The motion highlights the need for effective leadership and accountability from the government during the pandemic.

title: Deltidsstudier och sjukersättning
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament evaluate the financial support allocated to Luftfartsverket in the context of competition, following a proposed increase of 900 million kronor to compensate for revenue losses due to the pandemic. The motion argues that support measures should be applied equitably across all air traffic management providers—public and private—to prevent distortion of competition, as many regional airports rely on private companies for air traffic services.

title: F-skatt och ofrivilligt egenföretagande
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish parliament should reject parts of the government's extra budget related to COVID-19, specifically the capital investment proposals aimed at supporting SAS AB and local airports. The Left Party argues that financial support should not exacerbate climate issues and should prioritize environmentally friendly transportation alternatives. They also call for conditions on governmental support to SAS, such as ceasing operations on short routes that can be covered by train and ensuring labor agreements in the Nordic region. There is a focus on the need for climate-conscious policy responses to the pandemic while still addressing the crisis's impact on public services and workers.

title: Bilstöd
summary: This motion from the Sweden Democrats calls for the government to evaluate the recapitalization of SAS AB and the capital injection to Swedavia AB in light of the economic impacts of the coronavirus pandemic. The proposal emphasizes the importance of supporting both companies to ensure the survival of the Swedish aviation industry while maintaining a focus on market-driven conditions rather than imposing stringent environmental requirements that could jeopardize profitability. Moreover, it criticizes the need for taxpayer funding to sustain Lernia AB, a state-owned educational company that has been running at a loss, suggesting that the state should ultimately divest from this entity.

title: Stoppa fusket på vägarna
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1840 av Isak From och Åsa Karlsson (båda S)
summary: The Swedish government proposes a change to the Public Access to Information and Secrecy Act, allowing authorities to require advance payment of fees for copies of public documents in certain cases. This measure aims to address situations where the prescribed fees are not paid and is intended to come into force on January 1, 2021.

title: Förarbevis eller körkort för små snabba båtar och vattenskotrar
summary: The government proposes complementary regulations to the exit agreement between the United Kingdom and the EU concerning the rights of UK citizens residing in Sweden. The proposal includes provisions for British citizens and their family members to apply for a new residency status that aligns with the exit agreement, enabling them to continue residing and working in Sweden. It also stipulates that the Migration Agency will decide on these residency applications and that those granted residency status will be subject to the same expulsion rules as EEA citizens. These regulations are set to come into effect on December 1, 2020.

title: Norra Sverige behöver också bra vägstandard
summary: The report from the Swedish National Audit Office evaluates the 'rutavdraget' (a tax deduction for household services) and assesses whether the intentions of the parliament have been met. It concludes that while there have been some positive effects on market activity among buyers of services and on employment for some groups, the claim that the tax deduction is self-financing lacks solid empirical support. The audit office recommends that the government revisit calculations regarding the long-term sustainability of the tax deduction and consider the effects of potential labor immigration on employment policies.

title: För klimatets skull bygg mera i trä
summary: The proposal aims to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of municipal rescue services in Sweden by introducing stronger governmental oversight and clearly defined guidelines for disaster prevention and response. Key changes include the establishment of national objectives for safety operations, improved organization of command structures within municipalities, increased supervisory authority for the Civil Contingencies Agency (MSB), and the ability for MSB to allocate resources from a national perspective during emergencies. The proposed changes emphasize the need for municipalities to maintain comprehensive leadership in their rescue services and to improve their disaster response capabilities, especially in rural areas.

title: Ekonomisk trygghet vid sjukdom och funktionsnedsättning
summary: The proposal introduces a regional tax reduction that enables individuals living in specified sparsely populated municipalities, primarily in Norrland and northwestern Svealand, to receive a tax deduction of 1,675 kronor annually against their municipal income tax. The proposal also includes provisions for business owners to qualify for this tax reduction if they meet the EU's minimal economic aid conditions and requires them to disclose any other minor aid received in the past three years when exceeding 150,000 kronor. The changes are set to take effect on December 1, 2020, applicable to the tax year following December 31, 2019.

title: Krafttag mot bidragsfusk och felaktiga utbetalningar
summary: The proposed legislation aims to empower the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority (Finansinspektionen) to impose special fees on parties that violate their obligations under the EU regulations regarding OTC derivatives and transparency in securities financing transactions. The amendments are necessitated by updates in EU regulations that mandate stricter compliance measures. Additionally, the changes will allow for enforcement actions against non-legal entity counterparties, thereby enhancing regulatory control and oversight.

title: Ekonomisk trygghet vid ålderdom
summary: The proposal suggests implementing confidentiality regulations within a government agency's operations concerning the licensing or supervision of financial transactions and holdings. Specifically, it aims to protect information about transactions with or holdings of financial instruments to prevent the disclosure of identities related to suspected breaches of credit institution regulations. The changes are intended to align with European Union directives and ensure a uniform approach to confidentiality in financial matters. The law modifications are set to take effect on December 1, 2020.

title: En trygg välfärd under coronakrisen
summary: The government presents a report detailing the management of state-owned companies and their operations as of the end of 2019. The document outlines the government's active role in ensuring the long-term value development of these companies, emphasizing the importance of social mandates while adapting to changing global conditions. It highlights the strategic goals for sustainable value creation and increased transparency regarding climate impact. Additionally, the report discusses the regulatory frameworks for how these companies operate, recent performance metrics, and the government's ongoing initiatives to enhance their stewardship while balancing financial interests with social responsibilities.

title: Barnvänlig familjepolitik
summary: The Swedish government's proposal involves additional changes to the 2020 state budget in response to the impact of the coronavirus pandemic. Key measures include financial compensation for at-risk groups who cannot work from home, capital investments in government-owned companies, increased support for healthcare and cultural initiatives, and infrastructure enhancements related to the COVID-19 outbreak. The proposal seeks to enhance social safety nets and ensure economic stability during the crisis.

title: Försenade EU-ersättningar till lantbruket
summary: The suggestion calls for a comprehensive reform of primary care in Sweden, emphasizing the need for clear definitions of primary care duties, incorporating preventive work and rehabilitation, ensuring continuity of care through designated physicians and coordinated healthcare teams, and establishing guidelines for national compensation systems to support coordinated care. It highlights the necessity of digital healthcare solutions, systematic health checks, and quality measurement within the primary care framework, aiming to enhance accessibility and efficiency for vulnerable and chronically ill patients.

title: Dispenser i fråga om avloppslösningar
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish government amend the Mineral Act to extend the validity period of all exploration permits valid as of July 1, 2020, by an additional year. This extension is aimed at mitigating the impact of COVID-19 on the mining and mineral sector, which is vital for the Swedish economy, particularly for prospecting companies lacking income from their own mining production. The proposal seeks to provide clarity and stability for all valid permits, as current provisions only cater to permits extended under special circumstances, leaving out many stakeholders.

title: Sexualbrott
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1829 av Betty Malmberg och Marléne Lund Kopparklint (båda M)
summary: The proposal calls for the Swedish government to amend the Mineral Act to extend the validity period of all exploration permits by one year, in response to the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic. The motion highlights the difficulties faced by small, specialized prospecting companies that rely on external capital for their operations, stressing the importance of maintaining and supporting the mining industry to meet the increasing demand for metals and facilitate the energy transition. The motion argues against the government's current proposal, which only extends permits in their final year, labeling this limitation as unjustified.

title: En modernisering av rättegångsbalken avseende omedelbarhetsprincipen
summary: The motion calls for the Swedish government to amend the mineral law to extend the validity period for all exploration permits valid as of July 1, 2020, by one additional year. This proposal aims to address the negative impacts of the coronavirus pandemic on the mining and mineral sector, particularly on small prospecting companies that lack revenue from mining production and rely on external capital. The motion criticizes the government's original proposal for being too narrow, as it only applies to permits in their final renewal phase, potentially leaving many companies without the needed extension, which risks the future of the Swedish mining industry.

title: Preskriptionstid för sexualbrott mot barn och andra typer av sexualbrott
summary: The motion proposes reforms to strengthen primary healthcare in Sweden, emphasizing the inclusion of health promotion in primary care's fundamental mission, the right to a fixed doctor, and support for a manageable patient load per physician. It advocates for direct state funding to ensure staffing and competence in primary care and aims to reduce administrative burdens on healthcare personnel. Additionally, it calls for a national definition of primary care's tasks to guarantee equitable access to healthcare across the country.

title: Placera viltmyndigheten i Skaraborg
summary: The Kristdemokraterna (Christian Democrats) motion seeks to grant the Swedish Customs (Tullverket) expanded powers to seize suspected stolen goods, responding to the government's proposal for strengthening Tullverket's enforcement capabilities against organized crime. The motion emphasizes the need for the government to align its actions with the Swedish Parliament's prior demands for increased Customs authority, as well as a thorough review of the legislative framework surrounding Tullverket's operations to ensure effective crime prevention.

title: Se över reglerna för allemansrätten
summary: This motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament grants the Customs Authority (Tullverket) the power to prevent stolen goods from being exported out of the country and to enhance its crime-fighting responsibilities. The authors argue that increased authority for Tullverket is necessary to address the growing challenges posed by theft rings, which have been able to export stolen goods relatively effortlessly. They emphasize the need for better border protection and collaborative efforts with other agencies to combat rising international crime effectively.

title: Lagen om belastningsregister
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament support a renegotiation of the Audiovisual Media Services Directive (AV-directive) to abolish the requirement for streaming services to maintain a quota of 30% European productions in their offerings. The authors argue that EU intervention in media content is inappropriate and that such quotas limit the diversity of programming available to audiences. They emphasize that decisions about programming should be left to media companies and consumers, rather than being regulated by political bodies.

title: Livsmedelsverkets effektivitet när det gäller besiktning av slaktdjur
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish government should amend the Mining Act to extend the validity period for all exploration permits to prevent them from expiring, particularly as several permits are set to run out in the summer and fall of 2020. The Liberals agree with the government's timeline for the new law to take effect on July 1, 2020, but they argue that the proposed legal solution may exclude certain exploration permits, especially those in early stages, from the extension. They assert that all permits should be extended regardless of their progress in the exploration process, while agreeing that permits for coal, oil, and gas exploration should not be included in the extension.

title: Organisationers påverkan på skyddsjakt och licensjakt
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish government should amend the Minerals Act to extend the validity period for exploration permits for mining, especially in light of challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, which has negatively impacted the mining industry and investment. The motion calls for a uniform extension for all valid exploration permits, excluding those related to oil or natural gas, in order to provide certainty and stability for the sector and ensure its growth as an essential part of Sweden's export-driven economy.

title: Återinför ett utvidgat tjänstemannaansvar
summary: The motion by the Sweden Democrats (SD) addresses the modernization of radio and TV legislation in light of the revised Audiovisual Media Services (AV) Directive. It proposes improvements to content requirements for streaming services while opposing the introduction of a quota mandating 30% European content. The motion argues that such regulations restrict freedom of expression and access to diverse content. Additionally, it raises concerns about public service media's inclusion in a new media ethics system and advocates for transparency and parliamentary oversight in media funding.

title: Märkning av importerat halalslaktat kött
summary: The motion proposed by Karin Rågsjö and others from the Left Party focuses on reforming primary healthcare in Sweden to enhance accessibility, quality, and equity of care. It calls for the government to assess the needs for primary care units, improve rehabilitation services, and review how patient responsibility is allocated. The motion emphasizes the need for a shift away from mandatory market mechanisms in primary care, advocating for more state control and a structured approach to address disparities in healthcare access, particularly for vulnerable populations.

title: Bättre förutsättningar för privata helikopterföretags medverkan i samhällsviktiga verksamheter
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1819 av Isak From och Helén Pettersson (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish government should analyze the consequences of the proposed transition support for individual entrepreneurs and provide an evaluation by September 21, 2020. The Moderaterna party emphasizes the importance of adapting crisis measures to the long-term economic challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic. They argue for necessary changes to ensure that individual entrepreneurs receive equitable support compared to other business forms and advocate for a temporary adjustment to unemployment insurance, allowing partial receipt while maintaining business activities.

title: Rättvisa system
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1818 av Isak From och Björn Wiechel (båda S)
summary: The suggestion proposes that the Swedish government should evaluate the temporary support measures for businesses affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly looking into the duration of the support and regulations regarding profit distribution for companies. It emphasizes the need for an extension of the support period from two to four months, consideration of smaller businesses' unique circumstances, and strong measures against fraud within the support framework. Additionally, the proposal calls for a rejection of certain agreements regarding European guarantees for unemployment support due to concerns about complicating the national response to economic challenges.

title: Fjällens hjältar
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1817 av Isak From och Björn Wiechel (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes several evaluations and modifications regarding government assistance measures for businesses and non-profit organizations affected by the coronavirus pandemic. It emphasizes the need to extend the support period for transitional assistance beyond March-April 2020, to include vital income sources for civil society organizations, and to clarify eligibility criteria for private companies that predominantly serve public actors. The motion advocates for adjustments to ensure fair access to support for various sectors and to make the comparison periods for assessing financial loss more flexible.

title: Konkurrens med rättvisa villkor för tunga godstransporter
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1816 av Isak From och Åsa Karlsson (båda S)
summary: The motion from the Left Party critiques the government's proposals for economic support in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, specifically rejecting the proposed 'restructuring support' for businesses. They argue it disproportionately benefits capital owners and suggest alternative support mechanisms focused on small and medium-sized enterprises. The motion also opposes the government's agreement with the European Commission regarding guarantees related to the SURE initiative, citing concerns over increased EU financial power without democratic control, while advocating for further funding to the welfare sector to enhance resource allocation.

title: Studier som en väg tillbaka till arbete
summary: The government proposes an amendment to the Mineral Act in response to the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic on the mining industry, specifically allowing for an extension of the validity period for exploration permits that are due to expire. Permits valid as of July 1, 2020, that have previously been extended may be further extended for one additional year. This amendment is intended to support exploration companies facing difficulties due to the pandemic's effects on their operations.

title: Talmannens befogenheter
summary: The government proposes additional measures to address the societal impacts of the COVID-19 outbreak, introducing a transitional support scheme for businesses experiencing decreased revenue due to the pandemic. This support is intended for registered entities in Sweden, with specified requirements and oversight by the Tax Agency. The proposal also includes adjustments to the state budget to enhance welfare, increase testing capacity, and provide guarantees to the EU for loans to member states and institutions supporting businesses affected by COVID-19.

title: Förbifart Örnsköldsvik
summary: The motion proposes that the government enhance its oversight of public health measures in restaurants during the COVID-19 pandemic. It suggests that the government ensure that municipal health officials effectively supervise compliance with health regulations and clarify the criteria for such supervision. Moreover, it emphasizes the need for comprehensive communication and collaboration with restaurant operators and industry organizations to develop guidelines that mitigate virus spread. The motion calls for an exploration of expanding these public health measures to other sectors potentially at risk of virus transmission.

title: Ökat träbyggande
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1812 av Ingemar Nilsson och Kristina Nilsson (båda S)
summary: The government proposes a new law introducing temporary infection control measures for dining establishments to curb the spread of COVID-19. The law places the responsibility on restaurant operators to implement specific safety measures and allows local health authorities to oversee compliance, issue orders, and impose sanctions if necessary. The law is set to take effect on July 1, 2020, and will remain in force until the end of 2020.

title: Klyftan mellan stad och land
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1811 av Kalle Olsson och Anna-Caren Sätherberg (båda S)
summary: The Swedish government's response to the Riksrevisionen's report highlights several deficiencies in the implementation of state measures aimed at increasing the proportion of environmentally friendly vehicles since 2006. It emphasizes the need for thorough consequence analyses before the introduction of new incentives, efficient assessment of societal costs versus benefits, and the establishment of stable conditions for the automobile market. The government recognizes the recommendations for reducing export costs of subsidized environmental cars and improving the structuring of the bonus-malus system to achieve climate goals effectively.

title: Polisens närvaro på våra landsbygder
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1810 av Kalle Olsson och Anna-Caren Sätherberg (båda S)
summary: The government proposal outlines amendments to Swedish radio and television laws to implement changes to the EU's Audiovisual Media Services Directive. It includes provisions for new regulations on video-sharing platforms, protection for minors, requirements for accessibility for individuals with disabilities, and adjustments to advertising and product placement guidelines. Additionally, it suggests establishing a self-regulating system for media ethics and proposes the removal of certain privacy requirements for public service broadcasting if requested by the companies, with changes set to take effect on December 1, 2020.

title: Ännu mer lika - utjämna mer
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1809 av Kalle Olsson och Anna-Caren Sätherberg (båda S)
summary: The proposal expands the Swedish Customs Authority's (Tullverket) authority to initiate pre-investigations related not only to smuggling offenses but also to crimes involving possession or use of narcotics, possession of doping substances, and possession of health hazardous goods.
