summary: The proposal presents a comprehensive report on tax expenditures in Sweden for the years 2023 to 2025. It details the effects of special regulations in tax legislation on tax revenues and aims to provide a broader basis for prioritizing budgetary support and initiatives. The document includes methods for calculating tax expenditures, forecasts, and descriptions of individual tax expenditures. The report adheres to the legal requirements for transparency in tax expenditure reporting and emphasizes the importance of fiscal efficiency and equity in taxation.

title: Stoppa penningflödena till skatteparadisen
summary: The government proposes amendments to the state budget for 2024 to support the financial reconstruction of Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS), which has initiated a Chapter 11 process in the United States. This includes authorizing the government to allocate a portion of Sweden's outstanding loan claims against the SAS consortium to SAS AB as part of the reconstruction efforts. The measures seek to ensure that the state can act responsibly as a minority shareholder, while also stipulating that all actions are subject to approval by the European Commission.

title: Öläge
summary: The government proposes amendments to the Aviation Security Act that allow airport operators to cover certain costs related to passenger and baggage security checks through sources other than fees, specifically to alleviate the economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic. This change is set to take effect on August 1, 2024, and will remain in effect until July 31, 2025.

title: Delårsskatt, sommarskatt, rättvis skatt - se över möjligheten att låta kommuner få skatteintäkter som motsvarar faktiska kostnader och befolkningsunderlag
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1429 av Barbro Westerholm och Lina Nordquist (båda L)
summary: The proposal presents a new law on unemployment insurance in Sweden, which stipulates that eligibility for unemployment benefits will be dependent on income. Applicants must meet an income requirement, and the benefits will be calculated based on the same incomes used for qualification. The proposal includes varying benefit levels based on the duration of membership in an unemployment fund, a phased reduction of benefits during unemployment, and differentiation in the length of benefits based on the applicant's attachment to the labor market. The upper age limit for receiving benefits is proposed to be 66 years, aligning with pension eligibility starting from January 1, 2026. The new law is set to come into effect on October 1, 2025.

title: Dags att börja planera för en andra Ölandsbro
summary: The Swedish government's document outlines a ten-year national strategy for businesses in the cultural and creative sectors, addressing the need for comprehensive support to foster sustainable development and innovation. The strategy emphasizes six key areas: national statistics, copyright knowledge, guidance and financing support, workforce development, sustainable environments, and enhancing international outreach for cultural businesses. It aims to acknowledge the importance of these sectors in contributing to economic growth and cultural diversity in Sweden.

title: Maktutredning
summary: The government has submitted a memorandum to the parliament regarding the management of the cultural heritage within the Church of Sweden. The memorandum outlines the provisions for protecting ecclesiastical cultural monuments as specified in Sweden's cultural heritage legislation, as well as the utilization of government financial support for the maintenance and care of these monuments from 2002 to 2022. It also addresses issues of accessibility, knowledge, cooperation between the Church and government authorities, and the future funding and preparedness concerning the care of ecclesiastical cultural heritage. The government emphasizes the importance of continued collaboration between the state and the Church to preserve and develop these cultural assets.

title: Stärk den svenska spelutvecklingsbranschen
summary: The motion presented by Katarina Luhr and others from the Green Party calls for the Swedish government to propose new legislation that modifies the existing rules surrounding tenant evictions in cases of criminal behavior. It emphasizes the need to ensure a fair process for tenants whose behavior disrupts neighborhood safety, while also critiquing the government's previous proposals for being potentially disproportionate and insufficiently detailed, raising concerns about collective punishment. The Green Party advocates for preventive measures and collaboration among various stakeholders to enhance community safety without infringing on individuals' rights, particularly emphasizing the importance of protecting families from homelessness due to actions of individual members.

title: Stärk järnvägsförbindelsen mellan Stockholm och Oslo
summary: The proposal urges the government to evaluate and ensure that new legislation regarding housing supports the rights of children as outlined in the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, rejecting parts of a current proposition that would worsen security in residential areas. The motion argues that existing measures have failed to effectively reduce severe crime rates and claims that the government's punitive approaches, including easier eviction processes for tenants, are counterproductive. Instead, it calls for comprehensive support systems in socio-economically disadvantaged areas to prevent youth recruitment into gang crime.

title: Utbildningsinstitutioners regionala ansvar
summary: The proposal suggests that a Natura 2000 permit should not be a prerequisite for granting a mining concession under the Mineral Act. The changes aim to streamline the concession review process while ensuring compliance with EU regulations regarding assessments of impacts on habitats and species within a Natura 2000 area. The legal amendments are proposed to come into effect on July 1, 2024.

title: Stärk synskadades frihet
summary: The government's summary report addresses the conclusions and recommendations from the Riksrevision's evaluation of the emergency number 112 management by the state and SOS Alarm. The Riksrevision found that the handling of alarms was inefficient, partly due to the government's insufficient oversight and the absence of regulatory framework, which led to unclear roles and responsibilities. The government agrees with the findings, emphasizes the importance of meeting the goal of an average response time of 8 seconds, and acknowledges improvements in 2023. The report outlines recommendations for better regulation and oversight of SOS Alarm to enhance emergency service efficiency.

title: Stärk barns rättigheter vid nationella adoptioner
summary: The Swedish government acknowledges the findings of the Audit Office regarding the inefficiencies in the system for revoking residence permits. The government's response outlines its agreement with the recommendations made by the Audit Office and expresses the intention to improve the processes within the Migration Agency, increase priority on revocation cases, and enhance inter-agency information sharing to better manage and execute revocations when legally warranted.

title: Skydda Sveriges fornlämningar
summary: The Swedish government has submitted a report addressing the findings of the Riksrevisionen regarding information security at universities and colleges, particularly focusing on the management of sensitive research data. The Riksrevisionen concluded that these institutions are not effectively protecting such data, identifying significant gaps in classification and handling practices. Recommendations include enhancing knowledge and competency in information security measures among staff and establishing a collaborative support function for information security at these institutions. The government acknowledges the urgency of improved information security in light of increasing digital threats and has initiated steps to address these issues.

title: Oberoende och professionell revision av kommuner och regioner
summary: The Swedish government's report outlines the country's strategic export control policy regarding military equipment and dual-use products for 2023. It details the framework under which exports are permitted, emphasizing the need for compliance with both national laws and international obligations. The report highlights Sweden's export performance, collaborations within the European Union, and the impact of geopolitical events, particularly the ongoing conflict in Ukraine, which has significantly influenced export regulations and practices. The government stresses the importance of strict export controls to fulfill international commitments and ensure national security.

title: Lättnader för bebyggelse på jordbruksmark
summary: The government proposes an amendment to the law on electronic toll systems to comply with the EU's EETS directive, enabling toll collectors to access information about EETS payment service providers' customers and their vehicles. This is necessary for collectors to fulfill their obligations to tax authorities. The changes are intended to facilitate cross-border information exchange regarding unpaid tolls and will come into effect on July 1, 2024.

title: Förtydliga skattelagstiftningen i fråga om styrelsearvoden
summary: The government presented a report to parliament summarizing its assessment of the Swedish National Audit Office's observations and recommendations regarding the application of the fiscal policy framework in 2023. While the government generally agrees with the audit office's conclusions that the fiscal policy is largely compliant with the established framework, it acknowledges areas for improvement, such as enhancing transparency in the use of indicators and methods for calculating structural savings. The government partially disagrees with the recommendation to conduct a deeper analysis of municipal and regional budget requirements, citing challenges in obtaining quality data. Overall, the government reaffirmed its commitment to continuous improvement in fiscal reporting and analysis.

title: Friskvårdsbidrag för alla företagsformer
summary: The proposal from the Center Party advocates for various amendments to the legislation regarding tenancy agreements with a focus on improving the security of residential areas. Key suggestions include removing certain stipulations related to overcrowding in apartments, prioritizing specific urgent cases in tenancy disputes, and ensuring that landlords notify tenants with children before lease termination. Additionally, the motion seeks to establish a monitoring process for the effects of these legislative changes two years after they are enacted, while opposing the government's stance on property access for inspection purposes.

title: En riksomfattande kommunsammanslagningsreform
summary: The Swedish government proposes new regulations to implement two EU directives pertaining to corporate sustainability reporting and gender balance on company boards. The first directive aims to enhance transparency for investors by requiring comprehensive sustainability reports from a broader range of companies, including small and medium-sized ones. This aims to manage financial risks associated with climate change and promote sustainable investments. The second directive introduces reporting requirements regarding the gender composition of board members in publicly listed companies. These legislative changes are set to take effect on July 1, 2024, with specific provisions regarding gender balance applicable from fiscal years starting after 2024.

title: En hållbar strategi för regionala flygplatser
summary: The government submitted a report to the parliament addressing the findings and recommendations made by the Swedish National Audit Office (Riksrevisionen) regarding the state's governance and oversight of pharmaceutical prescriptions. The audit concluded that the government's management is ineffective and made several recommendations, including transferring pharmaceutical benefit funding to general grants for regions, clarifying oversight responsibilities, and improving the effectiveness of regulatory bodies. The government mostly agrees with the findings and plans to further analyze and implement necessary measures.

title: Minska rånrisk genom uppgifter på söksajter
summary: The government proposes the introduction of a new law governing state grants to religious communities, which includes criteria for eligibility, revisions to existing legislation, and the establishment of democratic conditions for funding. These changes aim to ensure that support is given to communities that respect democratic values while expanding the definition of eligible religious organizations beyond the Church of Sweden.

title: Delning av aska efter avliden
summary: The government proposes to extend the use of preventive coercive measures in law enforcement to better prevent and avert serious crimes. The proposal includes allowing the collection of information on electronic communications for more types of crimes, increasing the range of coercive measures available, such as secret room surveillance, and enabling remote searches in cases involving foreign nationals with qualified security aspects. The aim is to enhance the capabilities of law enforcement agencies while balancing the protection of individual rights through stronger safeguards against surveillance.

title: Utvisning på grund av brott
summary: The government proposes a new law aimed at implementing the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), which comes into effect on June 30, 2024. The law designates the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority (Finansinspektionen) as the competent authority responsible for overseeing applications and notifications related to cryptocurrency market operations. The proposal also includes a requirement for individuals at the Riksbank to report sales of financial instruments, in addition to existing reporting obligations for acquisitions.

title: Sänkt straffmyndighetsålder
summary: The motion proposes a series of measures to enhance the security of residential areas, including evaluating the broadened possibilities for the forfeiture of rental rights, protecting minors from losing their homes, strengthening legal protections for women experiencing violence, and ensuring that the needs of children in such situations are prioritized. It also calls for a control mechanism to assess the implications of new legislation two years after its implementation, along with a request for additional resources for state agencies and municipalities to manage the consequences of these legislative changes.

title: Grovt drogfylleri vid framförande av tung lastbil
summary: The motion presented by the Sweden Democrats (SD) aims to enhance cooperation among Nordic countries by addressing various issues, including the establishment of a Nordic advisory council, harmonization of corporate law and taxes, promotion of Nordic languages and cultures in education, environmental protection, and support for a unified Nordic energy policy. The motion emphasizes the need for a higher ambition level in addressing barriers to cross-border trade and employment, fosters a deeper cultural exchange, and calls for strategic initiatives to make the Nordic region the most integrated and sustainable.

title: Differentiera vapenlagen
summary: The motion proposes that the effects of stricter laws concerning hate speech against groups be evaluated five years post-implementation. It argues that while the government's proposed changes aim to strengthen legislation against hate speech related to genocide and war crimes, there are concerns regarding potential infringements on freedom of speech and the risk of unintended consequences. Various institutions have criticized the proposal, suggesting it may hinder discussions about historical events and may extend the scope of punishable offenses in ways not intended by the government.

title: Renodla statistiken för jaktbrott
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1408 av Åsa Coenraads och John Widegren (båda M)
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament supports the establishment of a proactive action plan for climate preparedness, emphasizing the necessity for clearer legislation, better coordination among authorities, increased investments, and solutions that prioritize public needs rather than tax cuts. Key components of the proposal include ensuring a secure drinking water supply, enhancing environmental monitoring, creating a national coordination function for effective climate adaptation, and instituting a preparedness general to oversee crisis management at various governmental levels.

title: Polisnärvaro på Östergötlands landsbygd
summary: Miljöpartiet proposes that the Swedish parliament reject portions of a proposition related to citizenship laws, advocating for reforms that would safeguard the citizenship process for those with a criminal record by considering the seriousness of the offense rather than the type of crime. The party emphasizes the importance of protecting children's citizenship and preventing arbitrary denials based on insufficient grounds, particularly for those in vulnerable situations. Furthermore, they propose that citizenship applications be put on hold if the individual is under reasonable suspicion of a crime until a final judgment is made.

title: Offentlig verksamhet bör anställa fler med funktionsvariationer
summary: The motion advocates for the Swedish government to develop a proactive national strategy for climate adaptation, including concrete proposals for decision-making. It emphasizes the need for increased governmental ambitions, long-term funding for climate adaptation projects, establishment of a parliamentary group to ensure consistency, and comprehensive plans for both local and national initiatives to address climate-related risks. It also highlights the importance of collaboration between public and private sectors, as well as education for relevant authorities and healthcare personnel regarding climate risks.

title: Flexibla avloppslösningar på landsbygden
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1405 av Sten Bergheden och Marléne Lund Kopparklint (båda M)
summary: The motion MP035 by the Green Party (MP) calls for the rejection of the government's energy policy proposal, emphasizing the need for concrete planning goals for 2030 and 2035. It advocates for a transition to a fully fossil-free energy system by 2035, enhancement of green baseload power, and improved energy storage capabilities. The motion also proposes financial support for local communities and residents affected by energy projects, a national strategy for energy storage, and a commitment to sustainable biofuel production in Sweden by 2030, amid criticism of the government's long-term energy planning efforts.

title: Kunskap om hörselnedsättning inom äldreomsorgen
summary: The proposal suggests rejecting the government's proposition to temporarily raise the ceiling for the tax deductions on home renovations (rotavdrag) and household services (rutavdrag), which are expected to favor high-income households disproportionately. The Green Party argues that instead of increasing these tax deductions, support should focus on energy efficiency and sustainable practices in construction, especially in rapidly growing municipalities. The party advocates for a fundamental reform of the rotavdrag system to promote resource sustainability and efficiency.

title: Nytt arbetssätt för mobila kranar
summary: The motion calls for the Swedish Parliament to reject the government's proposed planning and delivery security goals for the electricity system, advocating instead for the establishment of clearer and more ambitious targets for fossil-free energy by 2030. The authors emphasize the need for a broad political consensus on energy policy to ensure competitiveness, energy security, and to meet future electricity demands. It contends that without immediate and concrete measures, the long-term goals set for 2045 may not be achievable, potentially hampering both industrial investment and climate objectives.

title: Förvaring av ammunition
summary: This motion proposes that the Swedish government should prioritize the use of land-efficient technology when establishing regulations for electricity grid development. The Center Party argues that clearer criteria are needed for permit processes to avoid arbitrary decisions and to enhance local and regional coordination in planning. It suggests reviewing compensation for land intrusions to reflect true losses, advocating for alternatives to new infrastructure construction, and emphasizing a transition to more sustainable practices in electricity network expansion.

title: Stoppa innehav av potentiella brottsverktyg på särskilda ungdomshem
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1401 av Marléne Lund Kopparklint och Sofia Westergren (båda M)
summary: This motion proposes that the Swedish government ensure adequate financing for climate adaptation measures needed to protect critical infrastructure and services from the impacts of climate change. It emphasizes that while reducing emissions remains a priority, proactive preparations for a changing climate, such as enhancing buildings and infrastructure to withstand extreme weather and rising sea levels, are essential. The Center Party argues for increased financial support, noting that current government funding covers only a fraction of the estimated costs required for effective climate adaptation.

title: Barns rättigheter och skyldigheter
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1400 av Betty Malmberg och Marléne Lund Kopparklint (båda M)
summary: The proposal advocates for continuous evaluation of new legislation aimed at enhancing the protection of police employees against threats and violence, while also emphasizing the need for proper documentation in governmental procedures to ensure accountability and public transparency. Concerns are raised regarding the inadequacy of preparation and the brief consultation period for this legislative initiative, which could potentially affect the quality of policymaking and the safety of other vulnerable professional groups.

title: Medicinsk rådgivning till försäkringsbolag
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1399 av Marléne Lund Kopparklint och Sten Bergheden (båda M)
summary: The proposal from the Green Party calls for the Swedish government to adopt a comprehensive and social preventive strategy against crime that emphasizes the need for a functional welfare system, trust in societal institutions, and significant resources for integration. It critiques the current governmental approach, particularly regarding the impact of the Tidö Agreement on crime prevention and societal security, advocating for a focus on early intervention and support for families to prevent children from turning to crime. The motion highlights the need for adequate funding for education and social services as essential to combating crime effectively.

title: Upphandla utifrån funktion
summary: The Left Party, represented by Gudrun Nordborg and others, proposes that the Swedish Parliament reject the government's proposition 2023/24:102 which aims to strengthen protection for certain police employees against organized crime. The party emphasizes the need for better protection for public employees, such as police officers, who face violence, threats, and harassment, while also maintaining demands for legal security and accountability. They argue that the government's proposal should be coordinated with other ongoing legislative suggestions related to stronger protections for public employees, as recommended by the Council on Legislation.

title: Bankkonton för barn och ungdomar
summary: The motion proposed by Tony Haddou and others from the Left Party opposes the government's proposal to implement stricter requirements for obtaining Swedish citizenship through notification, particularly disqualifying individuals with certain criminal records or suspicions of criminal activity. The Left Party argues that these measures disproportionately affect children and young adults and may violate principles of justice and integration. They advocate for the preservation of easier access to citizenship as a means of promoting social inclusion and integration into Swedish society.

title: Stärkt rättssäkerhet
summary: The Left Party proposes that the Swedish Parliament reject the government's proposition to temporarily increase the ROT deduction cap to 75,000 SEK and to abolish the joint cap for ROT and RUT deductions. They argue that while ROT deductions can be justified as a counter-cyclical measure in the current failing construction market, the proposed increase disproportionately benefits higher-income earners and does not effectively combat the use of black wages in the construction sector, as highlighted by the Swedish National Audit Office.

title: Fullgod kontanthantering i hela landet
summary: Vänsterpartiet proposes to reject the government's energy policy proposition 2023/24:105, arguing that it lacks clear, quantifiable goals for increasing electricity production, particularly in terms of targets for 2030. The party criticizes the government's focus on nuclear energy without addressing the rising costs associated with it, and urges for significant investments in renewable energy sources like wind and solar power. Vänsterpartiet emphasizes the need for a more robust public control over the electricity system, asserting that energy production should be viewed as critical infrastructure and that the existing market model is inadequate for ensuring energy security and affordability. They advocate for a shift towards a 100% renewable energy system, alongside measures to improve public acceptance of wind energy projects.

title: Vapenskåp hos privatpersoner
summary: The proposal suggests that the Swedish Parliament reject certain parts of the government's bill 2023/24:108, which aims to enhance law enforcement's ability to use covert means to locate wanted individuals. Specifically, it opposes the use of secret surveillance on communication devices not belonging to the sought individuals, the use of covert measures against those subject to specific registration obligations without any allegations or convictions, and the unrestricted use of information obtained from secret surveillance for purposes other than those intended. The proposal emphasizes the importance of maintaining strict limitations on the use of coercive measures to protect fundamental rights and democratic principles.

title: Förvaring av vapen i annans vapenskåp
summary: The proposal addresses the inefficiencies and potential for abuse in subsidized employment programs, particularly focusing on the nystartsjobb (start-up jobs). It calls for the government to revise the structure of these jobs and to involve stakeholders such as labor market parties and regional centers against labor-related crime in verifying the suitability of workplaces for employing subsidized workers. The motion highlights the serious issues identified by the Swedish National Audit Office regarding the effectiveness of current controls and the substantial financial losses stemming from incorrect payments, suggesting that the current regulations facilitate misuse.

title: Avskaffa skatten på RUT-tjänster för seniorer
summary: The motion proposes measures to enhance the control of subsidized employment for workers, specifically targeting the regulation of companies without collective agreements and the review of the system for reclaiming incorrectly paid wage support. Additionally, it advocates for the reintroduction of state support for union consultations, arguing that current governmental measures are insufficient to combat fraud related to newly started jobs and labor market crime. The proposal aligns with recommendations from the National Audit Office and critiques the government's cuts in labor market policies, emphasizing the need for adequate administrative resources for effective oversight.

title: Trängselskattens påminnelseavgift
summary: The proposal contends that the government's intention to abolish high-cost protection for sick leave costs will disproportionately affect small businesses, making it difficult for them to manage expenses related to employee sick leave. It suggests that instead of removing this support, the government should implement better controls to prevent improper payments. The motion argues that the repeal of such protection will deter small businesses from hiring individuals with medical histories or disabilities, ultimately hindering job creation.

title: Ökning av reseavdraget för arbetspendling med bil
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish government take actions in line with the recommendations from the National Audit Office regarding subsidized employment, emphasizing the need for improved controls to prevent misuse and irregularities. It highlights issues of exploitation in the current system, particularly affecting long-term unemployed individuals and those with disabilities, and calls for a review of the procedures and transparency of the subsidized employment process, including the need for better collaboration with trade unions.

title: Ta bort eller minska reavinstbeskattningen vid bostadsflytt
summary: The Left Party, led by Isabell Mixter, proposes that the Swedish Parliament reject the government's proposal to discontinue compensation for high sickness salary costs, citing significant criticism from various stakeholders. They argue that ending this compensation could exacerbate discrimination in the labor market against individuals prone to sick leave and call for a more comprehensive approach to improve employer incentives to reduce absenteeism, rather than merely addressing high sickness costs.

title: Uppmuntra privat pensionssparande genom skattesystemet
summary: The Swedish government presents its response to the National Audit Office's report on the state's management of land intrusions, citing that while the handling is largely uniform and efficient, discrepancies exist in how authorities treat property owners and determine compensation. The government agrees with the audit's observations and emphasizes the need for a more consistent approach to compensation across different areas. However, it does not see a need for further actions beyond ongoing assessments.

title: Ett mer transparent och effektivt skattesystem
summary: The motion emphasizes the need for comprehensive reforms in the handling of electronic communications and visitation rules at special youth homes (Sis-institutioner), advocating for continuous monitoring of the reforms, the possibility of exceptions for individual cases, and the inclusion of children's rights representatives in oversight processes. It expresses concerns about the swift implementation of the proposed changes and calls for adequate time for effective execution, highlighting the importance of child rights and ensuring proper preventive care for youth involved with the justice system.

title: Översyn av personalliggaren
summary: The motion proposes that the government evaluate current legislation regarding the treatment of youth in state institutions, particularly in relation to electronic communication. It advocates for stronger oversight mechanisms and the establishment of regular reviews of individual placement decisions and their legal safeguards, to ensure that limitations on communication do not infringe upon the rights of the youths placed in these facilities. The motion emphasizes the need for well-informed and proportionate actions to minimize risks associated with youth criminality and ensure the safety and well-being of both the youths and staff.

title: Borttagen flygskatt och flygets roll för sysselsättning och företagande
summary: The government proposes measures to enhance security in residential areas by expanding landlords' rights to terminate rental agreements for tenants who commit crimes that negatively affect the neighborhood. The suggestions include clarifying tenants' responsibilities for ensuring that persons in their property do not create insecurity, as well as stricter controls on the use of rental units. The proposal also aims to provide stronger protections for tenants who are victims of domestic violence, allowing them to retain their lease under certain conditions. These changes are intended to strengthen the legal framework surrounding rental agreements and improve overall safety in housing communities.

title: Dags att sänka bensin- och dieselskatten
summary: This motion proposes that the Swedish government advocate for various measures in the EU, including appointing a special representative for Ukraine to promote peace and stability, ensuring Turkey ratifies the Istanbul Convention, enforcing binding climate goals, preventing ecological crimes, and reforming EU market structures while prioritizing human rights and democratic values in EU foreign relations.

title: Sänkt skatt på diesel
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament should reject the government's proposal to abolish the current system of compensation for high sick leave costs. The motion emphasizes the importance of developing this system rather than terminating it, highlighting concerns about the potential negative impact on small employers and the risk of increased discrimination in the labor market. It calls for the government to enhance cooperation between relevant authorities and improve the system to reduce the risk of incorrect payments.

title: Fartkontroller
summary: The motion by Maj Karlsson and others from the Left Party proposes several amendments to the government’s propositions regarding the placement and treatment of young people in secure care. It emphasizes that only those convicted of serious offenses should be placed in high-security facilities, while others should be accommodated in lower-security settings to better meet their specific care needs. Furthermore, it advocates for separating male and female youth in various settings to protect vulnerable groups, ensuring regular reviews of placement decisions, and allowing access to electronic communication services under specific conditions. The motion aims to prioritize the well-being and rights of children in state care, especially regarding safety and rehabilitation measures.

title: Slopa indexuppräkningen av bensin- och dieselskatten
summary: The proposal from Ulrika Liljeberg and others (C) calls for the Swedish parliament to reject the government's suggestion to introduce 'security zones' that would provide police with increased powers to search individuals and vehicles. The suggestion raises concerns about significant infringements on personal privacy and potential discrimination against certain groups, particularly ethnic minorities. Critics argue that the government's proposal, which lacks a clear demonstration of effectiveness in preventing crime, has been hastily prepared without adequate deliberation and infringes upon fundamental rights. The Center Party advocates for solutions that have proven efficacy instead of measures that compromise individual freedoms and rights.

title: Förebygg dödsfall och sjukdomar bland äldre under sommarhalvåret
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1380 av Marléne Lund Kopparklint och Betty Malmberg (båda M)
summary: The proposal from the Green Party (Miljöpartiet) urges the Swedish parliament to reject the government's bill on security zones due to concerns about increased discrimination and ineffectiveness in reducing crime. The motion calls for stricter requirements for establishing security zones, limits on their size and duration, protections for children facing intervention, and improved documentation and evaluation practices by the police to mitigate issues of ethnic profiling and to ensure adherence to democratic values.

title: Lantbrukets produktionsskatter
summary: The motion proposes amendments to the existing policing regulations, particularly regarding body searches and the introduction of a receipt system for individuals who are searched. It argues against the government's proposition to create specific visitation zones, claiming that such an approach may lead to increased distrust between the police and the community, could result in discrimination, and is ultimately ineffective in addressing gang-related violence. The motion calls for a clearer legislative framework for police actions and for regular evaluations of the effectiveness of any introduced laws.

title: Vite då förlossningsvård inte kan erbjudas
summary: The proposal suggests changes to laws governing the care of young people in special youth homes in Sweden, aiming to enhance security and differentiate between various types of homes based on the risk level of the residents. It endorses limited use of electronic communication tools for youths in secure facilities to eliminate destructive contacts and advocates a ban on solo work by staff during client interactions to ensure both employee and youth safety. The Social Democrats support these reforms as a continuation of previously initiated efforts.

title: Bortforsling av fordon
summary: The proposal aims to enhance the capacity of law enforcement agencies to locate individuals who are evading investigation, prosecution, or sentencing, particularly focusing on violent offenders or those likely to reoffend. It introduces measures such as the use of secret coercive measures to locate individuals avoiding legal action, extends capabilities to monitor foreigners who fail to comply with legal registration obligations, and proposes changes to ensure legal protections for individuals subject to such covert actions. The changes are designed to enable quicker and more effective enforcement of sentences beginning July 1, 2024.

title: Nedmontering av kopparnätet
summary: The government's proposal aims to amend the Swedish Citizenship Act to strengthen the significance of citizenship through stricter acquisition requirements. Applicants for citizenship by notification must demonstrate good conduct and respect for society, with disqualifications for those suspected or convicted of serious crimes, threats to national security, or connections to specific groups or organizations. The proposal also includes provisions to protect vulnerable individuals from being coerced into renouncing their citizenship, stipulating that all applications must be processed by a designated authority, with the changes set to take effect on October 1, 2024.

title: Kriterier för vinterdäck
summary: The Swedish government's proposition outlines a long-term direction for energy policy, emphasizing the need for an increase in electricity production capacity to meet the expected surge in electricity demand due to electrification in industries and the transport sector. The proposal aims to ensure a secure and cost-effective energy supply while facilitating the green transition and achieving climate goals. It sets planning and delivery security objectives for the Swedish electricity system, stresses the removal of unnecessary barriers to create an efficient market, and suggests a reassessment of current energy efficiency targets. The initiative is supported by a coalition of center-right political parties.

title: Individanpassade måltider
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1374 av Ann-Charlotte Hammar Johnsson m.fl. (M)
summary: The government presents a report to the parliament detailing the activities of the committees established by government decisions throughout 2023, including various investigations and evaluations across multiple sectors.

title: Mobiltäckning i hela landet
summary: The government proposes to strengthen the protection for police employees working against organized crime, who are often subjected to violence, threats, harassment, and undue influence. The proposal includes allowing police officers to use alternative identifiers instead of their names in official documents when there is a significant risk to their safety. It also seeks to establish confidentiality around information that could reveal the identity of these police personnel. This is aimed at ensuring the effectiveness of the police in crime prevention and enforcement.

title: Slopa plastpåseskatten
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1372 av Betty Malmberg och Marléne Lund Kopparklint (båda M)
summary: The Swedish government has presented a revised national strategy and action plan for climate adaptation for the next five years, outlining the direction for national efforts in climate resilience. The strategy emphasizes the importance of implementing effective measures to reduce vulnerability to climate change impacts, establishing clear goals, and coordinating responsibilities across various stakeholders. It also aims to enhance synergies with disaster risk prevention, emergency preparedness, and food security, ensuring that Sweden is resistant to climate changes and can leverage potential opportunities arising from these changes.

title: Receptfritt melatonin
summary: The proposal seeks the Swedish Parliament's approval of the Samoa Agreement, which establishes a partnership between the European Union, its member states, and members of the Organization of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS). The Samoa Agreement, which will govern the relationship for at least 20 years, emphasizes shared principles and defines priority areas for cooperation, such as human rights, democracy, sustainable development, and climate change, aiming to strengthen the capability of both parties to address global challenges collectively.

title: Stöd till ökad vaccination mot TBE
summary: The Swedish government's report outlines the activities and developments within the Council of Europe during the latter half of 2022 and the full year of 2023. It highlights ongoing challenges including human rights violations, democratic backsliding, and the impacts of geopolitical tensions, particularly due to the war in Ukraine. The report discusses various initiatives taken at the Council, including the adoption of the Reykjavik Principles for Democracy, the establishment of a register for damages caused by Russian aggression against Ukraine, and efforts related to the EU's accession to the European Convention on Human Rights. Emphasis is also placed on the importance of continued work in human rights and democratic governance amidst increasing political polarization and inequality.

title: Sjukdomen endometrios
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1369 av Ann-Charlotte Hammar Johnsson m.fl. (M)
summary: The government's proposition aims to clarify and expand the existing legal provisions against hate speech targeting specific groups in Sweden, particularly with regard to Holocaust denial and similar atrocities. It proposes explicit criminalization of Holocaust denial, extends the application of existing laws to include incitement to violence, and grants individuals from protected groups the status of victims with rights to compensation. The changes are set to come into effect on specific dates in 2024 and 2027.

title: Gårdsförsäljning i Västmanland
summary: The government proposes changes to the Sametinget election law to clarify the regulations regarding the election process. The amendments include clearer rules for registration and notification for candidates, protections for party designations similar to those in general elections, and specifications on voting procedures, polling stations, ballot counting, and seat allocation. Additionally, changes to the handling of personal data in the context of elections are suggested, aiming to enhance the integrity and transparency of the electoral process. The proposed changes are set to take effect on August 1, 2024.

title: Översyn av reavinstbeskattningen vid flytt och av bostadspolitiken i allmänhet
summary: The government proposes compensation for individuals born in 1957 due to an increased age limit for a higher basic deduction in tax law. The suggested legislation aims to make this compensation tax-free and outlines the administrative procedures involved. Additionally, it proposes delaying the implementation of the higher age limit from January 1, 2026, to January 1, 2027, allowing affected individuals more time before the new age criteria apply.

title: Slopad mängdrabatt vid upprepade återfall i brottslighet
summary: The Swedish government presents an overview of the Nordic cooperation conducted in 2023, focusing on the activities of the Nordic Council of Ministers. Emphasizing the importance of collaboration in the Nordic region and with the Baltics, the report highlights key areas such as security, integration, and sustainable development amid geopolitical challenges, particularly in light of Russia's aggression towards Ukraine. As chair of the Nordic Council of Ministers in 2024, Sweden aims to promote a safer, greener, and more integrated Nordic region, with notable projects and initiatives planned for the year.

title: REP- och ROST-avdrag
summary: The proposal aims to streamline and clarify the permit process for renewing, upgrading, and constructing electricity networks in Sweden. It includes legislation to modify the assessment criteria for high-voltage power lines, allowing only specific factors to be considered in the suitability evaluation within the permit process. Additionally, it proposes an exemption from certain environmental protections for the construction and maintenance of these power lines, effective from July 1, 2024.

title: Kraftfulla åtgärder mot organiserade bilstölder och bildelsstölder
summary: The government proposes a temporary increase in the tax deduction ceiling for 'rotavdrag' (a tax reduction for renovation work) and introduces separate limits for 'rutavdrag' (a tax reduction for household services) for the year 2024. The ceiling for 'rotavdrag' will be set at 75,000 SEK per person, while the combined limit for both deductions will be 75,000 SEK, with a separate maximum of 50,000 SEK for 'rotavdrag' until June 30, 2024. This proposition aims to stimulate employment in the construction sector during a period of economic downturn in Sweden.

title: Dags för gårdsförsäljning
summary: The government proposes a new law to establish obligations for state agencies, municipalities, and unemployment funds to share information to prevent incorrect payments from welfare systems, as well as to combat fraud, regulatory violations, and criminal activity in the labor market. This legislation aims to enhance cooperation among various authorities to ensure accurate decision-making and execution of controls in the workforce, ultimately improving the integrity of welfare disbursements. The law is set to come into effect on July 1, 2024.

title: En fast vårdkontakt
summary: The Swedish government has submitted a report to the parliament detailing the actions taken in response to previous parliamentary requests during the year 2023. The report covers various departmental activities and includes current statistics on the legislative framework. It aims to provide parliament with a comprehensive overview of how the government has addressed issues raised in past communications, ensuring transparency and accountability in governance.

title: Hälso- och sjukvårdens beredskap i krislägen
summary: The motion submitted by Gudrun Nordborg and others from the Left Party expresses opposition to the government's proposal for establishing safety zones, arguing that existing laws provide sufficient authority for police to conduct searches and that the proposed changes could lead to discrimination and stigmatization of vulnerable communities. The Left Party advocates for alternative measures that prioritize social welfare and preventive actions to combat gang violence and crime, including improved community resources and preventive strategies rather than increased police powers.

title: Systematiskt arbete mot antibiotikaresistens
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1360 av Betty Malmberg och Marléne Lund Kopparklint (båda M)
summary: The Swedish government's strategy focuses on a comprehensive approach to prevent crime, particularly targeting the recruitment of individuals into criminal networks and the involvement of youth in criminal activities. It emphasizes enhancing societal safety through stronger support for parenting, increased opportunities for youth engagement, and systematic interventions aimed at reducing criminality among vulnerable groups. The strategy advocates collaboration among various societal actors, including government agencies, municipalities, businesses, and civil society, to create a safer environment for all citizens.

title: Omstarta nollvisionen för självmord
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1359 av Betty Malmberg och Marléne Lund Kopparklint (båda M)
summary: The proposal suggests that the Swedish government should ensure sustainable funding for various activities, such as horse sports, amidst an increase in the gaming tax from 18% to 22%. It advocates for a review of the gaming tax structure to differentiate the effective tax rates for different types of gambling, aiming to discourage problem gambling while promoting healthy and enjoyable gaming practices.

title: Läkemedelstillverkning och miljö
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1358 av Betty Malmberg och Marléne Lund Kopparklint (båda M)
summary: The proposal emphasizes the need for the government to ensure adequate funding for municipalities to promote equality in education and to reassess the possibilities of distance education. It calls for a thorough revision of the proposed changes to facilitate their implementation in schools, highlighting the challenges faced by high-performing students and the discrepancies in educational opportunities based on municipal resources. The motion also stresses the importance of flexible regulations for distance education and requests more time for the implementation of these reforms to ensure quality education for all students.

title: Unga kriminella
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1357 av Ann-Charlotte Hammar Johnsson och Elisabeth Björnsdotter Rahm (båda M)
summary: The motion from Åsa Westlund and others argues against the proposed introduction of national recruitment elite programs at the primary and secondary school levels, citing concerns of increased marketization and profit-driven motives in Swedish education. It emphasizes the need to provide all students, regardless of their background, the opportunity to advance at a faster pace and higher level, while calling for thorough evaluations and clearer definitions regarding the target group for these programs. The proposal also highlights the importance of adequate funding and organization of resources in schools to ensure proper support and challenge for all students.

title: Ta bort momsen på körkort och inför ett RATT-avdrag
summary: The proposal seeks to expand the age limit for travel bans on children up to 20 years old, enhance support for children who have been abducted, and ensure adequate resources for the implementation of the legislation. It highlights the necessity to strengthen children's rights by protecting them from harmful international situations, such as forced marriages and female genital mutilation. The motion emphasizes the need for better support structures for children taken abroad and calls for legislative changes to prevent children from losing their Swedish citizenship. Additionally, it advocates for improved resources and training for social services to effectively address these issues.

title: Översyn av ränteavdraget för bolån
summary: The motion emphasizes the importance of equitable funding for Sweden's education system to ensure that all students, regardless of their background, have access to quality education. It stresses the need for a systematic evaluation of the government's proposed reforms aimed at improving educational outcomes and providing appropriate resources for diverse student needs, including gifted students. The motion highlights the disparities faced by students in different regions and socioeconomic situations and calls for the government to prioritize equal educational opportunities for all.

title: Undantag i kemikalieskatten för begagnade produkter
summary: The motion aims to amend the existing law regarding travel bans for minors to explicitly include the risk of female genital mutilation (könsstympning) as a reason for such bans. The proposal criticizes the government's recent changes, which removed explicit mention of this issue, arguing that it may weaken protections against this form of violence. The Social Democrats propose that the reference to genital mutilation should be reinstated to ensure its recognition in legal proceedings related to child protection.

title: Rymdturism - en möjlighet för Sverige
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1353 av Betty Malmberg och Ann-Charlotte Hammar Johnsson (båda M)
summary: The Swedish government has submitted a proposal to extend temporary protection to additional categories of displaced persons, notably Ukrainian nationals and others legally present in Sweden before December 22, 2023, in response to the ongoing humanitarian crisis resulting from Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The proposal includes exceptions for individuals convicted of serious crimes, while aiming to facilitate support for those who may not be able to return to Ukraine safely.

title: God kompetens och kunskap om adhd och dyslexi hos våra lärare och pedagoger
summary: The Swedish government proposes participation in the European Public Prosecutor's Office (EPPO), an EU authority responsible for investigating and prosecuting crimes that harm the financial interests of the EU. The proposal includes a new law to facilitate Sweden's involvement in EPPO and amendments to several existing laws, ensuring Swedish prosecutors can effectively execute their roles within this European structure. The proposed legislation aims to strengthen the fight against corruption and fraud involving EU funds.

title: Undersköterska som legitimationsyrke
summary: The Swedish government proposes to repeal the provisions concerning compensation for high sick pay costs as outlined in the law (1991:1047) on sick pay, effective from the end of June 2024. This repeal is intended to streamline regulations surrounding sick pay and compensation, although older regulations will remain in effect for costs reported through employer declarations up to June 2024.

title: Utveckling av kustnära fiske och vattenbruk
summary: The Swedish government's report addresses the effectiveness of controls surrounding subsidized employment, based on findings from the National Audit Office. The report acknowledges that, despite improvements, the control mechanisms currently in place remain inadequate, presenting risks of abuse, particularly with job creation programs. It outlines necessary measures to mitigate incorrect payments and recommends increased scrutiny and refinement of the administrative processes to enhance efficiency in identifying and managing errors related to subsidized positions.

title: Statens ansvar för sin skog
summary: The proposal aims to amend the investor deduction in the Income Tax Act to comply with updated EU regulations regarding state aid. The change lowers the threshold for the consideration of acquired operations in the evaluation of how long a company has been active, from 25% to 10%. This adjustment seeks to ensure the ongoing legality of the investor deduction under EU law, by adapting Swedish legislation to match the new general group exemption regulation from the EU.

title: Ackreditering av vattentorn
summary: The proposal outlines additional national provisions needed for the implementation of the EU Regulation on the establishment of a carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM). It aims to define the responsible authority, procedures for accreditation, oversight, and the consequences for non-compliance, including penalties. The law is set to come into force on July 1, 2024, facilitating compliance for importers required to declare embedded greenhouse gas emissions and obtain corresponding certificates starting January 1, 2026.

title: Enskilda fastighetsägares rätt över avloppslösningar
summary: The Swedish government proposes a new law to complement the EU's Data Governance Regulation, which includes provisions for the supervision of companies that handle data and provisions for making protected data available for reuse. The law aims to establish a regulatory framework for data sharing and oversight, ensuring compliance with EU standards while implementing additional national measures. It also introduces guidelines for authorities regarding the processing time for access to protected data and enables the government to appoint competent authorities and set fees for access to such data.

title: Krafttag mot oseriös telefonförsäljning
summary: The Swedish government presents a comprehensive overview of the activities undertaken within the European Union during 2023, highlighting developments in various areas such as economic and social cooperation, legal matters, and the EU's institutional framework. The report discusses decisions and events that took place in the EU, emphasizing the breadth of issues addressed by its various council configurations.

title: Ökad kontroll av avloppsvatten för att spåra pandemier
summary: The government proposes to enhance security and safety measures in special youth homes by classifying them into security levels and restricting the use of electronic communication services for certain residents. The proposal includes limiting communication to approved devices and allowing the State Institutions Board (SiS) to impose additional restrictions, including body searches for visitors and background checks on individuals wishing to communicate with or visit residents. These changes aim to ensure a safer environment in these facilities and are set to take effect on May 15, 2024.

title: Både samhället och seniorhushållen vinner på att hisslösa flerbostadshus åtgärdas
summary: The motion suggests that instead of abolishing the compensation system for high sick leave costs, the government should develop it further to minimize the risk of incorrect payments, as highlighted in a recent report by the National Audit Office. The proposal emphasizes the importance of maintaining this system to support small employers, especially in light of recommendations aimed at improving coordination between relevant authorities and reducing errors in compensation processes.

title: Relationerna med Kina
summary: The Swedish government proposes a law allowing the police to establish security zones where they can search for weapons and dangerous objects. This measure aims to combat gun violence and explosions related to conflicts in criminal environments more effectively. The police can designate a security zone in areas at risk of such criminal activity for a maximum of two weeks, and the decision can be appealed in court. Within these zones, police will have extended powers to conduct body searches and search vehicles to prevent or deter criminal activities.

title: Fler talanger till Sverige för forskning, investeringar, företagande och arbete
summary: The government proposes the removal of the requirement for original accounting materials to be preserved in physical form. This means that companies will not need to keep paper records as long as they are digitized, leading to significant time and cost savings. Furthermore, the proposal includes modernizing the regulations concerning 'combined assignments', which would facilitate companies in hiring auditors and utilizing the best technological solutions for their bookkeeping. The changes are slated to come into effect on July 1, 2024.

title: Underrättelser från Försäkringskassan
summary: The proposal seeks to amend the Education Act to enhance opportunities for students in compulsory education, special schools, and Sami schools to study at a higher level and to progress more quickly in their studies. It allows principals to enable students to follow high school curricula under certain conditions, regulate the presence of national recruitment advanced education programs, and facilitate the use of distance education and contracting out educational tasks to enhance learning experiences.

title: Rädda skogsbruket
summary: The government proposes increasing the gambling tax from 18% to 22% on the net revenue for each tax period, as part of the 2024 budget strategy. This adjustment aims to enhance public revenue without substantially harming the competitive landscape of licensed gambling operators. The change is set to take effect on July 1, 2024, and has generated mixed reactions from stakeholders, with concerns about potential negative impacts on various sectors of the gambling market.

title: Minska vargpopulationen i Västmanland
summary: The Swedish government proposes an extension of the existing travel ban for children and young people to protect them from harmful foreign experiences. The proposal allows a travel ban to be issued if there is a significant risk that a child may be taken abroad or leave Sweden, potentially harming their health or development due to abuse, neglect, substance abuse, or criminal behavior. Additionally, the proposal includes expanding the criminal liability for child abduction to cover situations where a child under 15 is taken away to prevent care under the relevant legislation. Proposed changes to confidentiality laws related to the enforcement of this travel ban are also included, aiming for enactment by June 1, 2024.

title: Producera mer växtbaserade livsmedel i Sverige
summary: The government presents a proposal for an extra budget amendment for 2024, primarily in response to the deteriorating security situation in Sweden's neighborhood due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The proposal includes funding for defense equipment and financial support for Ukraine, with measures such as the provision of military materials, educational initiatives, and increased financial commitments for future aid. The government seeks authorization from the parliament to provide military assistance and financial aid totaling up to 3.34 billion Swedish kronor.

title: Ökad brandsäkerhet för braskaminer
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1337 av Marléne Lund Kopparklint och Betty Malmberg (båda M)
summary: The proposal presents changes to road tolls within the Eurovignette cooperation, including an increase and differentiation of tolls based on vehicle emissions categories. It aims to extend toll obligations to additional vehicles and modify vehicle taxes accordingly. The measures are intended to align Sweden with recent EU directives regarding heavy vehicle tolls and improve the environmental impact of transportation by incentivizing lower emissions.

title: Skogsbruk i Skåne
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1336 av Ann-Charlotte Hammar Johnsson m.fl. (M)
summary: The Swedish government has evaluated Riksrevisionen's report on the compensation system for high sick leave costs, concluding that the current design increases the risk of erroneous payments. Riksrevisionen recommends enhanced reporting requirements for employers and greater coordination between Försäkringskassan and Skatteverket to mitigate errors. Despite this, the government plans to abolish the high sick leave cost compensation by June 2024, which it believes will eliminate the cause of erroneous payments and therefore sees no need for further measures.

title: Kortare handläggningstider för miljötillstånd
summary: This parliamentary motion emphasizes the need for the national strategy against organized crime in Sweden to adequately address issues such as human trafficking for sexual purposes and fraud against the elderly. It calls for the inclusion of these issues in the government’s strategy and highlights the importance of protecting vulnerable groups and ensuring that measures taken do not adversely affect civil society organizations. The motion advocates for a comprehensive approach to combat organized crime while stressing that any proposed actions should be carefully evaluated for their impact.

title: Vägmärke för plötsligt kommande dold nedförsbacke
summary: This parliamentary motion by the Green Party (Miljöpartiet) outlines several proposals aimed at combating organized crime in Sweden, emphasizing a preventive and rehabilitative approach. Key points include strengthening early interventions for at-risk children, allowing secret coercive measures for serious crimes committed by minors under 15 with appropriate safeguards, and rejecting the outsourcing of prison placements abroad. The motion advocates for preserving individual integrity in investigations, enhancing cooperation among authorities to prevent crime, and ensuring transparency in managing public funds for civil society organizations, while also cautiously exploring the use of AI in law enforcement.

title: Skatteavdrag för att ta buss- och lastbilskörkort
summary: The Swedish government's proposition aims to enhance macroprudential supervision by proposing that the Financial Supervisory Authority (Finansinspektionen) collaborate with the central bank (Riksbanken) on counter-cyclical capital buffer values. This initiative seeks to bolster the stability of the Swedish banking system during critical periods by requiring banks to maintain adequate capital. Additionally, the proposal outlines necessary legislative adjustments to align Swedish law with EU regulations related to the management of financial companies in crisis and cross-border payments in euros. These changes are set to take effect on July 1, 2024.

title: Angående en sömlös vård
summary: The government proposes the introduction of two new laws aimed at implementing changes to EU regulations concerning infrastructure fees and the categorization of heavy vehicles based on their carbon dioxide emissions. The proposed laws include a fee structure for road infrastructure to cover costs associated with environmental impacts such as air pollution and noise, alongside provisions for classifying heavy vehicles according to their carbon emissions. These changes are designed to align with the updated EU Eurovignette Directive and are set to take effect on May 1, 2024, with some provisions occurring earlier.

title: Tydligare redovisning av kommunernas användning av skattepengar
summary: The government presents a proposal for changes to Swedish law to align with recent EU regulations on medical devices and in vitro diagnostic products. The changes involve adjustments to existing laws concerning medical benefits, ethical review of human research, and transparency regarding confidentiality in discussions related to these products. Key provisions include the introduction of fees for exemptions from language requirements and allowing regional authorities to consult with relevant drug and medical benefits agencies during product assessments. These changes are intended to facilitate compliance with updated EU directives effective from May 26, 2024.

title: Kvalitetssäkring av skönhetsoperationer
summary: The Swedish government's national strategy against organized crime aims to strengthen society's resilience and capacity to combat the increasing threat posed by organized crime, which has significantly impacted public safety, trust, and democratic values. The strategy highlights five key areas: preventing criminal careers, reducing access to illegal weapons, dismantling the criminal economy, enhancing resilience against unauthorized influence, and ensuring reliable identities and effective information exchange. This collaborative effort seeks to mobilize all sectors of society to effectively combat organized crime and safeguard individual security and democracy.

title: Ett huvudmannaskap vid missbruksvård
summary: The government's document outlines Sweden's participation and contributions to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in 2023, discussing the IMF's assessments, policy recommendations for economic and financial stability, and the government's priorities related to the global financial landscape. Key points include evaluations of the international economic development, Sweden's economic situation, the IMF's lending activities, and future challenges for the institution as it navigates post-pandemic recovery and geopolitical tensions.

title: Större möjlighet för anhöriga att kunna få hjälpa till och bistå äldre och funktionsnedsatta
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1328 av Sten Bergheden och Marléne Lund Kopparklint (båda M)
summary: The proposal calls for the government to develop a comprehensive climate action plan that includes strategies to significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions throughout its current mandate, align with EU climate goals by 2030, 2040, and 2045, and integrate climate objectives across all political areas. It seeks to establish a national carbon budget, set consumption-based emission targets, and ensure active participation in international climate leadership. Additional provisions include enhancing climate education, promoting circular economy initiatives, increasing funding for green innovations, and implementing supportive measures for renewable energy development.

title: Tandvårdskostnader för asylsökande och tillfälliga besökare
summary: The motion proposes the establishment of a cross-party agreement to enhance Sweden's national strategy against violent extremism and terrorism. It emphasizes the need for additional concrete measures to combat terrorism financing and to prevent the recruitment of children and youth into extremist environments. The proposal calls for more proactive interventions within prisons and youth homes to mitigate radicalization, as well as support for civil society organizations working against radicalization.

title: Äldre och digital teknik
summary: The motion emphasizes that the government's climate action plan lacks concrete measures necessary to achieve the set emission reduction goals for 2030, 2040, and 2045, leading to increased emissions instead of fulfilling previously established climate obligations. It calls for the government to provide detailed forecasts for proposed emission reductions, accelerate the transition to fossil-free energy production, and ensure climate policies create green jobs while promoting sustainable practices in various sectors, including transportation, housing, and waste management.

title: Översyn av expropriationslagen
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1325 av John Widegren och Åsa Coenraads (båda M)
summary: The proposal urges the Swedish government to promptly present a new climate action plan that includes carbon calculations and cost analyses to meet Sweden's climate goals for 2030, 2040, and 2045. It calls for a reduction in fossil fuel subsidies, a national carbon budget, and concrete measures to strengthen the circular economy, arguing that immediate action is crucial to address climate change and maintain Sweden's leadership role in climate policies. The Center Party expresses concerns about the current government's climate strategy, which it sees as ineffective and detrimental to both environmental targets and economic opportunities.

title: En modern och trygg lagstiftning för ställföreträdare och huvudman
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1324 av Ann-Charlotte Hammar Johnsson m.fl. (M)
summary: The motion aims to address climate change by urging the Swedish government to implement specific measures for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Key proposals include the establishment of a carbon budget, achieving net-zero emissions by 2035, and prioritizing fossil fuel phase-out, while ensuring fairness in the transition for economically vulnerable groups. The motion emphasizes the necessity for a comprehensive national climate strategy aligned with EU commitments and reiterates the need for a transition council and increased investments in green technology.

title: Falska konkursansökningar
summary: The proposal aims to establish a legal framework for a national telecommunications collaboration group focused on crisis situations and heightened readiness. It mandates certain actors within the telecommunications sector to participate in national defense planning and coordination efforts during peace-time crises. The new regulations are intended to enhance infrastructure resilience and communication during such emergencies, with the proposed laws set to take effect on May 1, 2024.

title: Lätta på strandskyddet
summary: The proposed motion suggests that the Swedish government should enhance the role of the Swedish Health and Social Care Inspectorate (Ivo) in overseeing wait times, improve patient rights in accessing care, and strengthen the patient law to allow for better choice and access to both inpatient and outpatient services nationwide. It also argues against weakening existing care guarantees in primary care and emphasizes the need for clear, measurable goals in government health agreements to ensure effective resource allocation and tackle disparities in healthcare service delivery across regions.

title: Bostadsbyggande som riksintresse
summary: The Center Party opposes the government's proposal for a temporary ban on transporting individuals without valid identity documents to Sweden, arguing that it unnecessarily restricts the right to seek asylum. They highlight that current border police powers are sufficient to handle safety concerns without imposing such a ban, emphasizing the importance of upholding asylum rights and addressing practical challenges related to identifying valid documents. The party criticizes the financial burden on transport companies and raises concerns about the constitutionality and proportionality of the proposed regulations.

title: Prövningstillstånd i förvaltningsdomstolen
summary: The motion proposes measures to strengthen consumer protection and combat criminal activities related to gambling. It emphasizes the need for transparency in public lotteries regarding the allocation of profits and calls for equal regulation across all types of commercial gambling, including the licensing requirements for restaurant casinos. Additionally, it highlights the importance of Sweden ratifying the international convention against match-fixing to enhance efforts against organized crime in gambling. The motion advocates for the review and follow-up of the effectiveness of new legislation in this area.

title: Myndighetsutövande när det kommer till utpekande av privat mark
summary: The Center Party proposes a review of Samhall's mission, operations, and conditions to ensure that unhealthy competition is avoided and to enhance the company's role in developing and supplying competence for the regular labor market. The motion emphasizes that Samhall should focus more on its social mission rather than purely on business efficiency, as the current approach threatens both its target groups and the competitiveness of private enterprises.

title: Överskuldsättningen ökar
summary: The proposal suggests that the Swedish government should follow up on new legislation related to consumer information about fuel consumption and carbon dioxide emissions for new cars, as outlined in a recent EU directive. It highlights the importance of comprehensive consumer information, similar to energy labeling for appliances, to encourage the transition to more efficient vehicles. Additionally, it calls for the inclusion of used cars in the legislation to benefit lower-income households and asserts that more clarity is needed regarding fuel and ownership costs to facilitate informed purchasing decisions.

title: Underlätta för seniorer att flytta genom lindrade bolåneregler
summary: The proposal from the Sweden Democrats calls for the government to assess the public health impacts of new legislation on heated tobacco products and to take action to strengthen Sweden's public health efforts. It also emphasizes the need to monitor potential economic consequences for companies and to prevent an increase in illegal trade linked to the new regulations. The party advocates for maintaining the availability of less harmful alternatives, such as snus and heated tobacco products, to promote better public health outcomes and support Sweden's low smoking rates.

title: Ett fungerande postväsen i hela landet
summary: The proposal advocates for adjustments to tobacco legislation in Sweden, specifically suggesting that the government should adopt more stringent requirements for heated tobacco products, including the need for health warnings and information labels. It emphasizes the importance of preventing youth from becoming addicted to nicotine and highlights concerns over flavored products that might attract new users. The motion also calls for clearer definitions in current laws and urges the government to explore additional measures to curb tobacco and nicotine accessibility among minors.

title: Respekt för djuren
summary: The motion from the Green Party (MP) aims to address the issue of waiting times in healthcare, advocating for an evaluation of the current waiting time guarantee initiative (kömiljarden) and improvements to the healthcare guarantee. The proposal highlights findings from the Swedish National Audit Office, suggesting that existing measures are ineffective and may lead to unintended patient exclusion. The Green Party emphasizes the need for adequate resources in healthcare, criticizing the government's budget cuts and suggesting that increased funding is essential to properly manage waiting times and improve the working conditions of healthcare personnel.

title: Förbättrade arbetsvillkor i yrkestrafiken
summary: Miljöpartiet argues against a proposed legislation that would ban the transport of individuals without valid identity documents to Sweden, citing inadequate preparation and a lack of consultation with relevant civil society organizations and legal authorities. They highlight significant risks to asylum rights and safety concerns for transportation staff, asserting that the proposal could undermine protections outlined in international agreements. They also express the need for clarity regarding valid identity documents and critique the potential human rights implications for children affected by this regulation.

title: Ett transporteffektivt samhälle
summary: The proposal suggests rejecting the government's proposition that aims to equalize conditions for private and public municipal service providers. The motion highlights concerns raised by various stakeholders about unnecessary administrative burdens and limitations on municipal autonomy, asserting that municipal and regional entities already have the responsibility to manage and oversee their services appropriately. Additionally, the proposal advocates for better recognition of non-profit service providers, which are often overlooked in discussions of service delivery.

title: Ökad och förbättrad kollektivtrafik
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament instruct the government to compile statistics on the notification of individuals subjected to secret coercive measures. It emphasizes the need for improved transparency in the use of such measures by police and prosecutors, advocating for a longer notification period of at least ten years for individuals affected.
