The motion underlines the importance of maintaining legal certainty while acknowledging the increase in the use of secret coercive measures, calling for an investigation to reduce exemptions for minor service errors in these cases.

title: Levande skogar
summary: The motion calls for the government to propose measures to reduce administrative costs associated with licensing for public lotteries, arguing that while proposed regulations for the gambling market aim to protect consumers and combat criminal activities, they inadvertently increase costs for non-profit lottery operators, affecting their vital contributions to civil society. The Left Party emphasizes the need for a balanced approach that does not penalize public interest lotteries with regulation designed for profit-driven companies, and seeks reassurance that legislative changes consider the impact on various organizational forms.

title: Upprustning av äldreomsorgen i spåren av covid-19
summary: The motion calls for the Swedish government to assign a suitable authority to quantitatively investigate the effects of the new 'kömiljarden' (waiting times funding) on healthcare waiting lists and any potential displacement effects. The Left Party criticizes the government's handling of waiting times, highlighting that the kömiljarden has not resulted in significant improvements and may instead have negative consequences. The party argues that existing evaluations by the Socialstyrelsen (National Board of Health and Welfare) are insufficient and advocates for a more thorough investigation in light of the findings by the National Audit Office.

title: Gynna kooperativa/arbetstagarägda företag
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1309 av Lorena Delgado Varas m.fl. (V)
summary: This parliamentary motion emphasizes the need for a thorough review of the tasks, operations, and conditions of Samhall, focusing on improving the work environment and influence for employees. It highlights concerns raised by the National Audit Office regarding Samhall's prioritization of business development over employee development. The motion calls on the government to ensure that an investigation includes evaluating the most suitable organizational form for Samhall to fulfill its societal mission effectively, particularly emphasizing the need for meaningful and developing employment for individuals with disabilities.

title: Ökad delaktighet i kulturlivet
summary: Vänsterpartiet argues against the government's proposal to implement uniform standards for targets and guidelines for municipal activities carried out by private operators, claiming that existing legislation allows municipalities and regions sufficient control over their operations. They posit that introducing formal requirements would lead to unnecessary administrative burdens and increased costs without addressing a real need. Several stakeholders, including municipalities and legal experts, concur with this assessment, suggesting that the proposal complicates the oversight of municipal services without providing any significant benefits.

title: Förbättringar i pensionssystemet
summary: The suggestion seeks to reject Proposition 2023/24:52, which proposes equal requirements for municipalities and private entities delivering municipal services. The motion argues that municipalities have a broader welfare responsibility compared to profit-driven private companies, and that imposing similar goals and guidelines on both would impose unnecessary administrative burdens and undermine municipal autonomy, especially during a cost crisis. The authors assert that the government's proposal reflects a broader privatization agenda characteristic of right-leaning administrations.

title: En ny sjukförsäkring
summary: The proposal suggests that the Swedish Parliament should support an investigation into the organizational structure of Samhall, a key player in providing meaningful employment for individuals with disabilities. It emphasizes the need to balance business and human perspectives, particularly regarding the design of compensation for additional costs, promoting a more flexible approach to meet individual needs. The motion highlights the importance of adapting work environments to support both personal and professional development while ensuring employee well-being during transitions of business operations.

title: Barn och vuxna i ekonomiskt utsatta familjer
summary: The proposal advocates for the government to evaluate measures taken in response to the Swedish National Audit Office's report on healthcare wait times, emphasizing the need for significant reforms to improve accessibility and reduce waiting times. The Social Democrats argue that previous measures, including the care guarantee, have been ineffective and call for a shift towards a more robust primary care system along with adequate funding and support for healthcare personnel.

title: Afrikas horn
summary: The Left Party opposes the government's proposal to temporarily ban the transport of individuals without valid identity documents to Sweden, arguing that it infringes upon the right to asylum and places excessive burdens on transport operators, with potential negative impacts on commuters and businesses. The proposal is claimed to be ineffective for law enforcement and inconsistent with EU regulations, with the party asserting that it would undermine Sweden's obligations to provide asylum and hinder those fleeing conflict and disaster.

title: Lagstiftning för att stoppa målvakter
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1303 av Ann-Charlotte Hammar Johnsson m.fl. (M)
summary: The Swedish government has submitted a response to the Riksrevisionen's report on state measures for the development of the electricity system, stating that it agrees with the audit's observations concerning insufficient preparation and implementation of measures impacting the electricity system. The report points out that government decisions have often been inadequately analyzed, lacking sufficient impact assessments, and that there is a need for improved handling of consequences from these decisions. The government acknowledges these shortcomings and emphasizes the necessity for long-term stability in energy policy while addressing the challenges posed by an evolving electricity infrastructure.

title: Utvärdering av promillegränsen på sjön
summary: The motion calls on the government to urgently clarify uncertainties in the law regarding preventive residence bans, particularly in relation to severe violent crime, including shootings and bombings by criminal networks. The Center Party emphasizes the need for effective tools for law enforcement to combat increasing violence and criticizes the government's proposed legislation for lacking clarity and implementation feasibility. It is argued that the law must ensure predictability for both individuals and legal authorities to be efficacious.

title: Förenkla inhemska adoptioner
summary: The motion proposes an evaluation of the legislation concerning preventive residence bans, which allow prosecutors to prohibit individuals from certain public areas if they are believed to promote criminal behavior. The motion emphasizes the need for deeper analysis regarding the impact on children and the protection of civil rights, as several stakeholders have raised concerns about the implications of such bans, particularly related to fairness and children's rights. The motion calls for continuous oversight and a comprehensive evaluation after one year.

title: Personlig skuldsättning
summary: The proposal suggests the introduction of a maximum geographical limitation for preventive residency bans in Sweden, emphasizing the need to consider the best interests of children and ensure individuals under such bans have access to legal assistance. It calls for continuous evaluation of the new law to ensure non-discriminatory application and sufficient protection against discrimination, while stressing the importance of a legislative process that respects individual rights.

title: Förändrat strandskydd
summary: The motion proposed by Gudrun Nordborg and others from the Left Party opposes the government's proposition on preventive residence bans, calling for a time limitation on such bans and advocating for public assistance for individuals subject to them. The motion argues that existing laws are sufficient to address public safety without creating new restrictions, which the Left Party believes may lead to stigmatization and is legally uncertain. The motion emphasizes a need for effective preventive measures against gang crime through societal improvements like enhanced welfare and resources for education and social services, rather than punitive measures that may exacerbate existing issues.

title: Rättssäkerhet kring beräkningar av byggnadshöjder
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1298 av Ann-Charlotte Hammar Johnsson m.fl. (M)
summary: The Swedish government has developed a new comprehensive national strategy to address violent extremism and terrorism, prioritizing actions to strengthen national security through prevention, intervention, protection, and management during and after potential attacks. The strategy acknowledges the increasing complexity of threats, including terrorism, extremist ideologies, and organized crime, and emphasizes the need for a coordinated response from various societal actors to safeguard democracy and public safety.

title: Dags att modernisera arrendelagstiftningen
summary: The government proposes to implement confidentiality measures regarding information related to hunters held by county administrative boards and the Police Authority. The proposed changes aim to prevent the disclosure of data that could facilitate the illegal use of firearms and ammunition. These amendments to the Public Access to Information and Secrecy Act are intended to take effect on April 15, 2024.

title: Förändra bygglovshantering för temporära byggnader
summary: The government presents a report to the parliament summarizing the findings from the follow-up and review of signal intelligence activities within defense intelligence operations conducted in 2022. This report, mandated by the parliament, outlines how the activities are regulated, the oversight mechanisms in place to protect personal integrity, and the annual control performed by the State Inspectorate for Defense Intelligence (Siun) and the Integrity Protection Council at the Defense Radio Agency.

title: Rättssäkerhet för beräkning av byggnadshöjder
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1295 av Ann-Charlotte Hammar Johnsson m.fl. (M)
summary: The Swedish government proposes a new law that would empower it to temporarily prohibit the transport of individuals lacking valid identification documents to Sweden via certain modes of transportation, such as buses, trains, or passenger ships. The law includes provisions for imposing fines on those who violate these restrictions. The government seeks to implement this measure in response to serious threats to public order and internal security arising from increased migration flows. The proposed law is set to take effect on March 1, 2024.

title: Förändrade bullerregler för mer bostadsbyggande
summary: The Swedish government presents its second climate action plan in accordance with the Climate Law, detailing efforts to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2045. The plan outlines specific measures and actions necessary for households and businesses to meet both national and EU climate commitments, as well as the government's intended international climate-related initiatives during its current mandate period. It emphasizes the importance of collaboration between several political parties and the integration of climate goals into a growing economy.

title: Återinförande av revisorsplikten
summary: The Swedish government proposes a new law aimed at preventing criminal activities by introducing a system of preventive bans on individuals from entering designated public areas if they are deemed to promote criminal behavior. This law is intended to enhance public safety, particularly in places like schoolyards and areas around preschools, in response to concerns about violent crimes involving firearms and explosives. Violators of this ban could face prison sentences of up to one year or fines for lesser offenses, with the law expected to come into effect on February 1, 2024.

title: Obligatorisk hemförsäkring i flerfamiljshus
summary: This government proposal (2023/24:55) aims to establish regulations requiring information about fuel consumption and carbon dioxide emissions to be clearly presented when marketing new passenger cars. It seeks to align Swedish law with EU directive 1999/94/EG, ensuring that consumers have access to significant data at the point of sale, fostering informed decision-making. The law is scheduled to come into effect on July 1, 2024.

title: Reseförsäkring som täcker sjuktransport hem till Sverige
summary: The Swedish government proposes a ban on heated tobacco products with characteristic flavors, following the EU directive that prohibits such products and mandates combined health warnings and informative texts. The proposal includes that the government or a designated authority will set regulations on which products are considered to have characteristic flavors, as well as extending oversight responsibilities to local municipalities and health authorities, who may charge fees for their supervision. The changes are set to come into effect on May 1, 2024.

title: Äganderätt och miljöundantag
summary: The Swedish government proposes measures to enhance consumer protection in the gambling sector, including allowing the processing of personal data by license holders to fulfill their duty of care towards players. This aims to prevent excessive gambling by enabling assessments of a player's health and financial status. Additionally, the proposal mandates written agreements for telephone sales of gambling services, making any non-compliant contracts invalid. The proposal also seeks to adjust fines related to anti-money laundering violations by gambling providers, aligning them with violations of gambling laws. If adopted, these changes would come into effect on April 1, 2024.

title: Reformera strandskyddet
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1289 av Maria Stockhaus och Kjell Jansson (båda M)
summary: The government proposes a legislative change that mandates municipalities and regions to establish equivalent requirements for goals and guidelines governing both private providers and their own internal operations regarding municipal matters. This aims to create fair and consistent conditions across all operators by ensuring that the same standards and public oversight apply, regardless of whether the service is provided by the public sector or private entities.

title: Avskaffa reglerna om krav på att varsla vid driftsinskränkning
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1288 av Mattias Karlsson i Luleå (M)
summary: The motion addresses concerns about the implications of lowering the renewable fuel mandate for gasoline and diesel in Sweden, emphasizing the necessity for thorough impact analyses concerning job preservation, public health, and climate goals. It advocates for the government to ensure that any changes to the mandate are supported by adequate assessments of their consequences on green jobs and national preparedness, while pressing for a clear strategy to meet Sweden's climate targets by 2030.

title: Möjligheterna att bygga även i störningsbelastade miljöer
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament supports the reduction obligation as an effective tool for meeting climate goals and calls for a study on a more cost-effective implementation of a unified reduction obligation for gasoline and diesel. It emphasizes the necessity of maintaining and improving current climate policies to significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions, especially in the transport sector, while also addressing the impact of rising fuel prices on vulnerable groups.

title: Behov av proportionalitetsprincip för stridsåtgärder på arbetsmarknaden
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1286 av Mattias Karlsson i Luleå (M)
summary: The proposal suggests that the nuclear waste fee should also provide financial support to non-profit environmental organizations involved in the process of assessing facilities for the management and final disposal of used nuclear fuel. The Green Party advocates for a phase-out of nuclear power in favor of renewable energy and argues that nuclear energy is costly, dangerous, and inadequate for addressing the climate crisis. The motion criticizes the government's recent decision to not include such funding in the nuclear waste fee, emphasizing the importance of public participation and oversight in the nuclear waste management process.

title: Rätten att äga skötesrenar
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1285 av Mattias Karlsson i Luleå (M)
summary: The motion advocates for an increase in compensation for municipalities involved in the management of nuclear waste, proposing that the funding should cover all phases of the evaluation process, including environmental impact assessments. The authors argue that since nuclear waste management is primarily a state responsibility, the financial burden should not fall on individual municipalities, which have to manage costs for extended periods.

title: Minskat strandskydd vid bostadsbyggande
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1284 av Mattias Karlsson i Luleå (M)
summary: The Center Party proposes a series of measures aimed at reforming Sweden's fuel reduction obligation to address the climate crisis, including the abolition of carbon tax on biofuels, a reduction in the reduction obligation fee, and a shift to European diesel standards. They advocate for increased production of biodiesel through agreements that secure pricing, as well as maintaining high blending levels of biofuels for transportation, to meet climate goals while ensuring supply security.

title: Stärk äganderättsprincipen i svensk skogspolitik
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1283 av Mattias Karlsson i Luleå (M)
summary: This government report outlines observations from the Swedish National Audit Office regarding Samhall's performance in fulfilling its societal mission to create meaningful employment for individuals with disabilities. Although Samhall has generated jobs that are in demand, the report points out deficiencies in providing development opportunities for employees. It concludes that both governmental and organizational leadership have overly prioritized business development over employee capabilities. Consequently, the government intends to conduct a thorough review of Samhall’s operations and organizational framework to better align with its societal mission.

title: Renodla kravet på personalliggare i byggverksamhet till ett arbetsgivaransvar
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1282 av Mattias Karlsson i Luleå (M)
summary: The government proposes a new law that mandates authorities and authorized organizations involved in the international adoption of children to provide necessary information to the Adoption Commission for the purpose of mapping and analyzing Sweden's adoption activities. The law aims to enhance transparency in adoption processes while ensuring the confidentiality of individuals' personal and financial information, with proposed confidentiality lasting up to 70 years for certain data.

title: Alternativt organisationsnummer för enskild firma
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1281 av Mattias Karlsson i Luleå (M)
summary: Vänsterpartiet proposes that the Swedish parliament should reject the government's proposal to tighten the repayment obligation for defendants in criminal cases, which aims to double the amount defendants must repay for attorney fees, as they argue it disproportionately burdens low-income individuals and may lead to increased debt and hinder their reintegration into society.

title: Möjlighet till avdragsrätt för friskvård i enskild firma
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1280 av Mattias Karlsson i Luleå (M)
summary: The proposal suggests that the Swedish government should reinstate funding from nuclear waste charges to support non-profit environmental organizations involved in oversight and advocacy regarding the disposal of nuclear waste, in light of the previous Ministry of the Environment's memo advocating for long-term financing. It criticizes the government's decision to eliminate funding, arguing that this undermines civic engagement and democracy, particularly in complex matters like nuclear waste management.

title: Upprätta en nationell handlingsplan för sällsynta diagnoser
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1279 av Mattias Karlsson i Luleå (M)
summary: The Swedish Government's memorandum outlines its evaluation of the National Audit Office's report concerning the management of decommissioned solar panels and wind turbine blades. The government acknowledges the report's findings that indicate inadequate state measures to effectively handle these waste materials, thus hindering recycling and reuse. It commits to clarifying EU legislation on producer responsibility and has tasked the Swedish Energy Agency to explore circular and non-toxic disposal methods. Further actions will be awaited until the Agency submits its findings by March 2024.

title: Förlängning av tiden för tömning av förarkort och digitala skrivare
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1278 av Mattias Karlsson i Luleå (M)
summary: The Swedish government's letter discusses the National Audit Office's report on the state's efforts to reduce waiting times in healthcare and assesses its effectiveness. The report concludes that current measures, including the care guarantee and funding initiatives, have not effectively shortened wait times or ensured equitable healthcare access. The government partially agrees with the audit findings and highlights the necessity for improved monitoring and collaboration among health authorities to enhance service delivery and accessibility.

title: Brott under pågående asylprocess
summary: The government presents a report detailing the usage of secret coercive measures, such as covert surveillance and eavesdropping, during the year 2022. This report includes applications of the Swedish Criminal Procedure Act concerning secret electronic monitoring, camera surveillance, room listening, data overriding, and preventative measures against severe crimes, alongside a review of the Swedish Security Service's usage of secret coercive methods.

title: Fritidspeng
summary: The Swedish government's report (2023/24:45) provides an overview of the implementation of the law regarding special control of certain foreigners from July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2023. It details actions taken against individuals based on suspicions related to terrorism and serious threats to national security, including decisions on deportations and the use of coercive measures. The report highlights trends in international terrorism and Sweden's participation in counter-terrorism efforts, noting that both violent right-wing extremism and violent Islamist extremism pose significant threats within the country.

title: Ta bort förmånsbeskattning av parkeringsplatser i anslutning till arbetsplatser
summary: The proposal suggests amending the current regulations regarding designated authorities under the EU regulation on a shared digital gateway, allowing individual authorities and organizations to identify themselves as competent authorities, rather than the government making these designations. This change aims to simplify the process and reduce administrative burdens as it is set to take effect on July 1, 2024.

title: Återställ förtroendet för vårt skattesystem
summary: The proposal calls for the Swedish government to assign a single authority responsibility for healthcare hygiene and to initiate an investigation into the legal conditions for the collection and handling of healthcare data to improve infection control in light of previous pandemic shortcomings. The Left Party emphasizes the need for stronger national infection control measures and better preparedness for future pandemics, criticizing the government's inadequate response and advocating for a more robust framework for data management and regional support.

title: Långsiktig plan för skattesänkningar
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1273 av Jan Ericson och Lars Beckman (båda M)
summary: The Swedish government proposes to tighten the repayment obligation for individuals convicted of crimes concerning the costs of public defenders. The new legislation suggests that the convicted may be required to repay an amount up to twice the standard legal aid fee, with limited options for reduction unless special circumstances apply. Additionally, if a convicted individual's appeal is discontinued due to their absence from a hearing, they would be liable for the full costs incurred during that appeal. These changes are expected to take effect on March 1, 2024.

title: Redovisning arbetsgivaravgift
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1272 av Jan Ericson och Sten Bergheden (båda M)
summary: The Swedish government's communication addresses the Riksrevisionen's report on the reduction obligation for petrol and diesel, acknowledging that while the obligation can contribute to climate goals, its current implementation is not feasible due to various risks that have not been adequately considered. The government welcomes the findings and intends to develop relevant measures to reduce emissions from the transport sector, including potential changes to the reduction levels for 2024-2030 and a focus on cost-effective methods for achieving climate objectives.

title: Begränsning av försörjningsstöd och bidrag till den som inte är svensk medborgare
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1271 av Jan Ericson och Ellen Juntti (båda M)
summary: The government has proposed a law to introduce a one-year probationary period for drivers holding an AM license, which applies to vehicles such as moped class I and A-tractors, in order to enhance traffic safety. If a driver's AM license is revoked during this period, they will be required to undergo the training process again. The proposed law aims to take effect on June 1, 2024.

title: Avskaffa Trafikverkets möjlighet att förbjuda nya utfarter på landsbygden
summary: Riksrevisionen har granskat förändringarna av inkomstskattereglerna mellan 2011 och 2023 och funnit att regeringens redovisning varit ofullständig och ibland förskönad. Skattesänkningarna på nästan 100 miljarder kronor har skapat förutsättningar för högre sysselsättning och en jämnare inkomstfördelning, men brister i konsekvensanalyser har resulterat i att riksdagen haft otillräckligt underlag för besluten. Riksrevisionen rekommenderar att regeringen förbättrar dessa analyser, särskilt effekterna på sysselsättning och inkomstfördelning, samt utvecklar modeller för att analysera äldres arbetsutbud.

title: Enklare och billigare att ta körkort
summary: The government proposal aims to allow Swedish municipalities to receive compensation from the nuclear waste fund for costs associated with public information regarding the planned and existing final storage of spent nuclear fuel and nuclear waste. This includes funding for municipal efforts related to safety assessments and environmental consultations. The goal is to enhance public oversight and evaluation of the environmental and safety implications of nuclear waste management. The proposed legal changes are planned to take effect on July 1, 2024.

title: Bevarandet av det rörliga kulturarvet
summary: The Green Party (Miljöpartiet) proposes measures to strengthen the rights of women and children in protected housing. The motion urges the government to ensure the operation of women's shelters, evaluate the impact of legislation on profit-driven and non-profit organizations, and delay the implementation date of the new law to January 1, 2025. It emphasizes the unique role of women's shelters, calls for a ban on private profit-driven shelters, requests an extended transition period for compliance with new regulations, and advocates for granting children their own legal representatives in all custody and visitation cases.

title: Avskaffande av statens stöd till genusforskning
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1267 av Jan Ericson och Lars Beckman (båda M)
summary: The proposal from the Green Party seeks to reject the government's initiative to allow the revocation of residence permits based on suspected links to terrorism under the Immigration Act. The Green Party argues that the proposed expansions are legally precarious, highlighting concerns raised by the Council on Legislation regarding the vagueness of 'links to terrorism' and the potential for arbitrary application, thereby undermining legal certainty for those with residence permits in Sweden.

title: Avskaffa Barn- och elevombudet
summary: The proposal from the Centerpartiet seeks to oppose the government's suggested expansion of the ability to revoke residence permits under certain terrorism-related circumstances as outlined in the Swedish Aliens Act. The motion emphasizes the need for precise and legally secure legislation in the fight against terrorism, arguing that the government's approach could lead to legal insecurity for individuals with residence permits in Sweden.

title: Forskning om nästa generations kärnkraft
summary: The proposal by the Center Party advocates for the establishment of national guidelines for the social services' oversight of children in sheltered housing, ensuring transparency in decisions regarding the confidentiality of location and visitation limitations. It calls for government oversight of court implementations, targeted educational initiatives for social service staff, systematic evaluations of reforms, and stable funding for sheltered housing services. The motion emphasizes the need for equality, high-quality services, and robust legal protections for children and adults in vulnerable situations.

title: Förbud mot högt spelande fordon på allmän plats
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1264 av Malin Höglund och Ann-Britt Åsebol (båda M)
summary: The suggestion from the Sweden Democrats advocates for increased governmental oversight and quality assurance for protected housing services that support individuals affected by violence and abuse. It proposes continuous supervision by the Inspectorate for Care and Care (Ivo), as well as a requirement for the government to report on the effectiveness of recently instituted permit requirements for these services. Furthermore, it underscores the need for specialized restrictions on visitation rights for those in protected housing, especially in cases involving domestic violence, aligning with children's rights and safety. Additionally, the proposal emphasizes the importance of guarding these facilities against organized crime.

title: Tillsyn inom servicenäringen
summary: The proposal emphasizes the need for comprehensive reform regarding the rights of children and adults seeking protected housing in light of domestic violence. It advocates for measures to ensure that survivors, particularly women and children, do not risk being placed with offenders. The motion calls for the government to perform a gender power analysis of new laws and guarantees the placement of children with their mothers in protected environments without consent from the other guardian. It also highlights the importance of upholding women's rights and child protection in legislation, against the backdrop of rising risks associated with privatization and profit-motivated actors in this sector.

title: Trafikplikt på Mora flygplats
summary: The Swedish government's report responses to the National Audit Office's review of the national infection control system. The report concludes that while the current system is effective, it requires strengthening to better handle future outbreaks. Recommendations include designating a single authority for infection control, clarifying oversight regulations for regional infection control, and assessing the legal framework for data collection and management related to healthcare. The government agrees with these assessments and outlines actions taken or planned in line with the recommendations.

title: Erkännande av EU:s vapenpass
summary: The Left Party opposes the government's proposal to expand the possibilities for revoking residence permits based on security concerns, arguing that it relies on insufficient evidence and could lead to arbitrary deportations. They express concerns that the proposed changes, allowing for easier revocation of residence permits due to suspected activities related to terrorism or state-sponsored espionage, may undermine personal integrity and legal security for those residing in Sweden.

title: Införande av s.k. declaration of interest för offentligt anställda
summary: The Swedish government proposes to ratify an agreement with Finland and Norway regarding the Foundation for Education in the North Calotte for the period 2024-2027. The foundation aims to enhance the job market, improve Nordic skills and competitiveness, and strengthen cooperation in the northern regions of the three countries. The agreement specifies the foundation's activities, organization, and educational commitments among the countries involved, with a focus on providing support that allows more individuals to complete their studies, particularly assisting those farther from the labor market.

title: Ekologisk odling - ett problem för livsmedelsförsörjningen
summary: The government proposes amendments to Swedish laws concerning the surrender of suspects and convicted individuals under European and Nordic arrest warrants. This is in response to rulings from the EU Court of Justice, which necessitate updates to existing legislation that governs the extradition process, including provisions for courts to evaluate the grounds for refusal and for certain foreign nationals to serve sentences in Sweden. The suggested legal changes aim to align Swedish regulations with evolving EU standards and are set to take effect from March 1, 2024.

title: Miljöbalken och äganderätt
summary: The document outlines the activities of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) during 2022 and the first half of 2023, particularly highlighting the impact of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The report discusses the shift in focus towards holding Russia accountable for violations of OSCE principles and the deterioration of security within the region. It details Sweden's engagement in promoting human rights, democracy, and the rule of law, aligning with its foreign policy goals, as well as Sweden's role within the OSCE leadership as part of a three-member chairmanship. The report emphasizes the need for continued attention to other regional conflicts and issues, even amidst the ongoing crisis in Ukraine.

title: Huvudmannaskapet för länssjukvården/specialistsjukvården
summary: The document outlines Sweden's presidency of the European Union Council during the first half of 2023, detailing the preparations, implementation, and results achieved. It highlights Sweden's leadership in legislative and political work within the EU, maintaining unity among member states amidst challenges such as the war in Ukraine, addressing migration policies, and promoting a green transition. The report also emphasizes the significant decisions made under this presidency, which include support for Ukraine, enhanced security measures, and initiatives for a greener EU.

title: Postutdelning i glesbygd
summary: The proposal seeks to impose stricter penalties for serious weapon crimes, including gun offenses and violations related to explosive materials. The Center Party argues that the government's current proposal for a minimum sentence of four years for particularly severe offenses is insufficient and calls for it to be raised to at least five years. They emphasize the need for a comprehensive approach to combat gang crime, including targeted policing efforts and preventive measures in education and employment.

title: Landsbygden bör prioriteras
summary: The motion proposes the adoption of a supplementary tax law aimed at ensuring that multinational and domestic corporations in Sweden meet a minimum taxation threshold of 15%, in alignment with an EU directive. It emphasizes the need for a review and simplification of the existing legislative text to address concerns about clarity and implementation costs for companies. The Center Party requests that the government expedite this legislative overhaul to prevent undue burdens on taxpayers and ensure compliance with EU requirements.

title: Tydligare färdtjänstregler
summary: The motion advocates for the strengthening of water authorities' powers and calls on the government to propose a redistribution of tasks among them and other relevant agencies to effectively implement the new EU drinking water directive in Sweden. The Center Party believes that current responsibilities are too fragmented and that water authorities should be phased out in favor of a more unified management approach for water governance as outlined in a previous investigation.

title: Ändrade beräkningsgrunder för infrastrukturmedel
summary: The proposal advocates for comprehensive reforms in Swedish water management to align with the new EU drinking water directive. It calls for mandatory actions for municipalities to enhance and expand water supply systems, improve environmental monitoring related to water quality, and establish clearer parameters for potentially harmful chemicals in drinking water. The motion emphasizes the urgent need for resources to protect water sources and ensure maintenance responsibilities for water and sewage systems, addressing the challenges posed by aging infrastructure and environmental contaminants.

title: Entreprenörskap hos unga
summary: The motion proposes a modification to the government's draft law regarding the additional tax for companies in large groups, specifically to clarify the definition of generally accepted accounting standards in Sweden. The aim is to ensure that Swedish accounting standards can qualify as generally accepted, even if they deviate from IFRS, thereby supporting Swedish businesses.

title: Gör utbildningarna mer relevanta för de lokala arbetsmarknaderna
summary: The motion calls for the government to promptly develop a plan for how the Criminal Care Service can fulfill its responsibilities in light of the proposed tougher penalties for serious weapon crimes and the smuggling of explosive materials. It highlights the urgent need for enhanced legislation to tackle the recruitment of minors into serious crimes and emphasizes the importance of a new weapon amnesty for reducing crime rates. The motion also expresses concerns regarding the Criminal Care Service's capacity to handle an expected increase in offenders due to the anticipated changes in law.

title: Stärkt elevhälsa
summary: The proposal calls for an immediate review of the legislation concerning additional taxes on large corporate groups, with an emphasis on enhancing the fairness and legitimacy of the tax system to ensure sufficient public revenue for welfare funding. It emphasizes the need to analyze responsibilities of representatives in companies and the application of accounting standards in relation to the proposed definitions. The proposal underlines the importance of combating tax evasion and ensuring that all companies, regardless of size, are subject to the same tax obligations, while advocating for a comprehensive legislative process that examines the implications for small and medium enterprises.

title: Säkerställ utbildningscentrum för högre utbildning
summary: The Swedish government has introduced a proposal to amend the Aliens Act to enhance national security measures. Key changes include the ability to revoke a foreign passport for security reasons, classify cases by the Security Police that involve refusals or revocations of such passports as security matters, and allow for the revocation of residence permits in cases where it's presumed that the individual may engage in state-sponsored corporate espionage or terrorist activities. The proposed changes are aimed at streamlining the legal framework surrounding security-related immigration matters, and are set to take effect on March 1, 2024.

title: Ersättning till närboende vid vindkraftsetablering
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Government assigns the Chemical Agency and the Medical Products Agency to create and regularly update a national list of hazardous substances and pharmaceutical residues in drinking water, in compliance with EU's new drinking water directive. It also calls for risk assessments related to property installations to specifically include bisphenols and to set limit values for bisphenol A in tap water, aligning with the European Food Safety Authority's recommendations.

title: Stötta svenskt mathantverk
summary: The proposal from the Green Party (MP) opposes the government's initiatives to reduce taxes on gasoline, diesel, and agricultural diesel, arguing that such reductions would exacerbate climate change by increasing emissions. The MP suggests alternative ways to support households, particularly in rural areas, that do not worsen the climate crisis, such as targeted tax cuts and support for public transport and electric vehicles. Additionally, the MP emphasizes the need for sustainable agricultural practices that reduce dependence on fossil fuels and promote self-sufficiency in the food system.

title: Minska Trafikverkets makt över kommunernas planarbete
summary: The proposal argues against the government's proposition to reduce taxes on gasoline and diesel, stating that such reductions would undermine efforts to combat climate change by increasing fossil fuel consumption. The proposal emphasizes the need for enhanced economic support for households amid rising inflation and suggests differentiated road tax strategies for rural and urban areas. It advocates for the phasing out of environmentally harmful subsidies, while increasing support for the agricultural sector to encourage a transition to fossil-free farming and greater self-sufficiency in fuel.

title: Begränsa och precisera riksintressenas areal
summary: The Centre Party proposes rejecting the government's plan to lower taxes on gasoline and diesel while advocating for a special rural fuel deduction to provide direct financial relief to rural residents reliant on cars. They recommend implementing fuel vouchers allowing a 3 SEK per liter reduction for all fuels, including climate-friendly options. Additionally, they support extending the temporary reduction of diesel taxes for agriculture while calling for a permanent, technology-neutral agricultural fuel deduction from 2025 to ensure equitable treatment of all fuel types used in the sector.

title: Ändra expropriationslagen
summary: The suggestion emphasizes the need for improved collaboration between Sweden's national cybersecurity center and the private sector, as highlighted by the Swedish National Audit Office's report. It calls for the establishment of an IT crime center to better address and investigate cybercrimes. The motion critiques the current ineffective government oversight of cybersecurity efforts and the lack of a unified approach among various departments, leading to a failure to adequately involve the private sector and address IT-related crimes.

title: Lantmäteriets handläggningstider
summary: The motion proposes to adjust the threshold for state income tax in response to the government's suggestion to pause the inflation adjustment for 2024, which would keep the threshold at 51,000 SEK per month instead of increasing it to 57,000 SEK. This pause would result in 300,000 additional taxpayers facing state income tax and a total of 1.1 million wage earners paying higher taxes. The motion argues that this tax increase disproportionately affects skilled workers in high-demand professions and suggests that the adjustment method should instead reflect the average wage growth to mitigate the impact of the proposed tax increase.

title: Översyn och modernisering av fastighetsbildningslagen
summary: The Center Party motion proposes rejecting the government's bill to reduce the blending obligation for gasoline and diesel, advocating instead for the abolition of the carbon tax on biofuels and a lowered blending fee. The motion emphasizes the importance of maintaining high blending levels of renewable fuels to meet climate goals, improve energy security, and stimulate the green transition in Sweden. Furthermore, it calls for a shift to European diesel standards and a significant increase in biodiesel production to enhance self-sufficiency, while proposing market-oriented measures to promote renewable fuel usage.

title: Bättre förutsättningar för svensk turist- och besöksnäring
summary: The motion proposes the establishment of a central database for government grants to civil society organizations and corresponding contributions at municipal and regional levels, as well as a national representative register. It emphasizes the need for thorough evaluation of the national support function to prevent public funding from reaching extremist organizations and calls for stricter democratic conditions for granting state funds. The proposal is driven by concerns over fraud and extremism infiltrating the civil society sector, demanding reforms to ensure taxpayer money is protected from misuse.

title: Ökat bostadsbyggande
summary: The motion presented by Anna-Caren Sätherberg (S) opposes the government's proposal to reduce the blending requirement for gasoline and diesel, advocating instead for the introduction of 'Sverigebränslet' to lower fuel prices, reduce emissions, create jobs, and improve Sweden's energy preparedness. It suggests maintaining specific blending ratios starting in 2024 and transitioning from MK1 to MK3 diesel standard to enhance biofuel integration and competitiveness in the market, addressing both economic and environmental challenges currently faced by Swedish households.

title: Fler företag och jobb i Norrlands inland
summary: The motion from the Green Party proposes rejecting the government's suggestion to lower the emissions reduction obligation for petrol and diesel, arguing that such a decrease will significantly hinder efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the transportation sector. The authors emphasize the importance of maintaining current obligations to achieve climate targets, propose tax relief for rural residents to facilitate the transition to greener alternatives, and stress the necessity of long-term climate policies to ensure business confidence and effective emissions reduction strategies.

title: Landsbygdsutvecklingen
summary: The parliamentary motion calls for strengthened oversight of state funding to civil society in Sweden. It underscores the need for a law on democratic conditions to ensure that public funds are allocated only to organizations that uphold democratic values and basic human rights. The motion references the Riksrevisionen's report highlighting inefficiencies in the current funding system and proposes the establishment of a central database of state grants, improved support functions for managing risks, and enhanced controls for funding agencies. The Social Democrats emphasize that while increased oversight is necessary, it should not burden civil organizations, and they express concern over the government's slow response to these issues.

title: En mer ändamålsenlig bullerlagstiftning genom bullerservitut
summary: The government's proposal aims to enhance the rights and support for individuals requiring protected housing, particularly focusing on the children's rights perspective for those accompanying a guardian. It suggests regulating protected housing under the Social Services Act to provide necessary support and protection due to threats or violence. The proposal includes provisions for assessing and granting assistance to children individually, clarifying parental consent requirements, and establishing quality standards and oversight for protected housing facilities. It also introduces new legal frameworks for emergency placements and the children’s rights to health checks and education within these settings.

title: Vattenkraftsproduktion
summary: The government proposes to the parliament a legislative change to increase penalties for serious crimes related to firearms and explosives. The proposed amendments aim to enhance the penal code by raising the minimum and maximum prison sentences for serious offenses such as firearm offenses, smuggling of weapons, and explosives, in response to the rising influence of criminal networks and associated violence, with new measures set to take effect from January 1, 2024.

title: Skarpare direktiv vad gäller myndigheterna och äganderätten
summary: The proposal aims to ensure that multinational and large national corporations pay a fair share of taxes regardless of their operational locations by introducing a national supplement tax. This is in response to EU directive 2022/2523 Establishing a global minimum tax rate of at least 15% for corporate entities with revenues of at least 750 million euros. Certain entities, such as governmental bodies and non-profits, may be exempted, and a simplified reporting process will be available during a transition period.

title: Vindkraftsanläggningar
summary: The motion by Kajsa Fredholm and others from the Left Party calls on the Swedish Parliament to reject the government's proposal to lower the reduction obligation for gasoline and diesel, arguing that such a reduction undermines Sweden's climate goals and leads to increased greenhouse gas emissions. The motion emphasizes the need for a sustainable alternative to fossil fuels and urges the government to present a comprehensive action plan aimed at increasing the production of domestically produced renewable fuels and mitigating the emissions gap caused by the proposed reduction. Additionally, it highlights the disproportionate impact of the reduction on economically vulnerable households.

title: Halva basbeloppsregeln
summary: The proposition proposes necessary legislative changes to implement the EU's new drinking water directive, which emphasizes a risk-based approach to drinking water safety. It includes regulations concerning materials that come into contact with drinking water and mandates measures to prevent water leakage. The proposed laws will allow municipalities and water providers to report data essential for assessing risks to drinking water quality, intending to enhance public health and water safety standards.

title: EU och biståndet
summary: The government proposes a new data protection regulation for the Social Insurance Agency and Pension Authority aimed at creating technology-neutral legislation to facilitate a digital and efficient operation while protecting individual privacy. The proposed changes include expanding the purposes for which these authorities can process personal data to include necessary control measures for preventing and detecting erroneous payments and benefit fraud. It also suggests lifting specific restrictions on the disclosure of personal data through automated means, ensuring that such disclosures are done securely and confidentially. The changes are set to come into effect on February 15, 2024.

title: Sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter inom biståndet
summary: The proposal suggests a reduction in the energy tax on gasoline and diesel, specifically lowering the tax on gasoline by 1.31 SEK per liter and on diesel by 341 SEK per cubic meter for 2024. The bill also includes a provision for an extended tax reduction for diesel used in agricultural, forestry, and aquaculture activities, alongside a quarterly refund application process for the tax. The respective changes are set to take effect from January 1, 2024, and January 1, 2025.

title: Motionen utgår
summary: The proposal from the Green Party (MP) urges the Swedish Parliament to reject the government's legislation allowing an increase in the number of nuclear reactors and the locations where they can be built. The motion argues that nuclear power poses significant environmental risks and costs, primarily due to uranium mining and the handling of radioactive waste. Instead, the Green Party advocates for investments in renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power, citing their economic viability and environmental benefits over nuclear energy.

title: Förstärkta rättigheter för sparande och investeringar
summary: The motion proposed by Åsa Westlund and colleagues emphasizes the need for the government to assess the impact of removing student choice in education on the status of culture and sports within schools. It calls for an investigation into how to strengthen the school's cultural mission, given concerns raised by several stakeholders that eliminating student choice may lead to negative consequences for artistic subjects and physical education. The proposal stresses the importance of practical and aesthetic subjects to foster creativity and health among students and underscores the necessity of providing aesthetic courses to all high school students.

title: Anpassade tillståndskrav för tjänstepensionskassor
summary: The motion proposes that all students in municipal adult education and those enrolled in Swedish for immigrants (SFI) programs be granted the right to access free high-quality learning materials. It highlights that many adult education students cannot afford materials, negatively impacting their learning. The motion calls for a clearer legal stipulation ensuring that costs for learning tools cannot be passed onto the students. It also calls for strengthened availability of learning materials within SFI, arguing that such resources are crucial for language development.

title: Stoppa stöldligorna
summary: The motion by Fredrik Olovsson and others from the Social Democrats (S) calls for the rejection of the government's proposals to amend the Environmental Code and the Nuclear Activities Act, while advocating for a new direction in Sweden's energy policy focused on increasing nuclear power capacity. They emphasize the importance of securing energy supply for Sweden's green transition and industrialization, stressing the need for a coordinated political approach to energy production, particularly in using existing nuclear sites more efficiently rather than expanding to new locations. The motion argues for maintaining democratic control over energy infrastructure and the safety implications of nuclear energy.

title: Skärpt straffpåföljd vid försäljning av narkotika
summary: The proposal from Vänsterpartiet suggests that the government should instruct Skolverket to investigate the establishment of a quality certification for educational materials aligned with the values of the curriculum. Additionally, it recommends an inquiry into the availability of relevant printed educational materials for various subjects, and advocates for a legislative proposal ensuring that students in adult education only need to acquire essential learning tools at minimal cost, affirming the need for equitable access to educational resources.

title: Olaglig yrkestrafik
summary: The suggestion by the Center Party proposes that the Swedish Parliament reject the government's bill regarding new nuclear power, which seeks to remove the existing limitation on the number of operational nuclear reactors. The Center Party advocates for maintaining the restriction that new reactors can only be established at existing nuclear sites, arguing that this approach is essential for rapidly expanding Sweden's energy production to meet climate change targets while ensuring safety and efficiency.

title: Nationellt tiggeriförbud
summary: The government proposes to reduce the emissions reduction requirement for gasoline and diesel to six percent for the years 2024 to 2026, with plans to eliminate the reduction levels for 2027 to 2030. This legislative change is intended to take effect from January 1, 2024, as part of efforts to lower fuel prices for households and comply with EU regulations.

title: Förstärkning av polisen i Norrland
summary: The government's proposal suggests pausing the adjustment of the income tax threshold for the tax year 2024, maintaining it at 598,500 SEK. This decision aims to address current economic challenges, especially inflation, and prioritize financial resources for other initiatives supporting households. The proposal has received mixed feedback from consultative bodies, with concerns raised about potential negative effects on work incentives and economic growth.

title: Avskaffande av fastighetstaxeringen
summary: The Left Party opposes the government's proposal for new nuclear power in Sweden, arguing that it is an unsuitable and costly energy solution that hampers the transition to renewable energy sources. They advocate for phasing out nuclear power and investing in 100% renewable energy by 2040, specifically emphasizing the potential of wind power, both onshore and offshore. The Left Party criticizes the government's approach, claiming it focuses too heavily on nuclear energy while neglecting the renewable sector and fails to address the nation's energy needs adequately.

title: Ökade krav på kommunernas dokumentation vid underkännande av enskilt avlopp
Tillämpningen av EU-bestämmelser
summary: The motion proposes to reject the government's bill on tax changes and instead seeks to expand tax reductions specifically in the job tax deduction for low and middle incomes. It advocates for a significant decrease in income taxes on work to incentivize transitioning from benefits to employment, decrease business costs, and stimulate investment in Sweden. The proposed changes would result in a total tax reduction of 2 billion SEK more than the government's plan, benefiting low-income earners more significantly.

title: Avskaffa kravet på hotelltillstånd
summary: The Swedish government's letter to the parliament outlines its assessment of the Riksrevisionen's report regarding the effectiveness of the government's management of societal information and cybersecurity. The report identifies significant shortcomings in the government's strategic direction, prioritization, and coordination in this domain, noting that existing efforts have not conformed to international best practices. The government acknowledges these findings and intends to develop a new national cybersecurity strategy to address these issues, improve collaboration with relevant stakeholders, and enhance the operational and tactical competencies necessary for effective information and cybersecurity management.

title: Översyn av lagen om hets mot folkgrupp
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1219 av Jan Ericson och Lars Beckman (båda M)
summary: This motion addresses the need for the Swedish government to enhance the development of digital services by public authorities, emphasizing user involvement in the design process. It calls for the Digital Administration Authority (Digg) to receive clearer directives and tools to ensure uniformity across various agencies. The proposal underscores the importance of improving user accessibility and experience, particularly for citizens with special needs, to facilitate a smoother transition to digitized public services.

title: Avveckling av Jämställdhetsmyndigheten
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1218 av Jan Ericson och Lars Beckman (båda M)
summary: The Swedish government's report addresses the effectiveness of state funding to civil society organizations as assessed by the National Audit Office. The audit concluded that the current system lacks sufficient efficacy and recommended enhanced controls to restore trust in the funding system. Key recommendations include establishing a central database for all available state grants, creating national support functions to manage risks, and improving the monitoring and compliance of grant recipients to ensure funds are used appropriately. The government acknowledges the audit's findings and outlines actions taken and planned to improve the funding mechanisms.

title: Fribelopp vid högre studier
summary: The Center Party argues against the government's proposal to tighten immigration conditions for family reunification and limit possibilities for residence permits on humanitarian grounds. They advocate for a balanced immigration policy that combines compassion with order, and they emphasize the importance of family reunification for asylum seekers. The party criticizes the removal of unconditional support for family reunification for individuals with alternative protection status, asserting that this change would lead to family separations and hinder integration. Furthermore, they oppose the government's plan to restrict humanitarian grounds for residence permits, emphasizing the need to protect vulnerable children and adults in Sweden.

title: Värna Umeå universitet
summary: Miljöpartiet motions till riksdagens beslut syftar till att avslå regeringens proposition om skärpta villkor för anhöriginvandring och begränsade möjligheter till uppehållstillstånd av humanitära skäl. Partiet uttrycker skarp kritik mot de föreslagna förändringarna, som de menar kommer att ha negativa effekter, särskilt för barn, och påpekar att de strider mot internationella konventioner och rekommendationer från myndigheter. Miljöpartiet anser att regeringens argument för en mer restriktiv migrationspolitik är otillräckliga och anser att barnets bästa bör prioriteras.

title: Uppvisande av körkort
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament should reject the government's bill which tightens the conditions for family immigration and limits the possibilities for granting residency permits on humanitarian grounds. The Left Party argues that these changes represent a shift towards more restrictive immigration policies, which would negatively affect vulnerable groups, especially children, and violate Sweden's international commitments, including the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child.

title: Höjd hastighet för bärgningsbilar
summary: The proposal presents an amendment to the 2023 state budget, which allows the government to donate military equipment to Ukraine, including ammunition, spare parts, communication equipment, and infantry supplies, valued at up to 1,657 million kronor. This initiative responds to the deteriorating security situation in the region due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine and reflects Sweden's interest in supporting Ukraine amidst ongoing needs for military assistance.

title: Fortkörning vid vägarbeten
summary: The government proposes the introduction of a regulatory framework for the acquisition and management of distressed credit agreements, which are contracts where borrowers are unable to pay on time. The proposal aims to strengthen the regulation of the market for transferring distressed credit agreements, enhance borrower protection, and ensure that credit managers are supervised by the Financial Supervisory Authority. Key changes include requiring licenses for managing distressed credit agreements, providing relevant information during transfers, and consolidating the supervision of debt collection companies.

title: Fortkörning där blåljuspersonal arbetar
summary: Centerpartiet föreslår i sin motion till riksdagen 2024 budgetanslag för klimat-, miljö- och naturåtgärder. Motiveringen fokuserar på att påskynda klimatomställningen och uppnå FN:s klimatmål genom stöd till grön teknik och innovationer, stärkta insatser för den biologiska mångfalden, samt förbättringar av befintliga skyddade områden. Förslagen inkluderar en klimatbilbonus för att uppmuntra köp av klimatvänligare fordon, samt förstärkningar av den så kallade Industriklivet för att stödja företag i deras klimatomställning.

title: Organdonationer
summary: This parliamentary motion proposes a budget for 2024 focused on regional development, emphasizing the need for improved coordination of state actions to enhance local and regional competitiveness. The Center Party calls for a review of regional support regulations to better assist small businesses and promote sustainability and gender equality. Additionally, the motion advocates for targeted financial relief for rural households impacted by rising fuel prices due to the Ukraine crisis, proposing a significant reduction in costs compared to the government's broader tax cut approach. Overall, the proposal maintains current funding levels while introducing a new allocation aimed at reducing fuel prices in rural areas.

title: Kontroll i fråga om assistansersättning
summary: Catarina Deremar proposes a budget for 2024 focused on enhancing culture, media, faith communities, and leisure activities across Sweden. The proposal includes increased funding for cultural initiatives and infrastructure, particularly in underserved areas, to ensure that cultural participation is accessible to all. It emphasizes the importance of public service in ensuring diverse news coverage and suggests a national culture plan. Additionally, the motion opposes a proposed change in legislation that would increase governmental control over folk education funding, advocating for greater autonomy in this sector.

title: Inför en nationell sköldkörtelstrategi i Sverige
summary: Rickard Nordin from the Center Party proposes a series of financial adjustments and recommendations aimed at improving Sweden's energy production and addressing the climate crisis. The proposal includes rejecting government plans for credit guarantees for new nuclear power investments, advocating for increased funding for energy efficiency measures, and calling for a cooperative energy agreement across party lines to reduce emissions. The suggestion emphasizes the need for quick electrification and the use of various renewable energy sources to foster energy independence and secure both environmental and economic interests.

title: Gårdsförsäljning
summary: The suggestion proposes adjustments to education funding in Sweden, aiming to increase work participation while supporting flexible study options. It advocates for a reformed student aid system that encourages quicker graduation, accommodates those with lower study pace, raises the age limit for obtaining student aid, and eliminates income restrictions on loan parts of student aid. The proposal also supports increased funding for vocational education and transitional study support to facilitate career shifts throughout one’s working life.

title: Framtidens infektioner
summary: The proposal by Jonny Cato calls for adjustments to the budget for 2024 within the Employment and Labor area, emphasizing the need for reforms to address rising unemployment and enhance job integration. It outlines the impact of recent economic crises on Sweden's labor market and advocates for measures such as reduced costs for hiring, increased support for competence development, and job creation initiatives, especially for those at a disadvantage in the job market. Additionally, it proposes changes to unemployment benefits and argues for a stronger presence of the Employment Service in all regions of Sweden.

title: Cancerscreening
summary: The proposal by Alireza Akhondi emphasizes the urgent need to address Sweden's housing crisis through increased support for housing construction, effective utilization of existing homes, and improved planning processes by locals and states. It advocates for the elimination of barriers to new housing development, especially in rural areas, and suggests reforms in rental regulations to enhance housing accessibility. The proposal also highlights the importance of sustainable housing policy and calls for measures that protect agricultural land while allowing for small residential developments.

title: Säkerhetspolitisk handlingsfrihet
summary: Centerpartiet proposes increased funding for education and university research in Sweden for the year 2024, aiming to improve the quality of education from preschool through higher education. The proposal emphasizes the importance of accessible and high-quality education for all students, particularly for those from disadvantaged backgrounds. It includes measures to enhance the preschool system, bolster the training and status of teachers, support adult education, and ensure that higher education meets labor market demands, all while simplifying funding mechanisms to reduce administrative burdens.

title: Traktamente för soldater
summary: This motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament recognizes e-sports as a legitimate sport and part of cultural heritage, advocating for the inclusion of gaming in the cultural framework. The motion calls for improved governmental support for e-sports, including funding and clarity around prize money for skill-based games. It emphasizes the social benefits of e-sports, the need for research on its impacts, and the importance of promoting equality and anti-racism within the e-sport community. Furthermore, it suggests the establishment of a national gaming strategy and institute to support the industry and enhance its integration into both culture and the economy.

title: Stoppa införandet av kilometerskatt
summary: The suggested parliamentary motion from Miljöpartiet focuses on enhancing economic security for families and children in Sweden. It proposes adjusting the budget allocations for child benefits, parental insurance, and housing allowances, and calls for a reevaluation of the impact of new parental leave policies. The motion emphasizes the need to prevent commercialization of parental leave and to ensure equality in parental responsibilities, stating that one-third of parental leave days should be reserved for each parent. Additionally, it argues for inflation adjustments to child support and maintenance allowances, highlights the importance of a commission aimed at combating child poverty, and advocates for making family structures more inclusive.

title: Skatteregler för barnvaktstjänster
summary: The parliamentary motion aims to strengthen protections against animal rights activism by proposing measures such as banning demonstrations on private property, increasing penalties for trespassing on farms, allowing farmers to use surveillance cameras, creating a separate crime code for animal rights-related offenses, and criminalizing the financing of violent animal rights extremism. It highlights the importance of safeguarding Swedish agriculture from the threats of radical animal rights activism, which has reportedly escalated in recent years, resulting in harassment, property damage, and increased insecurity for farmers and their families.

title: Skatteavdrag för gymkort
summary: Centerpartiet presents its budget proposal for 2024, emphasizing the need for real crisis management in light of multiple challenges facing Sweden, including economic, educational, climate, and crime-related issues. Key initiatives include substantial tax cuts amounting to 10 billion kronor, particularly benefiting low-income earners, along with increased funding for education and vital local services, a new climate bonus for environmentally friendly vehicles, support for rural areas, and increased resources to combat gang violence.

title: Ta bort överindexeringen av bensin och diesel
summary: Centerpartiet proposes a budget for 2024 focusing on healthcare, social services, and elder support, emphasizing accessibility and quality of care for all individuals regardless of age, gender, or location. Key initiatives include increasing funding for preventive health measures, mental health support for students, and enhancing caregiving for the elderly through a safety housing guarantee. The party advocates for more local decision-making in healthcare while stressing the importance of getting adequate resources for emergency healthcare services and social services.

title: RUT-avdrag för taxiresor
summary: The proposal from the Center Party requests the Swedish Parliament to allocate funds for 2024 within the area of economic security for the elderly, emphasizing the need for sustainable pension solutions. It highlights the importance of raising the retirement age, improving work conditions, and achieving gender equality in pensions. The Center Party supports maintaining the principles of the current pension system while criticizing the lack of cooperation among parties in the Pensionsgroup, urging for proposals that ensure secure pensions and uphold the principle of lifetime income.

title: Avskaffa flygskatten
summary: The proposal by the Center Party aims to allocate funds for 2024 to strengthen agriculture, rural areas, and food production in Sweden, recognizing their importance in sustainable food security, employment, and climate resilience. The motion emphasizes the need for improved competitiveness in the agricultural sector, addressing supply chain vulnerabilities, labor shortages, and enhancing environmental adaptation. It also calls for government initiatives to bolster wildlife management, sustainable fishing, and forestry practices while respecting property rights and encouraging participation in the green transition.

title: Villkor för turism i Sverige
summary: The Center Party proposes an increase in general government grants to municipalities by 1 billion kronor for 2024, emphasizing the importance of local governance in providing essential services such as education, healthcare, and public transport. The proposal aims to enhance the financial capacity of municipalities and regions to meet locally varying needs, while suggesting a reduction in funds for urban areas not eligible for travel deductions.

title: Villkor för småföretag
summary: Centerpartiet proposes a budget allocation for 2024 aimed at fostering growth across various sectors, including investments in education, infrastructure, and simplification of regulatory processes. The motion emphasizes the need to enhance Sweden's competitiveness by attracting skilled labor, reforming income taxation, and reinforcing the importance of digitalization. It outlines the critical role of basic industries, particularly forestry and mining, in sustaining economic welfare, and calls for the responsible extraction of essential metals while addressing bureaucratic inefficiencies that hinder business investments.

title: Exportstöd till svensk småbåtsindustri
summary: The Center Party's motion proposes budget allocations for migration in 2024, emphasizing the need for Sweden to contribute to a collective EU migration policy amidst global displacement crises, particularly due to the war in Ukraine. The motion seeks to maintain and improve current asylum legislation, ensure humane return processes for rejected asylum seekers, and reform labor immigration regulations to encourage foreign workers to contribute to the Swedish economy. It highlights the importance of integration and self-sufficiency for asylum seekers while addressing issues of fraud in work permits.

title: Stärkt äganderätt
summary: The Center Party proposes various reforms to the Swedish sickness insurance system, aiming to enhance economic security for individuals with illnesses or disabilities. The proposal emphasizes early interventions and rehabilitation to support a quick return to work, while advocating for the reinstatement of high-cost protection for sick leave costs. Additionally, it suggests allowing individuals on disability benefits to explore work or study opportunities without losing their support and calls for the removal of the refugee exception in sickness and activity allowances. The overall goal is to streamline the system and ensure better support for those affected.

title: Offentlig upphandling av mat bör ske utifrån minimikraven i svensk lag
summary: The Center Party proposes modifications to the budget for 2024 aimed at enhancing economic security for families and children. Key proposals include modernizing parental benefits to promote equality in parental leave, adjusting housing allowance regulations to better assist single parents and families living apart, and increasing child support payments. Additionally, the party suggests the removal of the two-child allowance to reallocate funds towards these initiatives, ultimately aiming to address the financial challenges faced by economically vulnerable families, especially single parents.

title: Förtroendet för allemansrätten
summary: The suggestion from the Center Party advocates for increased government funding in transportation and IT infrastructure, emphasizing the importance of a well-functioning system for both economic activity and rural living. It aims to reduce carbon emissions from transport by 70% by 2030 and proposes investments in public transport, cycling infrastructure, and digital communication to enhance accessibility and sustainability. Additionally, there are calls for improving air travel's environmental impact and supporting the maritime industry, while addressing necessary regulatory reforms for A-tractors and enhancing rural broadband access.

title: Förenklade strandskyddsregler
summary: The motion seeks to initiate an investigation into potential legislative changes to protect and promote traditional fäbodbruk (herding practice) in Sweden. It highlights the importance of fäbodar for biodiversity conservation, cultural heritage, sustainable living, and the challenges faced by fäbodbrukare, including the need for better knowledge dissemination, support for profitability, and the safeguarding of grazing rights. The motion calls for a review of relevant legislation to support these objectives.

title: Bredda granskningsnämndens uppdrag
summary: The proposal from the Center Party focuses on securing funding for gender equality and the integration of newly arrived immigrants. It emphasizes the need for stronger measures against men's violence towards women, improving women's economic independence, ensuring equal healthcare services, and enhancing the support systems for women facing violence. The proposal also highlights the importance of effective reforms for the integration of newcomers, emphasizing job opportunities and language education, and recommends increased financial support for various programs aimed at supporting both gender equality and integration initiatives.

title: Förenkla administrationen för företag - en uppgift en gång
summary: The proposal from the Center Party suggests adjustments to the budget for 2024 within the area of taxation and customs, emphasizing the importance of a functional tax system and administration for the economy. The motion advocates for a reduction in administrative burdens for small businesses, the introduction of simplified taxation for micro-enterprises, and increased funding for the Swedish Customs Authority to enhance its law enforcement capabilities against organized crime and smuggling. It also stresses the need for transparent and fair taxation to boost public trust and foster economic growth.

title: Digitalisera Myndighetssverige
motion_id: Motion 2020/21:1188 av Ann-Sofie Lifvenhage och Lotta Finstorp (båda M)
summary: The Center Party proposes an increase in funding for the Swedish criminal justice system in 2024, emphasizing the need for enhanced capabilities in policing, prosecution, courts, and correctional facilities due to rising crime rates, including violent and organized crime.
