Currently, fishing inspectors are only present in Swedish lakes and rivers, and the proposal calls for their extension to coastal areas, complementing the existing efforts of the Coast Guard.

title: Rimliga avgifter för betalningspåminnelser
summary: This proposal suggests that the Swedish Parliament should study the feasibility of implementing similar limitations on reminder fees for government agencies as those currently applicable to companies, in order to ensure fair treatment of debtors and prevent excessive charges by state entities for late payments.

title: Funktionsrättskonventionen
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish parliament supports making the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities a law, emphasizing the need for equal human rights and personal support for people with disabilities to live fully included lives in society. It highlights the ongoing disparities in living conditions for individuals with disabilities compared to the general population and stresses that the implementation of the convention is essential to uphold these rights.

title: Tillgänglighetsanpassade lekplatser
summary: The suggestion advocates for reviewing the potential to make playgrounds accessible for all children, regardless of physical, intellectual, or neuropsychiatric disabilities, in accordance with the principles of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, which is part of Swedish law since 2020. The proposal emphasizes the importance of social interaction and physical activity among children, urging municipalities to consider accessibility in their planning to foster equal opportunities and improve overall health.

title: Avdrag för köp och installation av miljöcertifierat avlopp
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament supports the investigation of a tax deduction for property owners who purchase and install environmentally certified sewage systems. It highlights the environmental issue of nutrient pollution caused by outdated sewage systems and suggests that financial assistance through tax deductions could encourage property owners to update their systems, benefiting both the environment and homeowners.

title: Certifiering för entreprenörer eller hantverkare som installerar avlopp
summary: The proposal suggests that the Swedish Parliament consider implementing a certification requirement for contractors and craftsmen who install sewage systems, emphasizing the need to prevent unnecessary emissions, damages, and accidents resulting from improperly installed systems. The motion argues that proper management of sewage is crucial for the health of water bodies and groundwater, highlighting the importance of addressing pollution in lakes and oceans through such certification.

title: Förtur i bostadsköerna för våldsutsatta kvinnor och barn
summary: This motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament study the conditions necessary to provide prioritized access to housing for women and children who have experienced violence. Highlighting the serious issue of domestic violence, the motion argues that the long queues for housing can force victims to remain with their abusers due to a lack of alternatives. It suggests that societal measures, such as giving priority in housing queues or creating a separate queue for these individuals, are needed to ensure their safety and well-being.

title: Kraftsamling mot mäns våld mot kvinnor
summary: The motion emphasizes the urgent need for a concerted effort to combat men's violence against women, highlighting the daily harassment, violence, and sexual crimes faced by women, often from partners or former partners. It calls for a comprehensive government program aimed at eradicating such violence, ensuring that the criminal justice system responds effectively and imposes significant penalties on offenders. The proposal advocates for sufficient resources for the police, necessitating offender treatment in prison, and ultimately a societal shift towards zero tolerance for violence against women.

title: Kornas rätt till bete och utevistelse
summary: The motion proposes to protect and enhance the right of cattle to graze and have outdoor access in order to promote animal welfare within the Swedish dairy industry. It emphasizes that grazing contributes to biodiversity and positively impacts the image of Swedish animal husbandry and rural life. The motion argues against changes to grazing legislation that would favor barn-reared cattle over free-range access, highlighting the health benefits for cattle when they can move freely outside. It also calls for extending outdoor grazing rights to young bulls, as many do not currently experience grazing. The proposal indicates strong consumer support for improved animal welfare standards in agricultural practices.

title: En ny internationell Östersjömyndighet med säte i Karlskrona
summary: The proposal advocates for the establishment of a new international Baltic Sea Authority based in Karlskrona, aimed at enhancing regional cooperation among Baltic Sea countries to address pressing environmental challenges such as pollution and overfishing, exacerbated by recent geopolitical tensions. The authority would have the mandate to coordinate efforts, issue binding regulations, and raise public awareness about the ecological state of the Baltic Sea, while excluding Russia from participation due to its aggression in Ukraine.

title: Högkostnadsskydd för hjälpmedel till personer med funktionsvariation
summary: The proposal advocates for the government to investigate the establishment of a uniform high-cost protection scheme for assistive devices accessible to all individuals with disabilities, regardless of their municipality or region of residence, ensuring equitable access and fees.

title: Omledning av kommersiell båttrafik från känsliga områden i Östersjön
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament study the conditions for redirecting commercial shipping routes away from sensitive areas in the Baltic Sea to mitigate environmental and wildlife disruption, particularly focusing on protecting endangered species such as the harbor porpoise affected by ship noise.

title: Företagshälsovård för alla arbetstagare
summary: The motion proposes that all employees should be covered by occupational health care services, highlighting a concerning trend where access is unevenly distributed, with larger workplaces having better access than smaller ones. The author argues that the current system often focuses on addressing existing problems rather than preventing them. By making occupational health care mandatory, the motion aims to improve employee rehabilitation, reduce sick leave, and ensure better workplace health management, particularly for underrepresented groups in various professions.

title: Statligt stöd till Sveriges kvinno- och tjejjourer
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament should investigate the possibility of establishing long-term state funding for women's shelters, which play a critical role in supporting women and children affected by domestic violence. It emphasizes the alarming statistics of partner violence against women and the necessity of ensuring stable financial resources for shelters to maintain their operations and provide essential services to victims. The motion calls for the government to prioritize this issue to protect vulnerable individuals and strengthen societal responses to domestic violence.

title: Ekosystembaserad havsförvaltning
summary: The motion advocates for Sweden to pursue strong implementation of ecosystem-based marine management, emphasizing a holistic approach that considers interspecies interactions and sustainable use of marine ecosystems. It highlights the need for such management to address the historical overfishing that has led to imbalances in marine ecosystems, and argues that resilient ecosystems are better equipped to handle climate change and other challenges. The proposal calls for action both nationally and within the EU.

title: Stärkt skydd av marina områden
summary: The motion proposes that Sweden aims to protect 30% of its marine areas by 2030, with one-third of these areas being strictly protected. It calls for enhanced oversight to combat illegal fishing and harmful environmental practices, and advocates for the sustainable management of protected marine areas to promote biodiversity and resource use.

title: Statligt ansvar för ekologisk märkning och certifiering i Sverige
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish government study the benefits of establishing a state responsibility for ecological labeling and certification, similar to the successful model used in Denmark. This approach is suggested to boost the organic sector in Sweden by creating a partnership between politicians, officials, and the agricultural and food industry, ultimately enhancing competition, sustainability, and employment. The motion emphasizes the need for clearer regulation and reduced costs for organic farmers and producers to better compete with imported goods.

title: Högkostnadsskydd för tandvården
summary: The motion proposes the introduction of a high-cost protection for dental care, similar to that available within healthcare, to ensure that low-income individuals can access necessary dental services without financial burdens. It emphasizes the importance of early dental visits for children and the negative impact of poor dental health on overall health, particularly among disadvantaged groups. The motion urges the government to review the feasibility of implementing such a protection, highlighting recent reductions in dental benefits for young adults under the current government.

title: Satsning för kvinnors hälsa
summary: The motion emphasizes the need for increased investment in women's health within the healthcare system, highlighting that current practices do not always provide equitable care for women, particularly regarding gender-specific diseases. It points out the historical bias in medical research towards male diseases, resulting in inadequate understanding and treatment of conditions that predominantly affect women. The proposal calls for the government to acknowledge and act on these disparities to enhance the quality of care for women.

title: Heltid som norm i statligt ägda bolag
summary: The proposal advocates for the introduction of full-time work as the standard in state-owned companies in Sweden, emphasizing its importance for gender equality. It argues that women, who are more likely to work part-time and shoulder unpaid domestic responsibilities, would benefit from full-time positions, leading to improved economic independence and better pension outcomes. The motion highlights that establishing full-time work as the norm can enhance workplace conditions for all employees, reduce absenteeism, and promote a fairer labor market where responsibilities are shared equally between genders.

title: Stöd till de politiska ungdomsförbunden
summary: This motion proposes that the Swedish government conduct a review of how to establish a mandate-based support system for political youth organizations, responding to concerns about declining political engagement among young people aged 15 to 24. The motion highlights the difficulties these organizations face in reaching schools and communities, and argues for increased state support and guidelines to enable local governments to support political youth organizations more effectively, with the aim of strengthening democracy.

title: Avskaffa orättvisan i karensavdraget
summary: The motion proposes to abolish the waiting days deduction for sick leave, which creates financial insecurity for workers, particularly those with low incomes and unstable jobs. The author argues that this deduction leads to individuals working while sick, contributing to the spread of illness and negatively impacting public health. Eliminating the deduction would promote a safer work environment and allow individuals to prioritize their health without fearing economic repercussions.

title: Införande av ett nytt investeringsstöd till byggnation av hyresbostäder och bostäder för studenter
summary: The suggestion proposes the introduction of a new investment support scheme aimed at the construction of rental housing and student accommodations in Sweden. It highlights the growing housing queue and the urgent need for affordable rental options due to decreased purchasing power, rising interest rates, and increased construction costs. The proposal emphasizes the importance of investment support for revitalizing the housing market, which has seen a drastic decline in new constructions, and asserts that housing is a human right that should be prioritized.

title: Ett statligt fastighetsbolag med uppdrag att förvärva och bygga fastigheter i hela landet
summary: The proposal advocates for the establishment of a state-owned real estate company tasked with acquiring and building properties across Sweden, with a focus on reducing housing segregation and promoting sustainable, climate-friendly construction. The initiative aims to address socio-economic challenges in underprivileged areas, mitigate inequality, and enhance access to green spaces for community recreation.

title: Reglering av användning och tillgång till lustgas
summary: The motion proposes the introduction of stricter regulations and oversight on the sale, distribution, and use of nitrous oxide (commonly known as laughing gas) in Sweden due to its rising recreational use among youth, which poses significant health risks and environmental concerns. It suggests measures such as setting a minimum age for purchase, requiring licenses for sellers, banning recreational use, enhancing monitoring by relevant authorities, running awareness campaigns about the risks, and supporting research on the long-term effects of nitrous oxide. The aim is to protect public health, particularly for young people, and mitigate its environmental impact.

title: Möjlighet att göra Sverige till ett elprisområde igen
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament expresses its support for creating a unified electricity pricing area in Sweden, with the aim of addressing significant price disparities between northern and southern regions. The motion highlights the current division into four pricing areas since November 2011 and argues that the existing regulations lead to unfair pricing for consumers. The proposal calls for the government to be informed of the Parliament's stance as part of an ongoing review of electricity pricing areas.

title: Politiska ungdomsförbunds tillgång till skolan är avgörande för demokratin
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament ensure that political youth organizations have regular access to high schools and secondary schools, even outside of election years, to foster trust in democracy and engage young people in societal issues. It highlights a worrying trend of declining confidence in democracy among youth, attributing this to a lack of political engagement and rising concerns about personal wellbeing and economic stability.

title: Räddade sill- och strömmingsbestånd i Östersjön
summary: The motion proposes an immediate pause on large-scale herring and sprat fishing in the Baltic Sea to allow fish stocks to recover, as they have significantly declined due to overfishing and eutrophication. The motion calls for a ban on all herring and sprat fishing not intended for human consumption, to reduce pressure on these vulnerable stocks. It emphasizes the need for ecosystem-based management of marine resources to promote sustainability and protect biodiversity in the Baltic Sea.

title: En sammanhållen politik mot PFAS
summary: The motion proposes the development of a cohesive national strategy to combat PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances), highlighting the need for immediate action to ban these harmful chemicals and implement strict regulations. It emphasizes the importance of supporting affected communities and individuals, funding local healthcare for PFAS screening and treatment, ensuring that waterworks have the necessary resources for PFAS removal, and providing financial support for the remediation of contaminated areas. The motion calls for a national PFAS law to guarantee a unified approach to addressing this urgent health and environmental issue.

title: Förbud mot PFAS i Sverige, EU och världen
summary: This motion proposes a complete ban on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in Sweden and the EU, and advocates for a global prohibition through relevant international bodies. The use of PFAS, which are prevalent in various consumer products and are linked to severe health and environmental risks, poses an immediate threat to both human and animal health. The motion emphasizes the necessity of political action against these chemicals, highlighting that alternatives exist and calling for human rights to a safe environment.

title: Förslag om nationellt stöd till vattenverk för rening av PFAS från dricksvatten
summary: The proposal suggests that the Swedish parliament support a national initiative to assist waterworks in purifying drinking water from PFAS contaminants. It emphasizes the serious health risks posed by PFAS, which are persistent chemicals linked to various health issues. The proposal calls for earmarked funds for the National Food Agency to distribute to waterworks for PFAS removal projects, as well as technical support for implementing effective purification technologies. It stresses the need for coordinated national efforts to ensure all citizens have access to safe drinking water.

title: Förslag om nationellt stöd till samhällen och individer drabbade av PFAS-föroreningar
summary: The proposal advocates for national support for communities and individuals affected by PFAS contamination, emphasizing the need for health monitoring, treatment resources, and public information to manage the long-term health impacts associated with PFAS exposure. It stresses the inadequacy of merely banning PFAS and calls for a proactive government response to assist those already harmed by these substances.

title: Införande av gränsvärden för PFAS i livsmedel
summary: The motion proposed by Magnus Manhammar advocates for the Swedish Parliament to study the feasibility of establishing strict limits for PFAS (per- and polyfluorinated alkyl substances) in food products. It emphasizes the health risks associated with PFAS exposure through contaminated food, which can lead to serious health issues, including immune system impairment and increased cancer risk. The proposal aims to protect public health, enhance food safety, and strengthen consumer protection by ensuring that food sold to the public is free from harmful chemicals.

title: Kriminalisering av psykisk misshandel
summary: This motion proposes the criminalization of psychological abuse, emphasizing its prevalence in cases of men's violence against women and in intimate partner relationships. The motion argues that psychological abuse, often alongside physical violence, is a significant societal issue that causes severe suffering for victims. Currently, psychological abuse is not recognized as a standalone criminal offense, which prevents victims from reporting such abuse. The motion highlights the support from law enforcement for the criminalization and references similar laws in other countries, urging the government to take action on this issue.

title: Lagen om hets mot folkgrupp
summary: The proposal suggests that the Swedish Parliament initiate an investigation into the possible reform or abolition of the law against incitement against ethnic groups, citing concerns about its impact on free speech. The motion argues that the law's application has led to subjective judgments that restrict open debate, potentially causing self-censorship among citizens. The sponsors believe that a review of this legislation is necessary to enhance the protection of freedom of expression in society.

title: Jämställdhet och bistånd
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:870 av Lotta Johnsson Fornarve m.fl. (V)
summary: The motion proposes that Sweden should adopt a feminist foreign policy and create a comprehensive action plan for gender equality across all areas of the Ministry for Foreign Affairs' responsibilities, including security, trade, and development. It emphasizes the importance of directing at least 50% of aid towards women and girls, increasing support for sexual and reproductive health rights, and ensuring that all international collaborations prioritize gender equality. The motion also calls for the reinstatement of Sweden's gender equality ambassador and urges increased funding for women’s rights organizations and initiatives aimed at preventing gender-based violence.

title: En välfärd utan vinstintresse
summary: The proposal advocates for a ban on profit-making in welfare services, suggesting that the government should develop non-profit alternatives to current market-driven models in public sectors like healthcare and education. The motion emphasizes the negative impacts of profit interests on service quality and equity, calling for enhanced oversight and national efforts to ensure services are delivered based on need rather than profitability, thereby aiming to restore public trust in welfare systems.

title: Skattereform för bättre fördelningspolitik
summary: The proposal advocates for a comprehensive review and reform of Sweden's tax system to address issues of income inequality and underfunding in welfare services. It critiques past tax cuts that have resulted in historically low tax levels, which have exacerbated economic disparities, particularly during challenging economic times marked by inflation and high interest rates. The motion calls for a unified approach among political parties to create a sustainable tax system that is fair, promotes growth, and ensures adequate funding for essential services.

title: Sveriges stöd för Ukrainas frihet och vägval mot Europa
summary: The suggestion advocates for Sweden to continue and intensify its support for Ukraine in its fight for freedom, including maintaining and expanding sanctions against Russia. It emphasizes the importance of standing united with the European Union and transatlantic partners to secure Ukraine's sovereignty and integration into European and transatlantic communities. The proposal also calls for accountability for war crimes committed during the conflict and highlights the need to support Ukraine's efforts toward EU and NATO membership based on merit and ongoing reforms.

title: En robust livsmedelsförsörjning som inte exkluderar halva Sverige
summary: The proposal emphasizes the need for a robust food supply system across all of Sweden, particularly addressing vulnerabilities in northern regions that may face food shortages during crises like war. It argues against relocating populations as a solution, instead advocating for enhanced local agriculture, resilient logistics, and food stockpiling to ensure national food security.

title: Avskaffande av betänketiden vid skilsmässa
summary: The proposal seeks to abolish the mandatory reflection period required before a divorce in Sweden, arguing that individuals should not be compelled to remain married against their will, even temporarily. The motion highlights the negative impact of this waiting period, especially on individuals in destructive or violent relationships, and asserts that marriage should fundamentally be a choice made by autonomous individuals without state interference.

title: Fungerande isbrytning
summary: The motion emphasizes the necessity of strengthening icebreaker preparedness in Northern Sweden to ensure the competitiveness of industry and export. It highlights that 90% of Sweden's import and export relies on maritime transport, and without effective icebreaking, ports could face closures during winter. The recent winter of 2023-2024 illustrated the challenges faced by the export-dependent industry in the region due to severe ice conditions, leading to increased costs and delays that threaten the logistic chains and global market competitiveness.

title: Farmaceut på distans på landsbygd
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:864 av Kalle Olsson och Anna-Caren Sätherberg (båda S)
summary: The proposal suggests that the Riksdag supports testing the implementation of remote pharmacists in rural areas to improve access to healthcare services, particularly in places with limited pharmacy availability. It acknowledges the growing trend of digital healthcare interactions and seeks to address the challenges posed by the shortage of pharmacists, which has led to restricted pharmacy hours and closures in smaller communities.

title: Suicidprevention
summary: The suggestion advocates for strengthening suicide prevention efforts within public authorities and emphasizes the need for increased funding and support for organizations dedicated to suicide prevention. It highlights the tragic reality of suicide as a leading cause of death among young people and urges for proactive measures to improve mental health interventions, promote knowledge dissemination, and provide support for those affected by suicide.

title: Höjning av nivån på bostadsbidraget
summary: The proposal calls for the long-term consideration of making the temporary increase in housing benefits permanent to address ongoing economic challenges faced by low-income individuals, particularly young adults, families with children, and those with disabilities. The motion argues that housing benefits help reduce economic disparities and provide essential support for vulnerable groups, especially during periods of high living costs and inflation.

title: Höjning av bostadstillägget
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament encourages the government to consider increasing the level of housing supplements for pensioners, emphasizing the importance of this social benefit in addressing economic disparities among the elderly. Currently, over 300,000 pensioners qualify for this benefit, which varies based on living circumstances, and the proposer argues that an increase would enhance the financial well-being of this vulnerable group.

title: Karensavdraget vid sjukdom
summary: The proposed motion aims to abolish the sick leave deduction (karensavdraget) in Sweden due to its perceived unfairness, particularly affecting those unable to work from home during illness. The motion highlights the financial pressures that lead many workers, particularly in manual labor and low-income roles, to continue working while sick, risking both their health and public health. It argues that the current system exacerbates inequality among different occupational groups and should be permanently reconsidered to promote equity in living conditions and improve public health.

title: En rättvis arbetslöshetsförsäkring
summary: The proposal advocates for necessary measures to establish a fair and adequate unemployment insurance system in Sweden, emphasizing the importance of a well-functioning, voluntary, and solidarity-based unemployment insurance managed by independent unemployment funds. It argues that a properly designed unemployment insurance system can facilitate economic transitions, provide financial security to those who lose their jobs, stimulate economic demand, and counteract downward pressure on wages. The motion points out the need to ensure that more individuals receive up to 80% of their previous income during unemployment to enhance equity and protect those in lower income brackets.

title: Energieffektivisering av bostadsbeståndet för en rättvis klimatomställning
summary: The proposal emphasizes the need for increased energy efficiency in Sweden's housing sector as a critical step towards a just climate transition. It advocates for regulatory measures that would facilitate necessary investments for individuals and ensure that energy efficiency improvements in rental properties do not lead to increased rents. The motion underscores the significant energy consumption attributed to residential housing and the potential for substantial energy savings through effective policies, aiming to stabilize household energy costs amid rising electricity demands.

title: Räddningstjänsten och ansvaret för olyckor
summary: The proposal suggests that the government should conduct an investigation into the regional or national control of emergency services to enhance uniformity and coordination across Sweden. It also calls for legislation mandating municipalities to take preventive measures for fire safety, especially for vulnerable groups, and to ensure rigorous oversight of fire safety in multi-family housing. Additionally, the motion advocates for integrating water safety into the school curriculum, setting swimming competency goals, and enhancing inspections in schools to promote drowning prevention. The introduction of a concept for civilian responders to assist in emergencies is also recommended.

title: En politik för studenter
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:856 av Lorena Delgado Varas m.fl. (V)
summary: This motion from the Left Party proposes a series of measures aimed at improving student conditions in Sweden, emphasizing the importance of education as a human right and advocating for free higher education. Key suggestions include the introduction of a qualification test for university admissions, a review of financial support structures for students, enhanced accessibility in education, and the elimination of fees for non-European students. Additionally, the motion calls for a stronger focus on student welfare, the rights of students with disabilities, and equitable access to resources such as course literature and student health services.

title: Motverka hatbrott på nätet
summary: This motion proposes that the Swedish parliament supports the idea that social media platforms should be able to link anonymous accounts to individual users. It emphasizes the need to improve conditions for democratic discourse in Sweden by strategically and effectively combating online hate crimes, particularly in light of concerns over the spread of disinformation and hateful content on social media that threatens democratic values and contributes to a deteriorating social climate.

title: Mäns våld mot kvinnor
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:854 av Alexandra Völker och Azadeh Rojhan (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes several measures aimed at combatting men's violence against women in Sweden, including the need to map municipal efforts to support women and children fleeing domestic violence, ensuring priority housing for victims, clarifying municipal responsibilities, and enhancing legal protections for victims, including the possibility of stripping a violent co-parent of visitation rights. The motion calls for reforms to eliminate waiting periods in divorce proceedings and to improve legal representation for victims in court, highlighting the challenges faced by women living with protected identities who suffer from continuous threats and violence.

title: Våldsutövande föräldrars vårdnadsrätt
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:853 av Azadeh Rojhan och Alexandra Völker (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes a review of legislation concerning the custody rights of violent parents, emphasizing the need for courts to conduct documented risk assessments in custody disputes. Reports indicate serious shortcomings in how domestic violence is handled in such cases, with many violent parents retaining custody despite evidence of abuse. The motion argues for prioritizing the safety and well-being of children and ensuring that violent parents are not granted custody, aligning with the principles of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child.

title: Energi
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:852 av Jennie Nilsson och Arber Gashi (båda S)
summary: The motion emphasizes the urgent need for cross-party discussions on energy issues in Sweden, highlighting the necessity for equal conditions for electricity consumers and businesses across different electric areas. It calls for an expansion of electricity production to meet increasing demand, especially focusing on reducing greenhouse gas emissions by replacing fossil fuels with electricity in industry and transport. The proposal also addresses the problem of bottlenecks in the power grid, which lead to higher electricity prices, particularly in southern Sweden, urging the government to create long-term, stable conditions for all energy sources to ensure competitive electricity prices and maintain the viability of energy-intensive industries.

title: Stärkt vård för familjehemsplacerade barn och bättre förutsättningar för familjehem
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:851 av Anna-Belle Strömberg och Peter Hedberg (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes measures to increase the number of foster care placements and ensure that foster parents can take leave from work to support children placed in their care. It highlights the current challenges faced in recruiting adequate foster homes and emphasizes the importance of providing stable and secure environments for children who cannot live with their biological parents. The authors argue that fostering is preferable to institutional care, and that more resources should be allocated to make fostering more accessible and effective.

title: Tydligare beaktande av klimat och miljö i statens offentliga utredningar
summary: The proposal aims to enhance the consideration of climate and environmental impacts within state public investigations in Sweden. It suggests that all investigations should include a consequence analysis regarding their effects on climate and environment, as current regulations do not mandate this, despite political decisions often impacting these areas. The motion emphasizes the urgency of the climate crisis and the necessity for comprehensive environmental assessments in governmental processes.

title: Om stärkt trygghet för företagare
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:849 av Mathias Tegnér och Jennie Nilsson (båda S)
summary: The motion aims to enhance security for entrepreneurs in Sweden by advocating for a more equitable safety net that does not differentiate between employees and self-employed individuals. Key proposals include establishing sickness benefit income for sole proprietors, improving unemployment insurance, and promoting entrepreneurship within the educational system. The authors argue that effective safety nets contribute to economic growth and support the increasing number of small and medium enterprises, which are vital to the Swedish economy.

title: Utvecklad rastverksamhet i skolan
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish parliament supports the consideration of a national initiative for organized recess activities in schools. It highlights the importance of structured breaks for students' health and academic performance, noting the need for national support to share best practices and research on the subject. The motion suggests the appointment of a national coordinator for recess, allocation of resources for municipalities to develop these activities, and collaboration with community organizations to provide free qualitative programs during recess and after school.

title: Utredning om rättegångskostnader för immateriella skydd
summary: The motion proposes an examination of litigation costs in patent disputes to ensure they remain manageable, particularly for small businesses and startups. It also calls for a review of the processing times in these cases to accelerate the legal processes. The background highlights challenges faced by smaller actors due to high litigation costs, which deter them from pursuing legal action, and suggests looking to countries like Germany and England for models that could help make the process more accessible.

title: Klimatmål inom trafikpolitiken
summary: The motion advocates for a shift in Sweden's infrastructure planning from being predominantly forecast-driven to goal-oriented, particularly in relation to achieving climate targets in the transport sector. It emphasizes the need for the planning process to focus on specific climate objectives rather than relying on growth projections that could reinforce the dominance of road transport, thus potentially undermining the overall transport policy objectives.

title: Hyresvärdars bedömning av sökandes betalningsförmåga
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:845 av Joakim Sandell och Rose-Marie Carlsson (båda S)
summary: The proposal suggests a study to require all incomes to be considered when assessing a rental applicant's ability to pay, regardless of whether the landlord is public or private. The motion highlights the current discrimination against low-income groups in the housing market, where rental providers often dismiss certain income types, such as unemployment benefits and housing allowances, which can lead to unreasonable barriers for potential tenants. The authors argue that this practice exacerbates the housing crisis and unfairly favors wealthier individuals over those in need.

title: Se över möjligheten att öka tryggheten och säkerheten på nätet
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:844 av Joakim Sandell och Rose-Marie Carlsson (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament examines ways to enhance online safety and security, particularly for children and youth, against the backdrop of increasing influence from social media and controversial influencers. It acknowledges the significant role of major tech companies in shaping the online environment and highlights the need for these companies to take responsibility in limiting the reach of misleading information through algorithms. The motion draws inspiration from similar discussions in the UK, emphasizing the urgent need for protective measures in Sweden.

title: Förverkligande av Öresundsmetron
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:843 av Joakim Sandell och Rose-Marie Carlsson (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes that Sweden and Denmark jointly investigate the feasibility of establishing the Öresund Metro, a subway connection between central Malmö and central Copenhagen. The proposal emphasizes the growing demand for improved public transport in the Öresund region due to an increasing population and economic growth. The motion highlights the past success of the Öresund Bridge in enhancing regional connectivity and calls for timely planning and investment to address future transportation needs, particularly as the Fehmarn Belt Tunnel opens in 2029.

title: Stärkt barn- och ungdomspsykiatri
summary: The proposal calls for the Swedish government to implement a national plan aimed at reducing waiting times for child and adolescent psychiatric services (BUP) and improving preventative and treatment efforts for mental health issues among youth. It highlights a significant increase in the number of children and adolescents seeking help and emphasizes the urgency of addressing staffing shortages and resource allocation to ensure BUP can fulfill its responsibilities. Strategies suggested include enhancing digital care options, improving collaboration with schools and social services, and investing in research to develop better treatment methods.

title: Om stärkta åtgärder för en förbättrad arbetsmiljö
summary: The proposal calls for a review of the enforcement of the Work Environment Act to ensure a safer and healthier work environment in Sweden. The motion emphasizes the need for employers to conduct regular risk assessments and take necessary actions to safeguard employees. It highlights the importance of improving education on workplace safety for both employers and employees, while also addressing psychosocial risks such as stress and bullying. The suggestion aims to hold both public and private employers accountable for systematic occupational safety efforts and to update the legislation to tackle existing challenges.

title: Inrättande av fler träffpunkter för ungdomar
summary: This motion proposes the establishment of more meeting points for youth across Sweden, emphasizing the importance of social environments for their development and future opportunities. It argues that access to such spaces can reduce the risks of exclusion, mental health issues, and crime among young people. The motion advocates for the creation of inclusive and accessible platforms, designed with input from the youth, which would offer a variety of activities including sports, music, and cultural engagement. The proposal calls for collaboration between municipalities, civil society, and local associations to ensure these meeting points cater to all youth, including those with disabilities.

title: Politisk styrning av forskningsmedel
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish parliament endorses the necessity to protect the independence of research by ensuring that research funding is allocated on scientific and independent grounds. It highlights concerns over political interference in research funding, particularly in development research, and stresses the importance of maintaining academic freedom to allow for credible and unbiased contributions to global issues. The motion calls for stricter regulations to ensure that research funding is free from political influence and that it is distributed based on scientific criteria rather than governmental priorities.

title: Vargjakt
summary: The parliamentary motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament supports reducing the wolf population to a range of 170-270 individuals, as set by previous decisions, through hunting or other measures. The motion highlights concerns raised by rural residents and farmers regarding wolf attacks on livestock and pets, asserting that the current population of approximately 375 exceeds the desired conservation goal.

title: Säkra svenska medborgares rätt till integration och frihet från förtryck av andra stater
summary: The suggestion proposes that the Swedish Parliament investigate how to better protect Swedish citizens, particularly those with roots in authoritarian regimes, from external pressures and control by their home countries. It highlights instances of coercion faced by the diaspora, particularly from Eritrea, where citizens are subjected to demands such as a 'diaspora tax' and threats towards family members. The proposal emphasizes the need for strengthened legislation and resources to ensure these individuals can fully integrate into Swedish society free from dictatorship influences.

title: En trygg och rättvis arbetsmarknad
summary: The motion proposes an overhaul of labor market measures to ensure a safer and fairer work environment, advocating for more permanent full-time positions. It emphasizes equal job opportunities regardless of gender, religion, sexual orientation, or background, advocating for job security as fundamental for a good life. The motion highlights the rising prevalence of insecure employment terms since 1990, particularly affecting women-dominated sectors, and critiques legislative changes that have made jobs more precarious, arguing this has not reduced unemployment as intended and has weakened union membership.

title: Sverige som innovativt och etablerat investeringsland
summary: The suggestion calls for the Swedish government to strengthen the country as an established nation for innovation and investment by actively engaging with the business sector to develop concrete policies that enhance competitiveness and job growth. It emphasizes the importance of a supportive regulatory environment, investment in digitalization and automation, and collaboration between industry and academia to drive innovation and attract both domestic and international investors.

title: Plattformsekonomin
summary: The motion proposes a review of the working conditions for workers in the gig economy, highlighting the shift from traditional full-time employment to a more flexible but insecure job market. The motion emphasizes the need to clarify the employment status of gig workers, who often operate in a three-party relationship with platforms, customers, and potentially other entities. It points out the lack of legal clarity regarding whether these workers should be considered employees or independent contractors, noting the adverse effects this ambiguity has on wage development and job security.

title: Krav på kollektivavtal vid offentlig upphandling
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish parliament should require collective agreements (kollektivavtal) for all suppliers involved in public procurement. Currently, legislation restricts contracting authorities from imposing such requirements, which is argued to undermine labor standards and contribute to poor working conditions. The motion asserts that allowing collective agreement mandates would ensure fair labor practices and a better working environment while enhancing compliance with EU norms, challenging previous rulings that viewed such requirements as detrimental to competitiveness for small businesses.

title: Rättvisa elpriser i södra Sverige
summary: The motion proposes to increase investments in fossil-free energy sources in southern Sweden and to investigate alternative pricing models for electricity, addressing the unfair price variations caused by historical decisions on electricity zone divisions. The author argues that current measures have led to increased prices for consumers and businesses in the region, necessitating urgent reforms to ensure a more equitable and sustainable electricity market in Sweden.

title: Israels ansvar för mordet på Bernadotte
summary: This parliamentary motion calls for the Swedish Riksdag to demand that the state of Israel issue a public apology to the family of Folke Bernadotte and to Sweden for his murder in 1948 by members of the Stern gang. Additionally, it seeks compensation for the Bernadotte family, asserting that a state should take responsibility for its actions, especially towards a mediator who played a significant role in international efforts during a time of conflict.

title: Förbud mot att använda skrubber på fartyg
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:830 av Magnus Manhammar och Eva Lindh (båda S)
summary: This motion proposes a ban on the use of scrubbers on ships in Sweden due to environmental concerns. It argues that while tougher regulations on air emissions from ships aim to reduce pollutants, the scrubber system, which cleans exhaust gases using water, releases harmful substances into the sea. The motion emphasizes the importance of protecting marine ecosystems and suggests that existing air quality improvements must not compromise the purity of surrounding waters.

title: Ökat handelsutbyte med Albanien
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament support increased trade between Sweden and Albania, highlighting the historical positive relations between the two countries. The motion emphasizes the economic potential of Albania, which has undergone significant reforms since the fall of communism, making it a more viable partner for international trade. By expanding trade relations, the proposal suggests benefits such as access to a growing market for Swedish goods and services and the introduction of Swedish technology and innovation to Albania. The motion calls for the Swedish government to facilitate trade and investment opportunities through bilateral agreements and increased cooperation between businesses in both nations.

title: Kosovos medlemskap i Europarådet
summary: The proposal advocates for Sweden to support Kosovo's membership in the Council of Europe, emphasizing the importance of promoting human rights and democratic values. Kosovo has made significant strides towards being recognized as a sovereign state and has sought to join European institutions. The motion calls for Sweden's government to actively work towards having Kosovo's membership issue placed on the agenda of the Council's ministerial committee, highlighting the need for Kosovo's inclusion as a means to bolster its human rights framework.

title: Differentierad skolpeng
summary: The proposal advocates for the investigation into a differentiated school funding system that acknowledges the differing conditions between public and independent schools. It argues that public schools face higher expenses due to responsibilities such as providing education across all geographical areas and accommodating students from independent schools in the event of closures. The suggestion aims to address financial imbalances by adjusting funding so that it reflects these challenges, ultimately promoting greater equity in the Swedish education system.

title: Dispositiv lagstiftning om lönegolv för arbetskraftsinvandring
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:826 av Helén Pettersson och Åsa Karlsson (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes making legislation regarding minimum salary levels for labor migration to Sweden negotiable, allowing for adjustments based on collective agreements between employers and unions. The authors argue that current regulations, which mandate a fixed minimum salary, lead to exploitation and competition distortion in the labor market. They assert that a negotiable approach will enable better alignment with actual labor demands and protect migrants from unscrupulous employers.

title: Statligt ansvar vid industrietableringar
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish government investigate the possibility of sharing the financial risks associated with large industrial establishments with municipalities, especially in light of significant investments for the green industry's establishment in Sweden. It highlights the substantial economic burdens on municipalities, such as Skellefteå, that are responsible for infrastructure and welfare development while alone carrying the financial risks. The intention is to create a supportive national framework that facilitates sustainable growth in these regions.

title: Tillgång till internet inom riksnormen för försörjningsstöd
summary: The motion proposes an investigation into the possibility of including internet access within the reasonable living standard of the national norm for social assistance in Sweden. It emphasizes the necessity of internet connectivity for education and access to information, highlighting the challenges faced by students from families on social welfare, particularly during the pandemic when remote learning became essential. The motion argues that having internet should be recognized as a right in the digital age and urges the government to consider this integration in the national support framework.

title: Kriminaliserande av ekonomiskt våld
summary: This proposal suggests that the Swedish Parliament investigate the criminalization of economic violence, which is identified as a form of control often exerted by men over women in abusive relationships. The motion highlights that while physical violence receives more attention, economic violence—which entails manipulating or restricting a partner's financial resources—also significantly harms individuals. The lack of legal provisions addressing economic violence is emphasized, and the proposal calls for the establishment of clear definitions and legal frameworks to detect, combat, and prosecute this form of abuse.

title: Rättspsykiatrin
summary: The motion proposes a comprehensive review and strengthening of Sweden's forensic psychiatry services. It emphasizes the increasing need for care for severely mentally ill individuals who have committed serious crimes and highlights issues such as overcrowding, long waiting times, and inadequate oversight within the system. The motion calls for improvements to the entire psychiatric chain, including legal reforms regarding discharge procedures and the need for a national intake system for forensic psychiatry. It also addresses the challenges posed by current legislation that limits the reporting of crimes within forensic settings and stresses the importance of state responsibility in addressing these issues.

title: Gemensam nordisk läkemedelsupphandling och beredskap
summary: The motion proposes increased cooperation among the Nordic countries for the procurement of vaccines and medications, and calls for a review of the possibility of shared procurement of certain medicines and medical technology. It also advocates for establishing joint stockpiles of medical supplies in response to lessons learned from the pandemic, highlighting the importance of collective action to enhance crisis preparedness and address existing gaps in the region's healthcare coordination.

title: Pornografi
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:820 av Eva Lindh och Åsa Eriksson (båda S)
summary: The motion advocates for a comprehensive investigation into the harmful effects of pornography on various aspects of society. It emphasizes that pornography often involves the exploitation of women, including those trafficked and in prostitution, and contributes to the normalization of violence and degrading attitudes towards women, particularly among children and youth. The legislators argue that existing laws against sex buying could be utilized to combat the production of pornography, but insufficient resources are currently allocated for enforcement. The motion calls for a concerted effort to address the societal implications of pornography, enhance gender equality, and protect human rights.

title: Stärkning av Tullverket
summary: The proposal aims to strengthen the Swedish Customs (Tullverket) by enhancing cooperation with neighboring countries and providing the necessary resources and training to utilize newly acquired powers effectively. It emphasizes the importance of strengthening customs to combat cross-border crime, particularly the influx of weapons and drugs into Sweden. The motion supports the expansion of Tullverket initiated by the Social Democrats and highlights the need for collaboration with other countries to address issues such as the illegal export of stolen goods.

title: Gemensamt ansvarstagande och finansiering för att klimatsäkra samhället
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish parliament should review and modernize the Water Services Act to enhance state support for municipal water companies. This is essential to enable necessary investments for climate adaptation of water networks in light of increasing extreme weather events such as heavy rainfall and flooding, which are projected to become more common due to climate change. The motion emphasizes the need for a comprehensive approach to climate adaptation, improved crisis preparedness, and a more equitable distribution of financing responsibilities among the state, municipalities, and private property owners.

title: MSB:s förstärkningsresurser vid översvämningar
summary: Linnéa Wickman proposes to enhance the preventive work of the Swedish Civil Contingencies Agency (MSB) regarding flood risk through improved availability of reinforcement resources such as flood barriers and high-capacity pumps. The motion argues that, unlike wildfire readiness, flood preparedness lacks a proactive approach tied to weather forecasts. By adopting strategies from wildfire management improvements following recent climate-related emergencies, the proposal seeks to increase the robustness and resilience of local emergency services and better adapt to climate change and increased instances of extreme rainfall.

title: Polisutbildning vid Högskolan i Gävle
summary: The proposal advocates for the establishment of a police education program at Högskolan i Gävle to increase the number of police officers in Sweden, especially in response to issues like gang crime and domestic violence. The motion stresses the need for local police presence and the importance of expanding police training opportunities across multiple locations to ensure a consistent increase in police workforce, aiming for 50,000 police employees by 2032.

title: Orosanmälan vid sexköp
summary: The motion proposes the investigation of the possibility of introducing a mandatory reporting requirement for cases of individuals purchasing sexual services, specifically when the buyer has minor children. It argues that purchasing sex represents a form of exploitation and is linked to patterns of violence against women and children. It emphasizes the need for relevant authorities to be alerted to potential risks for children and to provide necessary support to ensure their safety.

title: Rökfria miljöer genom en starkare tobakslag
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:814 av Anna Wallentheim och Linnéa Wickman (båda S)
summary: The motion proposes the implementation of a stricter tobacco law that explicitly bans smoking on balconies, patios, and other shared outdoor areas in multi-family residences. It highlights the public health risks associated with passive smoking, particularly for vulnerable groups like children and the elderly. The proposal suggests empowering landlords and housing associations to enforce smoking bans indoors and in common areas, with clear guidelines and penalties for non-compliance, aiming to create smoke-free living environments and promote health equity.

title: Digital e-legitimation
summary: The proposal suggests that the Swedish parliament supports the introduction of a state-managed digital e-identification system that ensures access for individuals without bank-ID or other digital identification. It emphasizes the need for a reliable e-identification infrastructure for crucial services such as healthcare, medications, and government contacts, particularly during outages. Furthermore, it highlights that Sweden is one of the few EU countries lacking a state e-identification and stresses the importance of equitable access to essential services amidst growing digital exclusion.

title: Förbud mot snara som fångstmetod för rödräv
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:812 av Rebecka Le Moine m.fl. (MP)
summary: The proposal aims to ban inhumane hunting methods, including the use of snares for capturing red foxes and live capture traps for other wildlife, while allowing exceptions for wild boar under specific conditions. It emphasizes the need for ethical treatment of animals during hunting practices and calls for regulations that prevent unnecessary suffering.

title: Ett globalt nedrustningsavtal för utvinning av fossila bränslen
summary: The proposal calls for Sweden to advocate for the establishment of a global disarmament agreement aimed at halting the extraction of fossil fuels. It emphasizes the urgent need for international cooperation to phase out fossil fuel production and accelerate the transition to renewable energy, highlighting the climate crisis and its risks. The motion references various global organizations and initiatives supporting such an agreement and argues that Sweden's historical commitment to disarmament and climate issues positions it well to lead this effort.

title: Sveriges ansvar för personal som bistått svenska styrkor utomlands
summary: The proposal urges the Swedish government to ensure protection for personnel who assisted Swedish forces in Afghanistan and their families, highlighting the severe risks they currently face from the Taliban. It calls for immediate action to safeguard these individuals and to establish a systematic approach for their protection in future similar situations, emphasizing Sweden's responsibility in providing safety for those who supported its military operations abroad.

title: Forskning om patientsäkerhet
summary: The motion proposes the initiation of a national research program focused on patient safety in healthcare, addressing the significant issue of avoidable healthcare injuries that result in personal suffering and societal costs. It emphasizes the need to enhance Swedish research in this area, establish a long-term program with specific funding, and integrate it into the government's research policy proposal. The plan also aims to improve knowledge and competencies related to patient safety and to evaluate existing measures' effectiveness more thoroughly.

title: Förbud mot sms-lån
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:808 av Janine Alm Ericson m.fl. (MP)
summary: The motion proposes a review and potential ban on SMS loans, citing an increase in individuals facing indebtedness and legal action due to the high interest rates and short repayment terms associated with these loans. It argues that SMS loans disproportionately affect economically vulnerable groups who cannot obtain loans from traditional banks, often resulting in excessive debt. The proposal aims to encourage more sustainable financial practices by eliminating access to SMS loans.

title: Rätten till aktiv dödshjälp
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:807 av Janine Alm Ericson m.fl. (MP)
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament investigate the introduction of euthanasia in Sweden, emphasizing the need for individuals to have the right to choose the circumstances of their own death, especially in cases of prolonged suffering without hope of recovery. It highlights the importance of self-determination at the end of life while acknowledging the ethical complexities and the need to carefully assess associated risks before legalization.

title: Barns rättigheter vid våld i nära relationer
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:806 av Janine Alm Ericson m.fl. (MP)
summary: The motion proposes to enhance children's rights in cases of domestic violence by ensuring that children are given their own legal representatives in custody disputes, preventing children with protected identities from being forced to contact a parent against their will, and stipulating that a parent convicted of repeated or severe violence against the child or their relatives should lose custody. The proposal highlights the inadequacy of current legal practices in protecting children's voices and experiences in custody matters, especially in the context of domestic violence.

title: Införande av fyra dagars arbetsvecka i Sverige
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:805 av Leila Ali Elmi m.fl. (MP)
summary: The Green Party proposes the introduction of a four-day workweek in Sweden as a means to create a more sustainable work life, reduce sick leave, and enhance work-life balance. The motion suggests amending the Working Hours Act to facilitate this change, alongside establishing a government investigation involving labor market participants and relevant authorities. The proposal advocates for a more flexible work environment that allows employees to recover and spend time with their families, reflecting a long-standing commitment of the party towards reduced working hours.

title: Grundlagsskydda transpersoners rättigheter
summary: The proposal advocates for amendments to Sweden's constitution to incorporate gender identity and gender expression into the foundational rights protected by the government. It emphasizes the need for legal recognition of these aspects to prevent discrimination against transgender individuals, reflecting concerns over their rights being increasingly challenged in public discourse. The motion promotes a robust protection framework within the constitution that acknowledges and safeguards the rights of a vulnerable minority group.

title: Reglera rätten till hjälpmedel i en särskild lag
summary: The motion proposes the establishment of a separate legislation for assistive devices to ensure equitable access and distribution across Sweden, particularly for individuals with disabilities. The current system is criticized for being inefficient and inconsistent, often tied to local healthcare provisions which hinder individuals' ability to work or study. This new law aims to rectify these issues, promote human rights, and support the integration of people with disabilities into the workforce, as emphasized by existing conventions and previous investigations.

title: Ett uppdrag till MUCF om unga med funktionsnedsättning
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament mandates the Agency for Youth and Civil Society Issues (MUCF) to investigate the situation of young people with disabilities in Sweden. This follows a previous investigation focused on LGBTQI youth, highlighting the need for current knowledge about various groups’ conditions to address significant challenges they face, particularly for those belonging to minority groups. The motion underlines the notion that young people with disabilities may face even greater difficulties and calls for a similar intersectoral analysis as previously conducted for LGBTQI youth.

title: Åtgärder för förbättrad ledsagning – hedrande av riksdagens tillkännagivande
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish government promptly provides information regarding the initiation of an investigation for a new law to regulate support for escorting visually impaired individuals. The proposal is in response to criticism from the UN committee regarding Sweden's failure to guarantee equal participation for visually impaired persons in society, highlighting instances where necessary escorting support has been denied, impacting their ability to engage in essential activities. The motion emphasizes the urgent need for legislative action to address the declining accessibility of escorting services under current laws.

title: Krav på att upphandlade resetjänster ska kunna boka tågresor
summary: The proposal calls for the Swedish Parliament to require all public agencies with contracted travel services to ensure those agencies can book international train journeys, including sleeper trains, as part of their travel offerings. The motion emphasizes the environmental benefits of train travel over flying, citing significant reductions in carbon emissions. It also argues that enhancing the competency of travel agencies in booking train services will facilitate a shift towards more sustainable travel choices among public employees and the general public.

title: Det ska löna sig att arbeta
summary: The proposal advocates for a review of the welfare system, suggesting that individuals receiving social assistance should be allowed to retain a greater portion of their benefits when they start working. The intention is to make it financially viable for low-income families, particularly those with children, to engage in work, thereby reducing economic inequality and fostering greater social participation among disadvantaged groups.

title: Identifiering och utfasning av miljöskadliga subventioner
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:798 av Rebecka Le Moine m.fl. (MP)
summary: This motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament instruct the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency (Naturvårdsverket) to identify environmentally harmful subsidies and develop an action plan for their phase-out as swiftly as possible. It highlights the global and national issues associated with such subsidies, including significant financial allocations to fossil fuels that undermine efforts to address climate change and biodiversity loss.

title: Ekonomiska garantier för avfallsplatser
motion_id: Motion 2024/25:797 av Martina Johansson och Malin Björk (båda C)
summary: The proposal suggests that the Swedish Parliament should investigate the establishment of financial guarantees for waste management companies to ensure funding for the cleanup of waste sites in the event a company ceases operations. It also calls for municipalities to receive compensation from companies that violate waste regulations, allowing them to use the funds for site remediation. This is aimed at preventing financial burdens on taxpayers when dealing with cleanup efforts.

title: Avdragsrätt för medlemskap i a‑kassa och fackförening
summary: The proposal suggests that the membership fees for unemployment insurance funds (a-kassa) and trade unions should be made tax deductible or eligible for tax reduction. It emphasizes the importance of strong trade unions for productivity and welfare in Sweden and argues that mutual deductibility for both employee and employer organizations would promote balance in the labor market. The proposal also references historical changes to tax rules regarding union fees and aims to reinstate deductions to strengthen the labor movement in Sweden.

title: Religiösa skrifter
summary: The proposal suggests that burning religious texts, such as the Quran, Bible, and Torah, should be classified as hate speech against specific groups. It emphasizes the importance of balancing freedom of expression with the potential harm caused by acts that are driven by hate and disrespect, particularly against religious communities. The motion calls for the government to review existing laws on hate speech and public disturbance to determine if they are adequately structured to protect religious sentiments and ensure public order.

title: Ökad finansiering av bibliotek
summary: The proposal aims to increase government funding for public libraries in Sweden to enhance their ability to provide a broader selection of literature, including course literature necessary for university students. It argues that current financial constraints limit libraries' offerings, which negatively affects students who rely on them for access to expensive course materials, while also supporting the libraries' primary mission of serving community residents.

title: Byggande av fler hyresrätter för unga
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament supports the construction of more rental apartments for young people and calls for the reinstatement of government investment support for housing. It highlights the pressing issue of housing shortages in Sweden, particularly affecting youth who struggle to move out of their parents' homes, which in turn impacts their ability to form families and pursue education. The proposal argues that increasing the number of affordable rental units is essential for fostering independence among young people and stimulating economic activity through construction.

title: Utrikes föddas upplevelse av sin arbetsmiljö
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament supports the implementation of procedures for handling discriminatory treatment in the workplace, particularly for foreign-born individuals who report poorer work environments compared to native-born workers. The motion highlights a focus report from the Swedish Work Environment Authority, which indicates a higher prevalence of negative experiences such as harassment and discrimination among foreign-born employees, and calls for collective efforts from employers, authorities, and society to ensure equitable and inclusive working conditions.

title: Säkra nattågen till Jämtland
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish parliament supports maintaining night train services to Jämtland from both Stockholm and Göteborg, expressing concern about the discontinuation of the Göteborg-Duved route after April 2025. The motion argues that it is unreasonable for the state to subsidize night trains on one route but not the other, calling for the government to ensure that night train traffic is preserved in future infrastructure plans.

title: Punktskatt på desinfektionsmedel
summary: The motion advocates for a clarification of the tax legislation concerning excise duty on disinfectants, highlighting the critical role these products play in maintaining hygiene, particularly in healthcare settings. The author argues that the current tax, originally designed for agricultural products, improperly affects disinfectants and could lead to higher costs for municipalities, thus undermining public health efforts. The motion calls for governmental action to ensure the availability and use of disinfectants, emphasizing that Sweden currently lacks a comparable tax regime seen in neighboring Nordic countries.

title: Ändra civilstånd
summary: The motion proposes to allow individuals to change their civil status in Sweden, addressing the current limitations that prevent people from self-applying to alter their civil status after events such as divorce or becoming widowed. The proponent suggests that the existing civil status categories are outdated, recommending the addition of other categories like 'single' and 'cohabitant' to better reflect modern relationships.

title: Bredbandsuppkoppling för alla i Sverige
summary: The motion calls for the Swedish Parliament to support the proposal ensuring that all households in Sweden have access to a fixed broadband connection. It highlights the importance of digitalization and points out that a significant number of households, particularly in the Kronoberg region, still lack such connectivity, which could hinder both individual residents and the broader digital transition in Sweden.

title: Bevarande av uppkörnings- och teoriprovsmöjligheter för motorcykel i flera orter, inklusive Älmhults kommun
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish government take measures to ensure that the Transport Agency maintains the availability of both theoretical and practical motorcycle tests across the country, particularly in smaller municipalities like Älmhult. It calls for the government to counteract the ongoing centralization of testing locations, which has made it more difficult for residents to access these services. The motion highlights the negative impact of reduced testing opportunities on local driving schools and the increased burden on individuals, particularly young people, who must travel significant distances to take their tests.

title: Lokalbefolkningens bostadssituation på populära turistmål
summary: Monica Haider's suggestion urges the Swedish parliament to consider regulating apartment rentals to tourists, citing the housing difficulties faced by locals in tourist areas like Gotland. The motion highlights how landlords often prioritize short-term rentals to tourists over long-term leases for residents, leading to increased living costs and potential displacement of local populations. Drawing on examples from cities like Barcelona, the proposal advocates for comprehensive regulations to ensure that the housing needs of residents are prioritized over tourist accommodation, aiming to prevent a crisis of affordability in popular destinations.

title: Tillåt körning av lätt motorcykel med B-körkort
summary: The suggestion proposes that Sweden allow individuals with a B driver's license to operate light motorcycles, aiming to alleviate traffic congestion, parking issues, and environmental impact in urban areas. The motion emphasizes that many EU countries already permit this and argues that adopting such a measure would promote the use of more space-efficient and environmentally friendly transportation, ultimately encouraging a shift away from car dependency in Sweden.

title: Gynnande av användningen av elnätsstolpar i trä
summary: The proposal advocates for promoting the use of wooden utility poles in Sweden's energy infrastructure to enhance sustainability and resilience against future challenges, particularly in the context of climate change and extreme weather. It highlights the environmental benefits of wooden poles as a renewable resource that can lead to reduced carbon emissions, lower maintenance costs, and improved adaptability during adverse weather conditions. The motion calls for increased research and development on this topic, as well as financial incentives and guidelines to support the adoption of wooden poles in the energy sector.

title: Jämställda lånevillkor
summary: The proposal urges the Swedish Parliament to mandate the Financial Supervisory Authority to collect and report gender-disaggregated statistics on loan conditions from all credit institutions. Additionally, it calls for an analysis of the conditions faced by women and men in the mortgage market and suggests updating the regulations to require banks to report average interest rates broken down by gender. The motion highlights that women, on average, earn about 20% less than men, particularly affecting those living alone, thereby creating disparities in access to mortgages and potentially higher interest rates for women.

title: Växtbaserad mat – en framtidsbransch för Sverige
summary: The motion proposes that the Swedish Parliament considers creating an action plan for plant-based food, aiming to enhance the country's agricultural sector and address increasing consumer demand for plant-based diets. It suggests initiatives to stimulate both private and public markets, raise consumer awareness of Swedish values in plant-based choices, and collaborate with various stakeholders. Key proposals for the action plan include objectives for protein crop cultivation, increased funding for plant breeding, investments in storage and processing technology, and targeted research in the plant-based food chain.

title: Samarbetet mellan myndigheter
summary: The proposal emphasizes the need for a coordinating function between various government agencies to enhance collaboration regarding individual cases. It highlights issues caused by confidentiality barriers that prevent agencies such as Försäkringskassan and Arbetsförmedlingen from effectively cooperating. This leads to individuals being stuck between the agencies without receiving proper support, resulting in mental health issues and financial difficulties. The motion calls for innovative solutions to ensure that more individuals can receive personalized assistance aimed at facilitating their return to work or education.

title: Sveriges roll i arbetet för ett fritt Västsahara
summary: The proposal advocates for Sweden to enhance its role in supporting the independence of Western Sahara, recognized as Africa's last colony. It emphasizes the ongoing humanitarian crisis faced by Sahrawi refugees in Algerian camps, exacerbated by dwindling international aid and human rights abuses under Moroccan occupation. The motion calls for Sweden to formally recognize Western Sahara as an independent state and to ensure a representation for its exiled government in Sweden, asserting this would pave the way for more countries to follow suit and promote freedom for the Sahrawi people.

title: Elevhälsa med särskilt fokus på neuropsykiatriska funktionsvariationer och psykisk ohälsa
summary: The proposal emphasizes the need to enhance student health services in schools with a specific focus on neuropsychiatric disorders and mental health issues, due to the alarming rise of psychological problems among youth. It highlights the inadequacies of current student health services and suggests that schools play a crucial role in identifying and addressing these mental health concerns.

title: Nationell likvärdighet i vården
summary: This motion calls for measures to enhance national equity in healthcare, emphasizing the need for equal treatment and care access across Sweden. It highlights disparities in care quality, accessibility, and costs based on geographic location, advocating for common patient fee levels, national standards for health data management, and uniform treatment timelines to ensure fair healthcare provision for all citizens.

title: Goda och lika möjligheter till tekniska hjälpmedel vid diabetesvård
summary: The motion presented emphasizes the need for equal access to technological aids for diabetes care, highlighting that many individuals in Sweden with diabetes face challenges in obtaining necessary monitoring devices. It calls on regional authorities to invest in these technologies to enhance health outcomes and reduce long-term healthcare costs associated with diabetes complications, underlining the importance of comprehensive care across the country.

title: Ändring av 3:12-reglerna
